cards.src_text: Then Joseph being raised from sleep did as the angel of Yahuah (Lord) had bidden him, and took unto him his wife:
cards.tgt_text: Sanctify unto me all the firstborn, whatsoever openeth the womb among the children of Yashar'el (Israel), both of man and of beast: it is mine.
cards.old_note: *Sanctify unto me all the firstborn* — the Torah's firstborn-consecration sets the framework for Yahusha (Jesus) as firstborn.
cards.note: Exodus 13:2 — *Sanctify unto me all the firstborn, whatsoever openeth the womb among the children of Yashar'el (Israel), both of man and of beast: it is mine.* *Then Joseph being raised from sleep did as the angel of Yahuah (Lord) had bidden him, and took unto him his wife:* (Matthew 1:24) A firstborn belongs to Yahuah (the LORD), *it is mine*. Joseph takes his wife and the child is her firstborn, so the child comes under that word of the Torah. Yahusha (Jesus) was set apart as a firstborn son of Yashar'el (Israel), in the Torah's own way.
cards.prose: A firstborn belongs to Yahuah (the LORD), *it is mine*. Joseph takes his wife and the child is her firstborn, so the child comes under that word of the Torah. Yahusha (Jesus) was set apart as a firstborn son of Yashar'el (Israel), in the Torah's own way.
cards.member_note: Exodus 13:2 — *Sanctify unto me all the firstborn, whatsoever openeth the womb among the children of Yashar'el (Israel), both of man and of beast: it is mine.* The Torah sets every firstborn apart to Yahuah (the LORD), which is the standing of the child Mary bears.

cards.src_text: Then Joseph being raised from sleep did as the angel of Yahuah (Lord) had bidden him, and took unto him his wife:
cards.tgt_text: Who is the image of the invisible Elohim (God), the firstborn of every creature:
cards.old_note: *The firstborn of every creature ... the firstborn from the dead* — the apostolic firstborn-Christology grounded in the Torah firstborn pattern.
cards.note: Colossians 1:15 — *Who is the image of the invisible Elohim (God), the firstborn of every creature:* *Then Joseph being raised from sleep did as the angel of Yahuah (Lord) had bidden him, and took unto him his wife:* (Matthew 1:24) Paul calls the firstborn *the image of the invisible Elohim (God)*. The Father is the one no man sees, and the firstborn Mary bore is his image, the one who can be seen. The word Matthew uses for the child reaches this far.
cards.prose: Paul calls the firstborn *the image of the invisible Elohim (God)*. The Father is the one no man sees, and the firstborn Mary bore is his image, the one who can be seen. The word Matthew uses for the child reaches this far.
cards.member_note: Colossians 1:15 — *Who is the image of the invisible Elohim (God), the firstborn of every creature:* Paul calls the firstborn the image of the invisible Father, so the child Mary bore is the Father's image.

cards.src_text: Then Joseph being raised from sleep did as the angel of Yahuah (Lord) had bidden him, and took unto him his wife:
cards.tgt_text: And he is the head of the body, the church: who is the beginning, the firstborn from the dead; that in all things he might have the preeminence.
cards.old_note: *The firstborn of every creature ... the firstborn from the dead* — the apostolic firstborn-Christology grounded in the Torah firstborn pattern.
cards.note: Colossians 1:18 — *And he is the head of the body, the church: who is the beginning, the firstborn from the dead; that in all things he might have the preeminence.* *Then Joseph being raised from sleep did as the angel of Yahuah (Lord) had bidden him, and took unto him his wife:* (Matthew 1:24) Paul calls him *the beginning, the firstborn from the dead*. The same word that names the child born to Mary names the one who rose first from the grave. The firstborn of Joseph's household is the first to rise.
cards.prose: Paul calls him *the beginning, the firstborn from the dead*. The same word that names the child born to Mary names the one who rose first from the grave. The firstborn of Joseph's household is the first to rise.
cards.member_note: Colossians 1:18 — *And he is the head of the body, the church: who is the beginning, the firstborn from the dead; that in all things he might have the preeminence.* Paul calls the firstborn the head of the body and the firstborn from the dead, the one with the highest place.

cards.src_text: Now when Yahusha (Jesus) was born in Bethlehem of Judaea in the days of Herod the king, behold, there came wise men from the east to Jerusalem,
cards.tgt_text: Then the king made Daniel a great man, and gave him many great gifts, and made him ruler over the whole province of Babylon, and chief of the governors over all the wise men of Babylon.
cards.old_note: Daniel's promotion to chief of the wise men of Babylon — the institutional source of the Magi's prophetic knowledge.
cards.note: Daniel 2:48 — *Then the king made Daniel a great man, and gave him many great gifts, and made him ruler over the whole province of Babylon, and chief of the governors over all the wise men of Babylon.* *Now when Yahusha (Jesus) was born in Bethlehem of Judaea in the days of Herod the king, behold, there came wise men from the east to Jerusalem,* (Matthew 2:1) The wise men of Babylon were the ones Daniel was set over, so when wise men come out of the east asking after a newborn King there is a road behind them. The chief of their schools had been a man of Yahuah (the LORD), and it is reasonable to think what he knew of the coming King did not simply vanish from that country.
cards.prose: The wise men of Babylon were the ones Daniel was set over, so when wise men come out of the east asking after a newborn King there is a road behind them. The chief of their schools had been a man of Yahuah (the LORD), and it is reasonable to think what he knew of the coming King did not simply vanish from that country.
cards.member_note: Daniel 2:48 — *made him ruler over the whole province of Babylon, and chief of the governors over all the wise men of Babylon.* Daniel is made chief over the wise men of Babylon, which gives the eastern wise men of Matthew a prophet's name behind their watching.

cards.src_text: Saying, Where is he that is born King of the Yahudim (Jews)? for we have seen his star in the east, and are come to worship him.
cards.tgt_text: Seventy weeks are determined upon thy people and upon thy holy city, to finish the transgression, and to make an end of sins, and to make reconciliation for iniquity, and to bring in everlasting righteousness, and to seal up the vision and prophecy, and to anoint the most Holy.
cards.old_note: The seventy-weeks prophecy giving the timing of *Messiah the Prince* — the Daniel-tradition Magi would have known the timing window from.
cards.note: Daniel 9:24 — *Seventy weeks are determined upon thy people and upon thy holy city, to finish the transgression, and to make an end of sins, and to make reconciliation for iniquity, and to bring in everlasting righteousness, and to seal up the vision and prophecy, and to anoint the most Holy.* *Saying, Where is he that is born King of the Yahudim (Jews)? for we have seen his star in the east, and are come to worship him.* (Matthew 2:2) Daniel was given the span of time before the most Holy is anointed, and the wise men asking where the King is born came from the country where that prophet had served. They arrive in the season his seventy weeks pointed to, looking for the one he was told would come.
cards.prose: Daniel was given the span of time before the most Holy is anointed, and the wise men asking where the King is born came from the country where that prophet had served. They arrive in the season his seventy weeks pointed to, looking for the one he was told would come.
cards.member_note: Daniel 9:24 — *to bring in everlasting righteousness, and to seal up the vision and prophecy, and to anoint the most Holy.* Daniel's seventy weeks fix the time of the anointed one, the timing the eastern wise men could have drawn from the prophet who served in their land.

cards.src_text: When they had heard the king, they departed; and, lo, the star, which they saw in the east, went before them, till it came and stood over where the young child was.
cards.tgt_text: And Yahuah (LORD) went before them by day in a pillar of a cloud, to lead them the way; and by night in a pillar of fire, to give them light; to go by day and night:
cards.old_note: The pillar of cloud and fire that led Yashar'el (Israel) in the wilderness — the Tanakh-pattern for the shekinah-leading-by-visible-sign that the Matthew-2 star manifests.
cards.note: Exodus 13:21 — *And Yahuah (LORD) went before them by day in a pillar of a cloud, to lead them the way; and by night in a pillar of fire, to give them light; to go by day and night:* *When they had heard the king, they departed; and, lo, the star, which they saw in the east, went before them, till it came and stood over where the young child was.* (Matthew 2:9) The star going before them until it stood over the place is the same kind of leading as the pillar of cloud and of fire: Yahuah (the LORD) going before travelers by a sign they could see. The sign does not leave them until they are standing where he meant them to be.
cards.prose: The star going before them until it stood over the place is the same kind of leading as the pillar of cloud and of fire: Yahuah (the LORD) going before travelers by a sign they could see. The sign does not leave them until they are standing where he meant them to be.
cards.member_note: Exodus 13:21 — *went before them by day in a pillar of a cloud, to lead them the way; and by night in a pillar of fire, to give them light.* Yahuah (the LORD) went before his people by day and by night in a visible sign, as the star goes before the wise men to the child.

cards.src_text: When Herod the king had heard these things, he was troubled, and all Jerusalem with him.
cards.tgt_text: For thy violence against thy brother Jacob shame shall cover thee, and thou shalt be cut off for ever.
cards.old_note: *For thy violence against thy brother Ya'aqov (Jacob) shame shall cover thee* — Obadiah's oracle against Edom; Herod's planned violence against the Davidic infant continues the pattern.
cards.note: Obadiah 1:10 — *For thy violence against thy brother Jacob shame shall cover thee, and thou shalt be cut off for ever.* *When Herod the king had heard these things, he was troubled, and all Jerusalem with him.* (Matthew 2:3) Herod is troubled at the news of a newborn King of the Yahudim (Jews), and the oracle against Edom shows what lies under his trouble. Herod was an Edomite by descent, and the sin named here is Edom's violence against his brother Jacob, which Herod now turns on the child of David's line.
cards.prose: Herod is troubled at the news of a newborn King of the Yahudim (Jews), and the oracle against Edom shows what lies under his trouble. Herod was an Edomite by descent, and the sin named here is Edom's violence against his brother Jacob, which Herod now turns on the child of David's line.
cards.member_note: Obadiah 1:10 — *For thy violence against thy brother Jacob shame shall cover thee, and thou shalt be cut off for ever.* Obadiah names Edom's violence against his brother Jacob, the old wrong that Herod's fear of the newborn King repeats.

cards.src_text: When Herod the king had heard these things, he was troubled, and all Jerusalem with him.
cards.tgt_text: And Moses sent messengers from Kadesh unto the king of Edom, Thus saith thy brother Yashar'el (Israel), Thou knowest all the travail that hath befallen us:
cards.old_note: Edom refusing passage to Yashar'el (Israel) at the wilderness border — the earliest beat of the Edom-against-Yashar'el pattern.
cards.note: Numbers 20:14 — *And Moses sent messengers from Kadesh unto the king of Edom, Thus saith thy brother Yashar'el (Israel), Thou knowest all the travail that hath befallen us:* *When Herod the king had heard these things, he was troubled, and all Jerusalem with him.* (Matthew 2:3) Moses sent word to the king of Edom and called him brother, and Edom would not let Yashar'el (Israel) through. That is the first time the brother's house stands in the way, and Herod's trouble at a King born in Bethlehem is the same standing in the way many centuries later.
cards.prose: Moses sent word to the king of Edom and called him brother, and Edom would not let Yashar'el (Israel) through. That is the first time the brother's house stands in the way, and Herod's trouble at a King born in Bethlehem is the same standing in the way many centuries later.
cards.member_note: Numbers 20:14 — *And Moses sent messengers from Kadesh unto the king of Edom, Thus saith thy brother Yashar'el (Israel), Thou knowest all the travail that hath befallen us:* Moses calls Edom's king his brother and asks for passage, the first place in the story where Edom stands against Yashar'el (Israel).

cards.src_text: When Herod the king had heard these things, he was troubled, and all Jerusalem with him.
cards.tgt_text: I have loved you, saith Yahuah (LORD). Yet ye say, Wherein hast thou loved us? Was not Esau Jacob’s brother? saith Yahuah (LORD): yet I loved Jacob,
cards.old_note: *Yet I loved Ya'aqov (Jacob), and I hated Esau* — the divine-side reading of the long pattern.
cards.note: Malachi 1:2 — *I have loved you, saith Yahuah (LORD). Yet ye say, Wherein hast thou loved us? Was not Esau Jacob’s brother? saith Yahuah (LORD): yet I loved Jacob,* *When Herod the king had heard these things, he was troubled, and all Jerusalem with him.* (Matthew 2:3) Against that long grudge stands Yahuah's (the LORD's) own word, *yet I loved Jacob*. Herod may shake the whole city, but the choice was made before he was born, and it is the blessed line he is reaching for when he asks where the King is to be found.
cards.prose: Against that long grudge stands Yahuah's (the LORD's) own word, *yet I loved Jacob*. Herod may shake the whole city, but the choice was made before he was born, and it is the blessed line he is reaching for when he asks where the King is to be found.
cards.member_note: Malachi 1:2 — *I have loved you, saith Yahuah (LORD). Yet ye say, Wherein hast thou loved us? Was not Esau Jacob’s brother? saith Yahuah (LORD): yet I loved Jacob,* Yahuah (the LORD) says he loved Jacob and answers the question of Esau and Jacob, the choice that stands under Herod's hatred.

cards.src_text: When Herod the king had heard these things, he was troubled, and all Jerusalem with him.
cards.tgt_text: Moreover the word of Yahuah (LORD) came unto me, saying,
cards.old_note: The prophecy against Mount Seir for the perpetual hatred.
cards.note: Ezekiel 35:1 — *Moreover the word of Yahuah (LORD) came unto me, saying,* *When Herod the king had heard these things, he was troubled, and all Jerusalem with him.* (Matthew 2:3) This is how the word of Yahuah (the LORD) against Mount Seir, Esau's mountain, opens, and a few verses on it gives the charge: *Because thou hast had a perpetual hatred, and hast shed the blood of the children of Yashar'el (Israel) by the force of the sword in the time of their calamity, in the time that their iniquity had an end:* (Ezekiel 35:5) Herod troubled in Jerusalem sits under that same word.
cards.prose: This is how the word of Yahuah (the LORD) against Mount Seir, Esau's mountain, opens, and a few verses on it gives the charge: *Because thou hast had a perpetual hatred, and hast shed the blood of the children of Yashar'el (Israel) by the force of the sword in the time of their calamity, in the time that their iniquity had an end:* (Ezekiel 35:5) Herod troubled in Jerusalem sits under that same word.
cards.member_note: Ezekiel 35:1 — *Moreover the word of Yahuah (LORD) came unto me, saying,* The word of Yahuah (the LORD) comes to Ezekiel against Mount Seir, and it answers Edom's lasting hatred of the children of Yashar'el (Israel).

cards.src_text: When Herod the king had heard these things, he was troubled, and all Jerusalem with him.
cards.tgt_text: Remember, O Yahuah (LORD), the children of Edom in the day of Jerusalem; who said, Rase it, rase it, even to the foundation thereof.
cards.old_note: *Remember, O Yahuah (LORD), the children of Edom in the day of Yerushalayim (Jerusalem)* — the cry against Edom for joining the Babylonian destruction.
cards.note: Psalm 137:7 — *Remember, O Yahuah (LORD), the children of Edom in the day of Jerusalem; who said, Rase it, rase it, even to the foundation thereof.* *When Herod the king had heard these things, he was troubled, and all Jerusalem with him.* (Matthew 2:3) The psalmist asks Yahuah (the LORD) to remember what the sons of Edom said on the day Jerusalem fell, *Rase it, rase it*. When Herod is troubled and all Jerusalem with him, the city has heard that cry before and has already asked to have it remembered.
cards.prose: The psalmist asks Yahuah (the LORD) to remember what the sons of Edom said on the day Jerusalem fell, *Rase it, rase it*. When Herod is troubled and all Jerusalem with him, the city has heard that cry before and has already asked to have it remembered.
cards.member_note: Psalm 137:7 — *Remember, O Yahuah (LORD), the children of Edom in the day of Jerusalem; who said, Rase it, rase it, even to the foundation thereof.* The psalmist asks Yahuah (the LORD) to remember Edom's cry to level Jerusalem, the same hostility now sitting on the throne at Herod's court.

cards.src_text: Then Herod, when he saw that he was mocked of the wise men, was exceeding wroth, and sent forth, and slew all the children that were in Bethlehem, and in all the coasts thereof, from two years old and under, according to the time which he had diligently enquired of the wise men.
cards.tgt_text: And Esau hated Jacob because of the blessing wherewith his father blessed him: and Esau said in his heart, The days of mourning for my father are at hand; then will I slay my brother Jacob.
cards.old_note: *And Esau hated Ya'aqov (Jacob) ... the days of mourning for my father are at hand; then will I slay my brother Ya'aqov (Jacob)* — Esau's first attempted-murder of Ya'aqov (Jacob); Herod's slaughter of the infants is the latest beat of the same hatred.
cards.note: Genesis 27:41 — *And Esau hated Jacob because of the blessing wherewith his father blessed him: and Esau said in his heart, The days of mourning for my father are at hand; then will I slay my brother Jacob.* *Then Herod, when he saw that he was mocked of the wise men, was exceeding wroth, and sent forth, and slew all the children that were in Bethlehem, and in all the coasts thereof, from two years old and under, according to the time which he had diligently enquired of the wise men.* (Matthew 2:16) Esau's hatred of Jacob went as far as murder in his heart because of the blessing. Herod's order to kill the children of Bethlehem is that same hatred, reaching for the line the blessing ran through.
cards.prose: Esau's hatred of Jacob went as far as murder in his heart because of the blessing. Herod's order to kill the children of Bethlehem is that same hatred, reaching for the line the blessing ran through.
cards.member_note: Genesis 27:41 — *And Esau hated Jacob because of the blessing wherewith his father blessed him.* Esau hates Jacob for the blessing and resolves to kill him, the first murder planned out of that hatred, which Herod acts on at Bethlehem.

cards.src_text: And when they were departed, behold, the angel of Yahuah (Lord) appears to Joseph in a dream, saying, Arise, and take the young child and his mother, and flee into Egypt, and be you there until I bring you word: for Herod will seek the young child to destroy him.
cards.tgt_text: Now there arose up a new king over Egypt, which knew not Joseph.
cards.old_note: Pharaoh's order to kill the Hebrew male infants — the Tanakh-pattern of slaughter-of-the-infants-to-prevent-the-deliverer that Matthew 2:16 recapitulates with Herod-Yahusha (Jesus) in the lead roles.
cards.note: Exodus 1:8 — *Now there arose up a new king over Egypt, which knew not Joseph.* *And when they were departed, behold, the angel of Yahuah (Lord) appears to Joseph in a dream, saying, Arise, and take the young child and his mother, and flee into Egypt, and be you there until I bring you word: for Herod will seek the young child to destroy him.* (Matthew 2:13) A new king who knew not Joseph is where the sons of Yashar'el (Israel) are first pressed down in Egypt, and Joseph in Matthew is told to carry the child down into that same land because another king means to destroy him. The land that was once a place of oppression becomes a hiding place from Herod.
cards.prose: A new king who knew not Joseph is where the sons of Yashar'el (Israel) are first pressed down in Egypt, and Joseph in Matthew is told to carry the child down into that same land because another king means to destroy him. The land that was once a place of oppression becomes a hiding place from Herod.
cards.member_note: Exodus 1:8 — *Now there arose up a new king over Egypt, which knew not Joseph.* A new king arises over Egypt who knew not Joseph, the beginning of the hard rule that falls on the sons of Yashar'el (Israel).

cards.src_text: And when they were departed, behold, the angel of Yahuah (Lord) appears to Joseph in a dream, saying, Arise, and take the young child and his mother, and flee into Egypt, and be you there until I bring you word: for Herod will seek the young child to destroy him.
cards.tgt_text: And there went a man of the house of Levi, and took to wife a daughter of Levi.
cards.old_note: The preservation of the infant Mosheh (Moses) on the Nile while the other Hebrew infants were killed — the Tanakh-pattern of the deliverer preserved through the infant-slaughter.
cards.note: Exodus 2:1 — *And there went a man of the house of Levi, and took to wife a daughter of Levi.* *And when they were departed, behold, the angel of Yahuah (Lord) appears to Joseph in a dream, saying, Arise, and take the young child and his mother, and flee into Egypt, and be you there until I bring you word: for Herod will seek the young child to destroy him.* (Matthew 2:13) Moses' parents were both of Levi, and the child they hid and then set on the water lived while the king's order took the others. Joseph taking the young child away by night is the same rescue of the one the king wants dead.
cards.prose: Moses' parents were both of Levi, and the child they hid and then set on the water lived while the king's order took the others. Joseph taking the young child away by night is the same rescue of the one the king wants dead.
cards.member_note: Exodus 2:1 — *And there went a man of the house of Levi, and took to wife a daughter of Levi.* A man of the house of Levi takes a daughter of Levi to wife, the house into which Moses is born and hidden from the king.

cards.src_text: When he arose, he took the young child and his mother by night, and departed into Egypt:
cards.tgt_text: And Yashar'el (Israel) took his journey with all that he had, and came to Beer-sheba, and offered sacrifices unto the Elohim (God) of his father Isaac.
cards.old_note: The patriarch Yoseph (Joseph) bringing Ya'aqov (Jacob) and his sons down to Egypt — the Tanakh-Yoseph initiating the Egypt-sojourn that the Matthew-Yoseph (Joseph) re-walks with the Messianic-Yashar'el (Israel) in his arms.
cards.note: Genesis 46:1 — *And Yashar'el (Israel) took his journey with all that he had, and came to Beer-sheba, and offered sacrifices unto the Elohim (God) of his father Isaac.* *When he arose, he took the young child and his mother by night, and departed into Egypt:* (Matthew 2:14) Jacob went down into Egypt with all that he had, and Elohim (God) spoke to him in the visions of the night about the going. Joseph takes the young child down by night on a warning from the angel of Yahuah (the Lord), so the road down follows the road the fathers walked.
cards.prose: Jacob went down into Egypt with all that he had, and Elohim (God) spoke to him in the visions of the night about the going. Joseph takes the young child down by night on a warning from the angel of Yahuah (the Lord), so the road down follows the road the fathers walked.
cards.member_note: Genesis 46:1 — *And Yashar'el (Israel) took his journey with all that he had, and came to Beer-sheba, and offered sacrifices unto the Elohim (God) of his father Isaac.* Jacob journeys toward Egypt with all he had and offers at Beer-sheba, the fathers' road down that Joseph and the child walk again.

cards.src_text: When he arose, he took the young child and his mother by night, and departed into Egypt:
cards.tgt_text: Now the sojourning of the children of Yashar'el (Israel), who dwelt in Egypt, was four hundred and thirty years.
cards.old_note: The four-hundred-year Egypt-sojourn ended by the Exodus — the duration the Matthew-Egypt-sojourn telescopes into a few years for the Messiah, but recapitulates as the same pattern.
cards.note: Exodus 12:40 — *Now the sojourning of the children of Yashar'el (Israel), who dwelt in Egypt, was four hundred and thirty years.* *When he arose, he took the young child and his mother by night, and departed into Egypt:* (Matthew 2:14) The sons of Yashar'el (Israel) were in Egypt four hundred and thirty years before they were brought out, and the child's stay there is short beside it. It ends the same way, with a word from Yahuah (the LORD) to come out, so Matthew sets him on the road his people took, down and then up.
cards.prose: The sons of Yashar'el (Israel) were in Egypt four hundred and thirty years before they were brought out, and the child's stay there is short beside it. It ends the same way, with a word from Yahuah (the LORD) to come out, so Matthew sets him on the road his people took, down and then up.
cards.member_note: Exodus 12:40 — *Now the sojourning of the children of Yashar'el (Israel), who dwelt in Egypt, was four hundred and thirty years.* The sojourn of the children of Yashar'el (Israel) in Egypt is counted at four hundred and thirty years before the going out.

cards.src_text: But when Herod was dead, behold, an angel of Yahuah (Lord) appears in a dream to Joseph in Egypt,
cards.tgt_text: And Yahuah (LORD) said unto Moses in Midian, Go, return into Egypt: for all the men are dead which sought thy life.
cards.old_note: *Go, return into Egypt: for all the men are dead which sought thy life* — the angelic-instruction to Mosheh (Moses) parallel to Matt 2:20's angelic-instruction to Yoseph (Joseph): *they are dead which sought the young child's life.* The verbal parallel is deliberate.
cards.note: Exodus 4:19 — *And Yahuah (LORD) said unto Moses in Midian, Go, return into Egypt: for all the men are dead which sought thy life.* *But when Herod was dead, behold, an angel of Yahuah (Lord) appears in a dream to Joseph in Egypt,* (Matthew 2:19) Moses is told in Midian to go back to Egypt because the men who sought his life are dead, and Joseph is told almost the same thing in his dream. The words are close enough that the reader hears Moses behind the child, with both men called back because the ones who hunted them are gone.
cards.prose: Moses is told in Midian to go back to Egypt because the men who sought his life are dead, and Joseph is told almost the same thing in his dream. The words are close enough that the reader hears Moses behind the child, with both men called back because the ones who hunted them are gone.
cards.member_note: Exodus 4:19 — *And Yahuah (LORD) said unto Moses in Midian, Go, return into Egypt: for all the men are dead which sought thy life.* Yahuah (the LORD) tells Moses in Midian to return to Egypt because the men who sought his life are dead, the words the angel echoes to Joseph.

cards.src_text: In Rama was there a voice heard, lamentation, and weeping, and great mourning, Rachel weeping for her children, and would not be comforted, because they are not.
cards.tgt_text: Behold, the days come, saith Yahuah (LORD), that I will make a new covenant with the house of Yashar'el (Israel), and with the house of Yahudah (Judah):
cards.old_note: The new-covenant promise — the deeper answer to the weeping, enacted in the blood of the Messianic child Matthew is protecting in the same chapter.
cards.note: Jeremiah 31:31 — *Behold, the days come, saith Yahuah (LORD), that I will make a new covenant with the house of Yashar'el (Israel), and with the house of Yahudah (Judah):* *In Rama was there a voice heard, lamentation, and weeping, and great mourning, Rachel weeping for her children, and would not be comforted, because they are not.* (Matthew 2:18) The weeping at Bethlehem is quoted out of the chapter where Yahuah (the LORD) promises *a new covenant* with the house of Yashar'el (Israel) and the house of Yahudah (Judah). Both houses are named, and the comfort for Rachel's lost children is that they are being brought back into his covenant, with his instruction written inward and not set aside.
cards.prose: The weeping at Bethlehem is quoted out of the chapter where Yahuah (the LORD) promises *a new covenant* with the house of Yashar'el (Israel) and the house of Yahudah (Judah). Both houses are named, and the comfort for Rachel's lost children is that they are being brought back into his covenant, with his instruction written inward and not set aside.
cards.member_note: Jeremiah 31:31 — *Behold, the days come, saith Yahuah (LORD), that I will make a new covenant with the house of Yashar'el (Israel), and with the house of Yahudah (Judah):* Yahuah (the LORD) promises a new covenant with both the house of Yashar'el (Israel) and the house of Yahudah (Judah), the comfort the same chapter gives Rachel.

cards.src_text: In Rama was there a voice heard, lamentation, and weeping, and great mourning, Rachel weeping for her children, and would not be comforted, because they are not.
cards.tgt_text: And they journeyed from Beth-el; and there was but a little way to come to Ephrath: and Rachel travailed, and she had hard labour.
cards.old_note: Rachel's death in childbirth near Beth-lehem (Ephrata) — the biographical anchor of the Rachel-weeps-for-children motif and the connection to the Beth-lehem geography of Matthew 2.
cards.note: Genesis 35:16 — *And they journeyed from Beth-el; and there was but a little way to come to Ephrath: and Rachel travailed, and she had hard labour.* *In Rama was there a voice heard, lamentation, and weeping, and great mourning, Rachel weeping for her children, and would not be comforted, because they are not.* (Matthew 2:18) Rachel died in childbirth a little way from Ephrath, which is Bethlehem, so the mother whose weeping Matthew hears lies buried beside the very road where the children were killed. The cry is not a figure of speech here; it rises from where she was laid.
cards.prose: Rachel died in childbirth a little way from Ephrath, which is Bethlehem, so the mother whose weeping Matthew hears lies buried beside the very road where the children were killed. The cry is not a figure of speech here; it rises from where she was laid.
cards.member_note: Genesis 35:16 — *And they journeyed from Beth-el; and there was but a little way to come to Ephrath: and Rachel travailed, and she had hard labour.* Rachel travails and dies a little way from Ephrath, which is Bethlehem, fixing her weeping at the place Herod's soldiers came.

cards.src_text: In Rama was there a voice heard, lamentation, and weeping, and great mourning, Rachel weeping for her children, and would not be comforted, because they are not.
cards.tgt_text: They shall come with weeping, and with supplications will I lead them: I will cause them to walk by the rivers of waters in a straight way, wherein they shall not stumble: for I am a father to Yashar'el (Israel), and Ephraim is my firstborn.
cards.old_note: *I will cause them to walk by the rivers of waters in a straight way, wherein they shall not stumble: for I am a father to Yashar'el (Israel), and Ephraim is my firstborn* — the gathering of the northern house, which Rachel's children (Yoseph (Joseph) and Binyamin (Benjamin)) are most associated with.
cards.note: Jeremiah 31:9 — *They shall come with weeping, and with supplications will I lead them: I will cause them to walk by the rivers of waters in a straight way, wherein they shall not stumble: for I am a father to Yashar'el (Israel), and Ephraim is my firstborn.* *In Rama was there a voice heard, lamentation, and weeping, and great mourning, Rachel weeping for her children, and would not be comforted, because they are not.* (Matthew 2:18) *They shall come with weeping* says the same chapter that gives Rachel her tears, and the children who were taken are led home by a straight way where they do not stumble. Rachel's sons are the northern house, and the weeping is over their being carried away, not over their being finished, since *Ephraim is my firstborn*.
cards.prose: *They shall come with weeping* says the same chapter that gives Rachel her tears, and the children who were taken are led home by a straight way where they do not stumble. Rachel's sons are the northern house, and the weeping is over their being carried away, not over their being finished, since *Ephraim is my firstborn*.
cards.member_note: Jeremiah 31:9 — *They shall come with weeping, and with supplications will I lead them: I will cause them to walk by the rivers of waters in a straight way.* Yahuah (the LORD) leads the weeping remnant of Yashar'el (Israel) home by a straight way, with Ephraim, Rachel's grandson, called his firstborn.

cards.src_text: In Rama was there a voice heard, lamentation, and weeping, and great mourning, Rachel weeping for her children, and would not be comforted, because they are not.
cards.tgt_text: For this is my blood of the new testament, which is shed for many for the remission of sins.
cards.old_note: *For this is my blood of the new testament, which is shed for many for the remission of sins* — Yahusha (Jesus) enacting the Jer 31:31-34 new covenant in his blood at the Last Supper, twenty-six chapters after the Matt 2 infant-protection.
cards.note: Matthew 26:28 — *For this is my blood of the new testament, which is shed for many for the remission of sins.* *In Rama was there a voice heard, lamentation, and weeping, and great mourning, Rachel weeping for her children, and would not be comforted, because they are not.* (Matthew 2:18) At the table Yahusha (Jesus) speaks of his blood *of the new testament*, and that is the covenant Rachel's chapter promised to both houses. The weeping at Bethlehem opens toward it, because *the remission of sins* is the door by which the children carried away are brought home.
cards.prose: At the table Yahusha (Jesus) speaks of his blood *of the new testament*, and that is the covenant Rachel's chapter promised to both houses. The weeping at Bethlehem opens toward it, because *the remission of sins* is the door by which the children carried away are brought home.
cards.member_note: Matthew 26:28 — *For this is my blood of the new testament, which is shed for many for the remission of sins.* Yahusha (Jesus) names his blood as the blood of the new covenant, the covenant of the chapter from which Rachel's weeping is quoted.

cards.src_text: And he came and dwelt in a city called Nazareth: that it might be fulfilled which was spoken by the prophets, He shall be called a Nazarene.
cards.tgt_text: Behold, the days come, saith Yahuah (LORD), that I will raise unto David a righteous Branch, and a King shall reign and prosper, and shall execute judgment and justice in the earth.
cards.old_note: *I will raise unto David a righteous Branch* (here *tsemach,* a different Branch-word but the same Messianic theme) — the broader prophetic Branch-tradition Matthew references with *the prophets* (plural).
cards.note: Jeremiah 23:5 — *Behold, the days come, saith Yahuah (LORD), that I will raise unto David a righteous Branch, and a King shall reign and prosper, and shall execute judgment and justice in the earth.* *And he came and dwelt in a city called Nazareth: that it might be fulfilled which was spoken by the prophets, He shall be called a Nazarene.* (Matthew 2:23) Matthew says the prophets, plural, called him a Nazarene, and Jeremiah is one of them, naming *a righteous Branch* raised up to David who will reign. The verses just before promise the flock gathered out of every country, so the Branch is the King of a scattered people being brought home.
cards.prose: Matthew says the prophets, plural, called him a Nazarene, and Jeremiah is one of them, naming *a righteous Branch* raised up to David who will reign. The verses just before promise the flock gathered out of every country, so the Branch is the King of a scattered people being brought home.
cards.member_note: Jeremiah 23:5 — *Behold, the days come, saith Yahuah (LORD), that I will raise unto David a righteous Branch, and a King shall reign and prosper, and shall execute judgment and justice in the earth.* Jeremiah promises a righteous Branch raised to David, who reigns over the flock gathered back from the countries where it was driven.

cards.src_text: And he came and dwelt in a city called Nazareth: that it might be fulfilled which was spoken by the prophets, He shall be called a Nazarene.
cards.tgt_text: In those days, and at that time, will I cause the Branch of righteousness to grow up unto David; and he shall execute judgment and righteousness in the land.
cards.old_note: *In those days, and at that time, will I cause the Branch of righteousness to grow up unto David* — the parallel Branch-prophecy.
cards.note: Jeremiah 33:15 — *In those days, and at that time, will I cause the Branch of righteousness to grow up unto David; and he shall execute judgment and righteousness in the land.* *And he came and dwelt in a city called Nazareth: that it might be fulfilled which was spoken by the prophets, He shall be called a Nazarene.* (Matthew 2:23) Again the prophet says the Branch will be made to grow up to David and will *execute judgment and righteousness in the land*. A King who grows up in a small town of Galilee fits that way of speaking, because the prophets describe him as growing up and not as arriving in a palace.
cards.prose: Again the prophet says the Branch will be made to grow up to David and will *execute judgment and righteousness in the land*. A King who grows up in a small town of Galilee fits that way of speaking, because the prophets describe him as growing up and not as arriving in a palace.
cards.member_note: Jeremiah 33:15 — *In those days, and at that time, will I cause the Branch of righteousness to grow up unto David; and he shall execute judgment and righteousness in the land.* Jeremiah says Yahuah (the LORD) will cause the Branch of righteousness to grow up to David and execute judgment in the land.

cards.src_text: And he came and dwelt in a city called Nazareth: that it might be fulfilled which was spoken by the prophets, He shall be called a Nazarene.
cards.tgt_text: Hear now, O Joshua the high priest, thou, and thy fellows that sit before thee: for they are men wondered at: for, behold, I will bring forth my servant the BRANCH.
cards.old_note: *Behold, I will bring forth my servant the BRANCH* — Zechariah's Branch-naming.
cards.note: Zechariah 3:8 — *Hear now, O Joshua the high priest, thou, and thy fellows that sit before thee: for they are men wondered at: for, behold, I will bring forth my servant the BRANCH.* *And he came and dwelt in a city called Nazareth: that it might be fulfilled which was spoken by the prophets, He shall be called a Nazarene.* (Matthew 2:23) *My servant the BRANCH* is promised to Joshua the high priest and those who sit before him as a sign of something to be wondered at. Matthew's *a Nazarene* carries the same name, worn by a servant who comes quietly from a small place.
cards.prose: *My servant the BRANCH* is promised to Joshua the high priest and those who sit before him as a sign of something to be wondered at. Matthew's *a Nazarene* carries the same name, worn by a servant who comes quietly from a small place.
cards.member_note: Zechariah 3:8 — *Hear now, O Joshua the high priest, thou, and thy fellows that sit before thee: for they are men wondered at: for, behold, I will bring forth my servant the BRANCH.* Yahuah (the LORD) promises to bring forth his servant the Branch, spoken to Joshua the high priest as a sign of what is coming.

cards.src_text: And he came and dwelt in a city called Nazareth: that it might be fulfilled which was spoken by the prophets, He shall be called a Nazarene.
cards.tgt_text: And speak unto him, saying, Thus speaketh Yahuah Tseva'ot (LORD of hosts), saying, Behold the man whose name is The BRANCH; and he shall grow up out of his place, and he shall build the temple of Yahuah (LORD):
cards.old_note: *Behold the man whose name is The BRANCH; and he shall grow up out of his place* — Zechariah's Branch-naming with the grow-up-out-of-his-place language that resonates with Matthew's coming-out-of-Natsareth.
cards.note: Zechariah 6:12 — *And speak unto him, saying, Thus speaketh Yahuah Tseva'ot (LORD of hosts), saying, Behold the man whose name is The BRANCH; and he shall grow up out of his place, and he shall build the temple of Yahuah (LORD):* *And he came and dwelt in a city called Nazareth: that it might be fulfilled which was spoken by the prophets, He shall be called a Nazarene.* (Matthew 2:23) Here the Branch is named outright, and it is said of him that *he shall grow up out of his place*. That is what Matthew shows in a child who is carried out of danger and settled in a Galilean town, to grow up where he was put, as the prophet said.
cards.prose: Here the Branch is named outright, and it is said of him that *he shall grow up out of his place*. That is what Matthew shows in a child who is carried out of danger and settled in a Galilean town, to grow up where he was put, as the prophet said.
cards.member_note: Zechariah 6:12 — *Behold the man whose name is The BRANCH; and he shall grow up out of his place.* Zechariah names the man whose name is the Branch, who grows up out of his place and builds the house of Yahuah (the LORD).

cards.src_text: And they said unto him, In Bethlehem of Judaea: for thus it is written by the prophet,
cards.tgt_text: But thou, Beth-lehem Ephratah, though thou be little among the thousands of Yahudah (Judah), yet out of thee shall he come forth unto me that is to be ruler in Yashar'el (Israel); whose goings forth have been from of old, from everlasting.
cards.old_note: The Old Testament prophetic source — Beth-lehem Ephratah as the birth-locale of the *ruler in Yashar'el (Israel); whose goings forth have been from of old, from everlasting.*
cards.note: Micah 5:2 — *But thou, Beth-lehem Ephratah, though thou be little among the thousands of Yahudah (Judah), yet out of thee shall he come forth unto me that is to be ruler in Yashar'el (Israel); whose goings forth have been from of old, from everlasting.* *And they said unto him, In Bethlehem of Judaea: for thus it is written by the prophet,* (Matthew 2:5) The scribes answer Herod with *In Bethlehem of Judaea*, and this is the page of the prophet they read it from. The ruler comes out of a town too small to count among the thousands of Yahudah (Judah), yet his *goings forth have been from of old, from everlasting*, so the child born there is older than the town.

cards.src_text: And they said unto him, In Bethlehem of Judaea: for thus it is written by the prophet,
cards.tgt_text: And Yahuah (LORD) said unto Samuel, How long wilt thou mourn for Saul, seeing I have rejected him from reigning over Yashar'el (Israel)? fill thine horn with oil, and go, I will send thee to Jesse the Beth-lehemite: for I have provided me a king among his sons.
cards.old_note: Beth-lehem as David's birthplace and the locale of his anointing — the seed-line geography.
cards.note: 1 Samuel 16:1 — *And Yahuah (LORD) said unto Samuel, How long wilt thou mourn for Saul, seeing I have rejected him from reigning over Yashar'el (Israel)? fill thine horn with oil, and go, I will send thee to Jesse the Beth-lehemite: for I have provided me a king among his sons.* *And they said unto him, In Bethlehem of Judaea: for thus it is written by the prophet,* (Matthew 2:5) Bethlehem was a town where Yahuah (the LORD) had already gone looking for a king, in the house of Jesse, after he rejected Saul. When the scribes name Bethlehem they are naming David's town, so the King Herod fears is born where the first of that line was found.

cards.src_text: And they said unto him, In Bethlehem of Judaea: for thus it is written by the prophet,
cards.tgt_text: And Samuel did that which Yahuah (LORD) spake, and came to Beth-lehem. And the elders of the town trembled at his coming, and said, Comest thou peaceably?
cards.old_note: Beth-lehem as David's birthplace and the locale of his anointing — the seed-line geography.
cards.note: 1 Samuel 16:4 — *And Samuel did that which Yahuah (LORD) spake, and came to Beth-lehem. And the elders of the town trembled at his coming, and said, Comest thou peaceably?* *And they said unto him, In Bethlehem of Judaea: for thus it is written by the prophet,* (Matthew 2:5) When Samuel came to Bethlehem the elders of the town trembled and asked if he came peaceably, because the business of a king was dangerous in that place. Now a king is born there again and it is the ruling house in Jerusalem that is troubled.

And the elders of the town trembled at his coming, and said, Comest thou peaceably?* Samuel comes to Bethlehem at Yahuah's (the LORD's) word and the elders tremble at his coming, the place where David was found.

cards.src_text: And they said unto him, In Bethlehem of Judaea: for thus it is written by the prophet,
cards.tgt_text: And all the people that were in the gate, and the elders, said, We are witnesses. Yahuah (LORD) make the woman that is come into thine house like Rachel and like Leah, which two did build the house of Yashar'el (Israel): and do thou worthily in Ephratah, and be famous in Beth-lehem:
cards.old_note: *Do thou worthily in Ephratah, and be famous in Beth-lehem* — the blessing on Boaz at the kinsman-redeemer marriage that produces the line of David.
cards.note: Ruth 4:11 — *And all the people that were in the gate, and the elders, said, We are witnesses. Yahuah (LORD) make the woman that is come into thine house like Rachel and like Leah, which two did build the house of Yashar'el (Israel): and do thou worthily in Ephratah, and be famous in Beth-lehem:* *And they said unto him, In Bethlehem of Judaea: for thus it is written by the prophet,* (Matthew 2:5) The elders at the gate asked Yahuah (the LORD) to make Ruth like Rachel and like Leah, who built the house of Yashar'el (Israel), and to let Boaz *be famous in Beth-lehem*. Ruth came into the line as the wife of a son of Yahudah (Judah), and from that marriage came David, and from David the King the scribes are asked about.
cards.prose: The elders at the gate asked Yahuah (the LORD) to make Ruth like Rachel and like Leah, who built the house of Yashar'el (Israel), and to let Boaz *be famous in Beth-lehem*. Ruth came into the line as the wife of a son of Yahudah (Judah), and from that marriage came David, and from David the King the scribes are asked about.

cards.src_text: And when they were come into the house, they saw the young child with Mary his mother, and fell down, and worshipped him: and when they had opened their treasures, they presented unto him gifts; gold, and frankincense, and myrrh.
cards.tgt_text: And Yahuah (LORD) said unto Moses, Take unto thee sweet spices, stacte, and onycha, and galbanum; these sweet spices with pure frankincense: of each shall there be a like weight:
cards.old_note: The frankincense in the holy incense of the tabernacle — the priestly significance of the second gift.
cards.note: Exodus 30:34 — *And Yahuah (LORD) said unto Moses, Take unto thee sweet spices, stacte, and onycha, and galbanum; these sweet spices with pure frankincense: of each shall there be a like weight:* *And when they were come into the house, they saw the young child with Mary his mother, and fell down, and worshipped him: and when they had opened their treasures, they presented unto him gifts; gold, and frankincense, and myrrh.* (Matthew 2:11) The frankincense among the spices Moses was given for the holy incense is the second gift laid before the child. It was *pure frankincense* in the worship of Yahuah (the LORD) at the tabernacle, so a priestly thing is set at the feet of a King.
cards.prose: The frankincense among the spices Moses was given for the holy incense is the second gift laid before the child. It was *pure frankincense* in the worship of Yahuah (the LORD) at the tabernacle, so a priestly thing is set at the feet of a King.
cards.member_note: Exodus 30:34 — *Take unto thee sweet spices, stacte, and onycha, and galbanum; these sweet spices with pure frankincense.* Yahuah (the LORD) tells Moses to compound the holy incense with pure frankincense, the priestly use of the gift the wise men bring.

cards.src_text: And when they were come into the house, they saw the young child with Mary his mother, and fell down, and worshipped him: and when they had opened their treasures, they presented unto him gifts; gold, and frankincense, and myrrh.
cards.tgt_text: All thy garments smell of myrrh, and aloes, and cassia, out of the ivory palaces, whereby they have made thee glad.
cards.old_note: *All thy garments smell of myrrh, and aloes, and cassia* — the Messianic-bridegroom psalm naming myrrh as a Messianic-royal attribute. The myrrh-gift also foreshadows the burial-preparation of Yahusha (Jesus) — myrrh appears at his birth and at his death (John 19:39).
cards.note: Psalm 45:8 — *All thy garments smell of myrrh, and aloes, and cassia, out of the ivory palaces, whereby they have made thee glad.* *And when they were come into the house, they saw the young child with Mary his mother, and fell down, and worshipped him: and when they had opened their treasures, they presented unto him gifts; gold, and frankincense, and myrrh.* (Matthew 2:11) Myrrh scents the garments of the King in this psalm, so it is a royal gift before it is anything else. The wise men put it in the hands of a child, and myrrh is also what a body is anointed with, so it points ahead to the day he would be given it again.
cards.prose: Myrrh scents the garments of the King in this psalm, so it is a royal gift before it is anything else. The wise men put it in the hands of a child, and myrrh is also what a body is anointed with, so it points ahead to the day he would be given it again.
cards.member_note: Psalm 45:8 — *All thy garments smell of myrrh, and aloes, and cassia, out of the ivory palaces, whereby they have made thee glad.* Myrrh, aloes and cassia scent the King's garments in the psalm, a royal perfume that the wise men lay before the child.

cards.src_text: But when he heard that Archelaus did reign in Judaea in the room of his father Herod, he was afraid to go thither: notwithstanding, being warned of Elohim (God) in a dream, he turned aside into the parts of Galilee:
cards.tgt_text: Nevertheless the dimness shall not be such as was in her vexation, when at the first he lightly afflicted the land of Zebulun and the land of Naphtali, and afterward did more grievously afflict her by the way of the sea, beyond Jordan, in Galilee of the nations.
cards.old_note: *The land of Zevulun (Zebulun), and the land of Naphtali ... the people that walked in darkness have seen a great light* — the Galilee-of-the-Gentiles prophecy that Matthew 4:13-16 will explicitly cite, prepared by Matthew 2:22-23's settling in the Galilee.
cards.note: Isaiah 9:1 — *Nevertheless the dimness shall not be such as was in her vexation, when at the first he lightly afflicted the land of Zebulun and the land of Naphtali, and afterward did more grievously afflict her by the way of the sea, beyond Jordan, in Galilee of the nations.* *But when he heard that Archelaus did reign in Judaea in the room of his father Herod, he was afraid to go thither: notwithstanding, being warned of Elohim (God) in a dream, he turned aside into the parts of Galilee:* (Matthew 2:22) Joseph turns *aside into the parts of Galilee*, and Isaiah's verse names that country: the land of Zebulun and Naphtali, the northern tribes the Assyrian struck first. It is the old northern ground where the scattered house was carried off, and the light the prophet goes on to promise rises there first.
