cards.src_text: Again, the devil takes him up into an exceeding high mountain, and shows him all the kingdoms of the world, and the glory of them;
cards.tgt_text: For we wrestle not against flesh and blood, but against principalities, against powers, against the rulers of the darkness of this world, against spiritual wickedness in high places.
cards.old_note: *We wrestle not against flesh and blood, but against principalities, against powers, against the rulers of the darkness of this world* — the apostolic naming of the present-age power-structure.
cards.note: Ephesians 6:12 — *For we wrestle not against flesh and blood, but against principalities, against powers, against the rulers of the darkness of this world, against spiritual wickedness in high places.* *Again, the devil takes him up into an exceeding high mountain, and shows him all the kingdoms of the world, and the glory of them;* (Matthew 4:8) Paul says our struggle is not with flesh and blood but with *the rulers of the darkness of this world*. The devil on the mountain is one of those rulers showing his holdings. The people under the kingdoms are not the enemy, and Yahusha (Jesus) refuses the power behind them.
cards.prose: Paul says our struggle is not with flesh and blood but with *the rulers of the darkness of this world*. The devil on the mountain is one of those rulers showing his holdings. The people under the kingdoms are not the enemy, and Yahusha (Jesus) refuses the power behind them.
cards.member_note: Ephesians 6:12 — *against principalities, against powers, against the rulers of the darkness of this world.* Paul names the principalities and rulers of this world's darkness as the real opponent, not the people under them.

cards.src_text: Again, the devil takes him up into an exceeding high mountain, and shows him all the kingdoms of the world, and the glory of them;
cards.tgt_text: And we know that we are of Elohim (God), and the whole world lieth in wickedness.
cards.old_note: *The whole world lieth in wickedness* — the present-age administration described.
cards.note: 1 John 5:19 — *And we know that we are of Elohim (God), and the whole world lieth in wickedness.* *Again, the devil takes him up into an exceeding high mountain, and shows him all the kingdoms of the world, and the glory of them;* (Matthew 4:8) John says the world as it stands *lieth in wickedness*, and that is the condition of the kingdoms the devil spreads out on the mountain. Those who belong to Elohim (God) know it. Yahusha (Jesus) will not take the world on the world's terms.
cards.prose: John says the world as it stands *lieth in wickedness*, and that is the condition of the kingdoms the devil spreads out on the mountain. Those who belong to Elohim (God) know it. Yahusha (Jesus) will not take the world on the world's terms.
cards.member_note: 1 John 5:19 — *And we know that we are of Elohim (God), and the whole world lieth in wickedness.* John says the whole world lies in wickedness, which is the state of the kingdoms the devil holds out.

cards.src_text: Again, the devil takes him up into an exceeding high mountain, and shows him all the kingdoms of the world, and the glory of them;
cards.tgt_text: I saw in the night visions, and, behold, one like the Son of Adam came with the clouds of heaven, and came to the Ancient of days, and they brought him near before him.
cards.old_note: *One like the Son of Adam came with the clouds of heaven ... and there was given him dominion, and glory, and a kingdom, that all people, nations, and languages, should serve him* — the Father's-timing transfer of the everlasting kingdom that Yahusha (Jesus) waits for; the kaph-comparative preserved as incarnation-honoring.
cards.note: Daniel 7:13 — *I saw in the night visions, and, behold, one like the Son of Adam came with the clouds of heaven, and came to the Ancient of days, and they brought him near before him.* *Again, the devil takes him up into an exceeding high mountain, and shows him all the kingdoms of the world, and the glory of them;* (Matthew 4:8) The devil offers the kingdoms at once, for one act of worship. Daniel sees them given another way, to the one like the Son of Adam brought near the Ancient of days: *And there was given him dominion, and glory, and a kingdom* (Daniel 7:14). That is the Father's gift in the Father's time, and Yahusha (Jesus) waits for it and will not take it from one who has no right to give it.
cards.prose: The devil offers the kingdoms at once, for one act of worship. Daniel sees them given another way, to the one like the Son of Adam brought near the Ancient of days: *And there was given him dominion, and glory, and a kingdom* (Daniel 7:14). That is the Father's gift in the Father's time, and Yahusha (Jesus) waits for it and will not take it from one who has no right to give it.
cards.member_note: Daniel 7:13 — *and they brought him near before him.* Daniel sees the kingdom given to the one like the Son of Adam in the Father's presence, not taken by a bow.

cards.src_text: Again, the devil takes him up into an exceeding high mountain, and shows him all the kingdoms of the world, and the glory of them;
cards.tgt_text: And the seventh angel sounded; and there were great voices in heaven, saying, The kingdoms of this world are become the kingdoms of our Lord, and of his Messiah (Christ); and he shall reign for ever and ever.
cards.old_note: *The kingdoms of this world are become the kingdoms of our Lord, and of his Messiah (Christ); and he shall reign for ever and ever* — the future consummation of the kingdom-transfer Yahusha (Jesus) refused to short-circuit.
cards.note: Revelation 11:15 — *And the seventh angel sounded; and there were great voices in heaven, saying, The kingdoms of this world are become the kingdoms of our Lord, and of his Messiah (Christ); and he shall reign for ever and ever.* *Again, the devil takes him up into an exceeding high mountain, and shows him all the kingdoms of the world, and the glory of them;* (Matthew 4:8) The kingdoms the devil held out do become the Messiah's (Christ's), but Revelation shows it happening at the sound of the seventh angel, with *great voices in heaven* announcing it. Yahusha (Jesus) refuses the short road by worship and receives the whole of it in the right hour.
cards.prose: The kingdoms the devil held out do become the Messiah's (Christ's), but Revelation shows it happening at the sound of the seventh angel, with *great voices in heaven* announcing it. Yahusha (Jesus) refuses the short road by worship and receives the whole of it in the right hour.
cards.member_note: Revelation 11:15 — *The kingdoms of this world are become the kingdoms of our Lord, and of his Messiah (Christ).* The kingdoms of this world become the Messiah's (Christ's) at the seventh trumpet, on the Father's timing.

cards.src_text: Again, the devil takes him up into an exceeding high mountain, and shows him all the kingdoms of the world, and the glory of them;
cards.tgt_text: And I will put enmity between thee and the woman, and between thy seed and her seed; it shall bruise thy head, and thou shalt bruise his heel.
cards.old_note: The original promise of the seed-of-the-woman bruising the serpent's head — the cross is the bruise; the temptation to take the kingdoms without the cross is the temptation to skip the prophecy.
cards.note: Genesis 3:15 — *And I will put enmity between thee and the woman, and between thy seed and her seed; it shall bruise thy head, and thou shalt bruise his heel.* *Again, the devil takes him up into an exceeding high mountain, and shows him all the kingdoms of the world, and the glory of them;* (Matthew 4:8) The serpent of the garden is the one now standing on the mountain, and the word spoken to him was that the woman's seed would *bruise* his head while he bruised the heel. The road to the kingdom runs through that heel, through the cross, and the offer on the mountain is a way around it. Yahusha (Jesus) will not skip what was spoken from the beginning.
cards.prose: The serpent of the garden is the one now standing on the mountain, and the word spoken to him was that the woman's seed would *bruise* his head while he bruised the heel. The road to the kingdom runs through that heel, through the cross, and the offer on the mountain is a way around it. Yahusha (Jesus) will not skip what was spoken from the beginning.
cards.member_note: Genesis 3:15 — *and between thy seed and her seed; it shall bruise thy head, and thou shalt bruise his heel.* The first word to the serpent says the seed of the woman will bruise his head, and the heel is bruised on the way.

cards.src_text: And says unto him, If you be the Son of Elohim (God), cast thyself down: for it is written, He shall give his angels charge concerning you: and in their hands they shall bear you up, lest at any time you dash your foot against a stone.
cards.tgt_text: Because he hath set his love upon me, therefore will I deliver him: I will set him on high, because he hath known my name.
cards.old_note: *Because he hath set his love upon me, therefore will I deliver him* — another qualifier-verse in the Psalm establishing the covenant-faithfulness condition of the promise.
cards.note: Psalm 91:14 — *Because he hath set his love upon me, therefore will I deliver him: I will set him on high, because he hath known my name.* *And says unto him, If you be the Son of Elohim (God), cast thyself down: for it is written, He shall give his angels charge concerning you: and in their hands they shall bear you up, lest at any time you dash your foot against a stone.* (Matthew 4:6) The psalm gives its reason in the same breath: the one delivered is he who *hath set his love upon me*, and who *hath known my name*. The devil's dare asks for deliverance with no love in it, only proof. The one who loves the Father keeps his word, so he will not throw himself down to see whether he will be caught.
cards.prose: The psalm gives its reason in the same breath: the one delivered is he who *hath set his love upon me*, and who *hath known my name*. The devil's dare asks for deliverance with no love in it, only proof. The one who loves the Father keeps his word, so he will not throw himself down to see whether he will be caught.
cards.member_note: Psalm 91:14 — *Because he hath set his love upon me, therefore will I deliver him: I will set him on high, because he hath known my name.* The promise of deliverance goes to the one who has set his love on Yahuah (the LORD) and known his name, not to a dare.

cards.src_text: Then the devil leaveth him, and, behold, angels came and ministered unto him.
cards.tgt_text: Are they not all ministering spirits, sent forth to minister for them who shall be heirs of salvation?
cards.old_note: *Are they not all ministering spirits, sent forth to minister for them who shall be heirs of salvation* — the standing angelic-ministry role; Matt 4:11 is the unforced fulfillment of what the devil had wanted to manipulate as a sign-test at vv.5-7.
cards.note: Hebrews 1:14 — *Are they not all ministering spirits, sent forth to minister for them who shall be heirs of salvation?* *Then the devil leaveth him, and, behold, angels came and ministered unto him.* (Matthew 4:11) After the third refusal angels come and serve him, which is what the devil wanted to stage as a sign on the pinnacle. Hebrews says what angels are for, *ministering spirits* sent for the heirs, and here it simply happens, with no leap to force it.
cards.prose: After the third refusal angels come and serve him, which is what the devil wanted to stage as a sign on the pinnacle. Hebrews says what angels are for, *ministering spirits* sent for the heirs, and here it simply happens, with no leap to force it.
cards.member_note: Hebrews 1:14 — *Are they not all ministering spirits, sent forth to minister for them who shall be heirs of salvation?* Angels are ministering spirits sent to serve the heirs, and here they come on their own once the testing is over.

cards.src_text: Then the devil leaveth him, and, behold, angels came and ministered unto him.
cards.tgt_text: And as he lay and slept under a juniper tree, behold, then an angel touched him, and said unto him, Arise and eat.
cards.old_note: Eliyahu (Elijah) ministered to by an angel after the contest at Carmel — the Tanakh-pattern of angelic ministry to the prophet after spiritual conflict.
cards.note: 1 Kings 19:5 — *And as he lay and slept under a juniper tree, behold, then an angel touched him, and said unto him, Arise and eat.* *Then the devil leaveth him, and, behold, angels came and ministered unto him.* (Matthew 4:11) Elijah lay worn out in the wilderness, and an angel touched him and fed him, and he went on *forty days and forty nights* (1 Kings 19:8) to Horeb. Yahusha (Jesus) has fasted the same forty days, and when the testing is done the same kind of help comes to him from the same hand.
cards.prose: Elijah lay worn out in the wilderness, and an angel touched him and fed him, and he went on *forty days and forty nights* (1 Kings 19:8) to Horeb. Yahusha (Jesus) has fasted the same forty days, and when the testing is done the same kind of help comes to him from the same hand.
cards.member_note: 1 Kings 19:5 — *And as he lay and slept under a juniper tree, behold, then an angel touched him, and said unto him, Arise and eat.* An angel touches Elijah in the wilderness and tells him to arise and eat, as angels serve Yahusha (Jesus) after his testing.

cards.src_text: From that time Yahusha (Jesus) began to preach, and to say, Repent: for the kingdom of heaven is at hand.
cards.tgt_text: And saying, Repent ye: for the kingdom of heaven is at hand.
cards.old_note: The verbally-identical preaching-formula of Yochanan (John) the Immerser; the deliberate continuity of message between Yochanan (John) and Yahusha (Jesus).
cards.note: Matthew 3:2 — *And saying, Repent ye: for the kingdom of heaven is at hand.* *From that time Yahusha (Jesus) began to preach, and to say, Repent: for the kingdom of heaven is at hand.* (Matthew 4:17) Yahusha (Jesus) takes up John's very words, with nothing changed. He does not start something new where John left off; he goes on with the same call, because the one who prepared the way and the one who came after are carrying one message.
cards.prose: Yahusha (Jesus) takes up John's very words, with nothing changed. He does not start something new where John left off; he goes on with the same call, because the one who prepared the way and the one who came after are carrying one message.
cards.member_note: Matthew 3:2 — *And saying, Repent ye: for the kingdom of heaven is at hand.* John the Immerser cries the same call to turn that Yahusha (Jesus) takes up in Galilee, one message passed on.

cards.src_text: From that time Yahusha (Jesus) began to preach, and to say, Repent: for the kingdom of heaven is at hand.
cards.tgt_text: And in the days of these kings shall the Elohim (God) of heaven set up a kingdom, which shall never be destroyed: and the kingdom shall not be left to other people, but it shall break in pieces and consume all these kingdoms, and it shall stand for ever.
cards.old_note: *In the days of these kings shall the Elohim (God) of heaven set up a kingdom, which shall never be destroyed* — the Tanakh-source of the everlasting kingdom Yahusha (Jesus) names as *at hand.*
cards.note: Daniel 2:44 — *And in the days of these kings shall the Elohim (God) of heaven set up a kingdom, which shall never be destroyed: and the kingdom shall not be left to other people, but it shall break in pieces and consume all these kingdoms, and it shall stand for ever.* *From that time Yahusha (Jesus) began to preach, and to say, Repent: for the kingdom of heaven is at hand.* (Matthew 4:17) The kingdom he announces is the one Daniel told the king about, set up by the Elohim (God) of heaven in the days of those kings, and one that *shall never be destroyed*. It is not a new idea arriving with the gospel. It is the old promise being called near.
cards.prose: The kingdom he announces is the one Daniel told the king about, set up by the Elohim (God) of heaven in the days of those kings, and one that *shall never be destroyed*. It is not a new idea arriving with the gospel. It is the old promise being called near.
cards.member_note: Daniel 2:44 — *shall the Elohim (God) of heaven set up a kingdom, which shall never be destroyed.* Daniel told the king the Elohim (God) of heaven would set up a kingdom that never ends, the kingdom Yahusha (Jesus) calls at hand.

cards.src_text: From that time Yahusha (Jesus) began to preach, and to say, Repent: for the kingdom of heaven is at hand.
cards.tgt_text: I saw in the night visions, and, behold, one like the Son of Adam came with the clouds of heaven, and came to the Ancient of days, and they brought him near before him.
cards.old_note: The Son-of-Adam-kingdom-transfer prophecy (kaph-comparative preserved); the kingdom-at-hand is this kingdom.
cards.note: Daniel 7:13 — *I saw in the night visions, and, behold, one like the Son of Adam came with the clouds of heaven, and came to the Ancient of days, and they brought him near before him.* *From that time Yahusha (Jesus) began to preach, and to say, Repent: for the kingdom of heaven is at hand.* (Matthew 4:17) Daniel saw *one like the Son of Adam* come to the Ancient of days to receive the kingdom, and that is whose kingdom Yahusha (Jesus) calls near. When he says it is at hand he speaks as the one Daniel saw, though the receiving of it waits on the Father's time.
cards.prose: Daniel saw *one like the Son of Adam* come to the Ancient of days to receive the kingdom, and that is whose kingdom Yahusha (Jesus) calls near. When he says it is at hand he speaks as the one Daniel saw, though the receiving of it waits on the Father's time.
cards.member_note: Daniel 7:13 — *one like the Son of Adam came with the clouds of heaven, and came to the Ancient of days.* Daniel sees the one like the Son of Adam brought to the Ancient of days, the king whose kingdom is at hand.

cards.src_text: And Yahusha (Jesus) went about all Galilee, teaching in their synagogues, and preaching the gospel of the kingdom, and healing all manner of sickness and all manner of disease among the people.
cards.tgt_text: Say to them that are of a fearful heart, Be strong, fear not: behold, your Elohim (God) will come with vengeance, even Elohim (God) with a recompence; he will come and save you.
cards.old_note: *Then the eyes of the blind shall be opened ... the lame man leap as an hart* — the Messianic-credential prophecy authenticated by Yahusha's (Jesus's) healing ministry; Yahusha (Jesus) cites this credential himself at Matt 11:2-5 when Yochanan (John) sends from prison to ask.
cards.note: Isaiah 35:4 — *Say to them that are of a fearful heart, Be strong, fear not: behold, your Elohim (God) will come with vengeance, even Elohim (God) with a recompence; he will come and save you.* *And Yahusha (Jesus) went about all Galilee, teaching in their synagogues, and preaching the gospel of the kingdom, and healing all manner of sickness and all manner of disease among the people.* (Matthew 4:23) Isaiah tells the fearful hearts to be strong, because their Elohim (God) is coming to save them, and the next verse says what that coming looks like: *Then the eyes of the blind shall be opened, and the ears of the deaf shall be unstopped.* (Isaiah 35:5) That is the work going on all through Galilee, and it is the sign Yahusha (Jesus) later points John to.
cards.prose: Isaiah tells the fearful hearts to be strong, because their Elohim (God) is coming to save them, and the next verse says what that coming looks like: *Then the eyes of the blind shall be opened, and the ears of the deaf shall be unstopped.* (Isaiah 35:5) That is the work going on all through Galilee, and it is the sign Yahusha (Jesus) later points John to.
cards.member_note: Isaiah 35:4 — *Say to them that are of a fearful heart, Be strong, fear not: behold, your Elohim (God) will come with vengeance, even Elohim (God) with a recompence; he will come and save you.* Isaiah promises that Elohim (God) will come and save, and the opened eyes and ears that follow are what Galilee sees.

cards.src_text: And Yahusha (Jesus) went about all Galilee, teaching in their synagogues, and preaching the gospel of the kingdom, and healing all manner of sickness and all manner of disease among the people.
cards.tgt_text: The Spirit of Adonai Yahuah (the Lord GOD) is upon me; because Yahuah (LORD) hath anointed me to preach good tidings unto the meek; he hath sent me to bind up the brokenhearted, to proclaim liberty to the captives, and the opening of the prison to them that are bound;
cards.old_note: *He hath sent me to bind up the brokenhearted, to proclaim liberty to the captives, and the opening of the prison to them that are bound* — the Messianic-mission summary Yahusha (Jesus) will explicitly quote at Luke 4:18-19 in his Natsareth (Nazareth) synagogue declaration.
cards.note: Isaiah 61:1 — *The Spirit of Adonai Yahuah (the Lord GOD) is upon me; because Yahuah (LORD) hath anointed me to preach good tidings unto the meek; he hath sent me to bind up the brokenhearted, to proclaim liberty to the captives, and the opening of the prison to them that are bound;* *And Yahusha (Jesus) went about all Galilee, teaching in their synagogues, and preaching the gospel of the kingdom, and healing all manner of sickness and all manner of disease among the people.* (Matthew 4:23) Isaiah's anointed one is sent to *bind up the brokenhearted* and to open the prison to the bound, and Galilee is where that work is seen. The preaching and the healing in Matthew are one commission, with the Spirit of Adonai Yahuah (the Lord GOD) resting on him.
cards.prose: Isaiah's anointed one is sent to *bind up the brokenhearted* and to open the prison to the bound, and Galilee is where that work is seen. The preaching and the healing in Matthew are one commission, with the Spirit of Adonai Yahuah (the Lord GOD) resting on him.
cards.member_note: Isaiah 61:1 — *he hath sent me to bind up the brokenhearted, to proclaim liberty to the captives.* The anointed one is sent to bind up the brokenhearted and free the captives, the commission Yahusha (Jesus) carries through Galilee.

cards.src_text: You have heard that it was said by them of old time, You shall not kill; and whosoever shall kill shall be in danger of the judgment:
cards.tgt_text: Thou shalt not hate thy brother in thine heart: thou shalt in any wise rebuke thy neighbour, and not suffer sin upon him.
cards.old_note: *Thou shalt not hate thy brother in thine heart* — the Torah's heart-substance of the sixth commandment; the oral tradition stopped at the act, the Torah always taught the heart-root.
cards.note: Leviticus 19:17 — *Thou shalt not hate thy brother in thine heart: thou shalt in any wise rebuke thy neighbour, and not suffer sin upon him.* *You have heard that it was said by them of old time, You shall not kill; and whosoever shall kill shall be in danger of the judgment:* (Matthew 5:21) The saying that had been handed down about killing stopped at the deed, and Moses had never stopped there. He had already put the commandment in the heart, in *Thou shalt not hate thy brother in thine heart*, so when Yahusha (Jesus) speaks of anger he is setting the sixth word back where it was given.
cards.prose: The saying that had been handed down about killing stopped at the deed, and Moses had never stopped there. He had already put the commandment in the heart, in *Thou shalt not hate thy brother in thine heart*, so when Yahusha (Jesus) speaks of anger he is setting the sixth word back where it was given.
cards.member_note: Leviticus 19:17 — *Thou shalt not hate thy brother in thine heart: thou shalt in any wise rebuke thy neighbour, and not suffer sin upon him.* Moses forbids the hatred in the heart and the bearing of sin on a neighbour, which is where the sixth commandment was always rooted.

cards.src_text: You have heard that it was said by them of old time, You shall not commit adultery:
cards.tgt_text: Thou shalt not covet thy neighbour’s house, thou shalt not covet thy neighbour’s wife, nor his manservant, nor his maidservant, nor his ox, nor his ass, nor any thing that is thy neighbour’s.
cards.old_note: *Thou shalt not covet thy neighbour's wife* — the tenth commandment, naming the heart-coveting that precedes the act of adultery; the Torah already named the heart-substance.
cards.note: Exodus 20:17 — *Thou shalt not covet thy neighbour’s house, thou shalt not covet thy neighbour’s wife, nor his manservant, nor his maidservant, nor his ox, nor his ass, nor any thing that is thy neighbour’s.* *You have heard that it was said by them of old time, You shall not commit adultery:* (Matthew 5:27) What was heard about adultery had been narrowed to the act. The tenth word of Moses names the wanting, so the look Yahusha (Jesus) speaks of is the seventh commandment and the tenth kept side by side as they were given, with the heart as the place where both are broken first.
cards.prose: What was heard about adultery had been narrowed to the act. The tenth word of Moses names the wanting, so the look Yahusha (Jesus) speaks of is the seventh commandment and the tenth kept side by side as they were given, with the heart as the place where both are broken first.
cards.member_note: Exodus 20:17 — *Thou shalt not covet thy neighbour’s house, thou shalt not covet thy neighbour’s wife.* The tenth commandment forbids coveting a neighbour's wife, so the Torah had already named the desire that comes before the act.

cards.src_text: It has been said, Whosoever shall put away his wife, let him give her a writing of divorcement:
cards.tgt_text: Therefore shall a man leave his father and his mother, and shall cleave unto his wife: and they shall be one flesh.
cards.old_note: *Therefore shall a man leave his father and his mother, and shall cleave unto his wife: and they shall be one flesh* — the original marriage-design Yahusha (Jesus) restores; Yahusha (Jesus) will explicitly cite this at Matt 19:4-9 as the framework against the Pharisees' Devarim (Deuteronomy) 24:1 question.
cards.note: Genesis 2:24 — *Therefore shall a man leave his father and his mother, and shall cleave unto his wife: and they shall be one flesh.* *It has been said, Whosoever shall put away his wife, let him give her a writing of divorcement:* (Matthew 5:31) The writing of divorcement spoke of how a marriage is ended and never said what a marriage is. Here, at the very start, it is said: a man leaves his father and mother, cleaves to his wife, and the two are one flesh. That beginning is what Yahusha (Jesus) sets the question against.
cards.prose: The writing of divorcement spoke of how a marriage is ended and never said what a marriage is. Here, at the very start, it is said: a man leaves his father and mother, cleaves to his wife, and the two are one flesh. That beginning is what Yahusha (Jesus) sets the question against.
cards.member_note: Genesis 2:24 — *Therefore shall a man leave his father and his mother, and shall cleave unto his wife: and they shall be one flesh.* The first marriage tells what a marriage is, one flesh from the beginning, and that is the measure for any talk of putting a wife away.

cards.src_text: It has been said, Whosoever shall put away his wife, let him give her a writing of divorcement:
cards.tgt_text: He saith unto them, Moses because of the hardness of your hearts suffered you to put away your wives: but from the beginning it was not so.
cards.old_note: *Mosheh (Moses) because of the hardness of your hearts suffered you to put away your wives: but from the beginning it was not so* — Yahusha's (Jesus's) explicit interpretation of Devarim (Deuteronomy) 24:1 as concession-to-hardness, not Torah-mandate-of-permission.
cards.note: Matthew 19:8 — *He saith unto them, Moses because of the hardness of your hearts suffered you to put away your wives: but from the beginning it was not so.* *It has been said, Whosoever shall put away his wife, let him give her a writing of divorcement:* (Matthew 5:31) When the Pharisees pressed him, Yahusha (Jesus) told them what the writing of divorcement was. Moses suffered it because of hard hearts, and from the beginning it was not so. So he is not overturning Moses in the Sermon, he is pointing back past the allowance to the marriage as it began.
cards.prose: When the Pharisees pressed him, Yahusha (Jesus) told them what the writing of divorcement was. Moses suffered it because of hard hearts, and from the beginning it was not so. So he is not overturning Moses in the Sermon, he is pointing back past the allowance to the marriage as it began.
cards.member_note: Matthew 19:8 — *Moses because of the hardness of your hearts suffered you to put away your wives.* Yahusha (Jesus) himself says Moses allowed the writing of divorcement because of hard hearts and that it was not so from the beginning.

cards.src_text: Again, you have heard that it has been said by them of old time, You shall not forswear thyself, but shall perform unto Yahuah (Lord) your oaths:
cards.tgt_text: Woe unto you, ye blind guides, which say, Whosoever shall swear by the temple, it is nothing; but whosoever shall swear by the gold of the temple, he is a debtor!
cards.old_note: Yahusha (Jesus) at Matt 23 indicts the same gradation-system explicitly — *whosoever shall swear by the temple, it is nothing; but whosoever shall swear by the gold of the temple, he is a debtor* — confirming that Matt 5:33-37 is correction of the oral-tradition apparatus, not abolition of all oath-taking.
cards.note: Matthew 23:16 — *Woe unto you, ye blind guides, which say, Whosoever shall swear by the temple, it is nothing; but whosoever shall swear by the gold of the temple, he is a debtor!* *Again, you have heard that it has been said by them of old time, You shall not forswear thyself, but shall perform unto Yahuah (Lord) your oaths:* (Matthew 5:33) What had been piled on the commandment about oaths shows plainly in the woes. A man who swore by the temple was said to owe nothing, while one who swore by its gold was bound. Yahusha (Jesus) is not striking down the oath Moses gave, he is clearing off the ladder of grades the scribes built on it.
cards.prose: What had been piled on the commandment about oaths shows plainly in the woes. A man who swore by the temple was said to owe nothing, while one who swore by its gold was bound. Yahusha (Jesus) is not striking down the oath Moses gave, he is clearing off the ladder of grades the scribes built on it.
cards.member_note: Matthew 23:16 — *Whosoever shall swear by the temple, it is nothing; but whosoever shall swear by the gold of the temple.* Yahusha (Jesus) names the system of graded oaths the scribes taught, which is what the saying in the Sermon had grown into.

cards.src_text: You have heard that it has been said, An eye for an eye, and a tooth for a tooth:
cards.tgt_text: For rulers are not a terror to good works, but to the evil. Wilt thou then not be afraid of the power? do that which is good, and thou shalt have praise of the same:
cards.old_note: *Rulers are not a terror to good works ... he beareth not the sword in vain: for he is the minister of Elohim (God), a revenger to execute wrath upon him that doeth evil* — the apostolic confirmation that the judicial-sphere retains the sword and the *lex talionis* function; Matt 5:38-42 is personal-disciple ethic, not abolition of the judicial Torah.
cards.note: Romans 13:3 — *For rulers are not a terror to good works, but to the evil. Wilt thou then not be afraid of the power? do that which is good, and thou shalt have praise of the same:* *You have heard that it has been said, An eye for an eye, and a tooth for a tooth:* (Matthew 5:38) An eye for an eye was a measure for the judge, keeping payment to the size of the wrong, and Paul shows the ruler still holds that office, one who is *not a terror to good works* but to the evil. What Yahusha (Jesus) answers in the Sermon is the private man taking that measure into his own hand.
cards.prose: An eye for an eye was a measure for the judge, keeping payment to the size of the wrong, and Paul shows the ruler still holds that office, one who is *not a terror to good works* but to the evil. What Yahusha (Jesus) answers in the Sermon is the private man taking that measure into his own hand.
cards.member_note: Romans 13:3 — *For rulers are not a terror to good works, but to the evil.* Paul shows the ruler's office to punish evil still stands, so the Sermon speaks to the person wronged and not to the court.

cards.src_text: You have heard that it has been said, You shall love your neighbour, and hate your enemy.
cards.tgt_text: But the stranger that dwelleth with you shall be unto you as one born among you, and thou shalt love him as thyself; for ye were strangers in the land of Egypt: I am Yahuah Elohaychem (the LORD your God).
cards.old_note: *The stranger that dwelleth with you shall be unto you as one born among you, and thou shalt love him as thyself* — the Torah's extension of the love-command to the stranger, the part the oral tradition had ignored.
cards.note: Leviticus 19:34 — *But the stranger that dwelleth with you shall be unto you as one born among you, and thou shalt love him as thyself; for ye were strangers in the land of Egypt: I am Yahuah Elohaychem (the LORD your God).* *You have heard that it has been said, You shall love your neighbour, and hate your enemy.* (Matthew 5:43) The saying took the neighbour commandment and added *hate thine enemy* to it. Moses had written the opposite, setting the stranger who lives among them beside the native born and telling them to love him as themselves. Yahusha (Jesus) takes off what was added and gives back what Moses wrote.
cards.prose: The saying took the neighbour commandment and added *hate thine enemy* to it. Moses had written the opposite, setting the stranger who lives among them beside the native born and telling them to love him as themselves. Yahusha (Jesus) takes off what was added and gives back what Moses wrote.
cards.member_note: Leviticus 19:34 — *the stranger that dwelleth with you shall be unto you as one born among you, and thou shalt love him as thyself.* Moses already extends the love command to the stranger dwelling with them, a part the added saying left out.

cards.src_text: You have heard that it has been said, You shall love your neighbour, and hate your enemy.
cards.tgt_text: If thou meet thine enemy’s ox or his ass going astray, thou shalt surely bring it back to him again.
cards.old_note: *If thou meet thine enemy's ox or his ass going astray, thou shalt surely bring it back to him again ... thou shalt surely help with him* — the Torah's positive command toward the enemy; there is no *hate thine enemy* command anywhere in the Tanakh.
cards.note: Exodus 23:4 — *If thou meet thine enemy’s ox or his ass going astray, thou shalt surely bring it back to him again.* *You have heard that it has been said, You shall love your neighbour, and hate your enemy.* (Matthew 5:43) There is no word of Moses telling anyone to hate an enemy, and the law says the plain opposite in work: find his ox wandering and take it back to him. Whoever tacked *hate thine enemy* onto the neighbour commandment was laying something on top of it, and Yahusha (Jesus) lifts it off.
cards.prose: There is no word of Moses telling anyone to hate an enemy, and the law says the plain opposite in work: find his ox wandering and take it back to him. Whoever tacked *hate thine enemy* onto the neighbour commandment was laying something on top of it, and Yahusha (Jesus) lifts it off.
cards.member_note: Exodus 23:4 — *If thou meet thine enemy’s ox or his ass going astray, thou shalt surely bring it back to him again.* The Torah commands a hand of help toward an enemy's straying animal, and nowhere commands hatred of an enemy.

cards.src_text: You have heard that it has been said, You shall love your neighbour, and hate your enemy.
cards.tgt_text: If thine enemy be hungry, give him bread to eat; and if he be thirsty, give him water to drink:
cards.old_note: *If thine enemy be hungry, give him bread to eat; and if he be thirsty, give him water to drink* — the wisdom-stream's love-of-enemy ethic; Paul quotes this directly at Romans 12:20.
cards.note: Proverbs 25:21 — *If thine enemy be hungry, give him bread to eat; and if he be thirsty, give him water to drink:* *You have heard that it has been said, You shall love your neighbour, and hate your enemy.* (Matthew 5:43) Solomon's proverb already put love for an enemy into bread and water, feeding the one who hungers and giving drink to the one who thirsts. Those who knew the Proverbs had not been taught to hate their enemies, and Yahusha (Jesus) speaks the same word they had open before them.
cards.prose: Solomon's proverb already put love for an enemy into bread and water, feeding the one who hungers and giving drink to the one who thirsts. Those who knew the Proverbs had not been taught to hate their enemies, and Yahusha (Jesus) speaks the same word they had open before them.
cards.member_note: Proverbs 25:21 — *If thine enemy be hungry, give him bread to eat; and if he be thirsty, give him water to drink:* The Proverbs tell the reader to feed a hungry enemy and give him water, which is love for an enemy shown in deed.

cards.src_text: Be you therefore perfect, even as your Father which is in heaven is perfect.
cards.tgt_text: And when Abram was ninety years old and nine, Yahuah (LORD) appeared to Abram, and said unto him, I am the El Shaddai (Almighty God); walk before me, and be thou perfect.
cards.old_note: *I am El Shaddai (the Almighty God); walk before me, and be thou perfect (tamim)* — the *tamim*-standard from the Torah; *teleios* at Matt 5:48 is the Greek translation of *tamim.*
cards.note: Genesis 17:1 — *And when Abram was ninety years old and nine, Yahuah (LORD) appeared to Abram, and said unto him, I am the El Shaddai (Almighty God); walk before me, and be thou perfect.* *Be you therefore perfect, even as your Father which is in heaven is perfect.* (Matthew 5:48) Abram heard *walk before me, and be thou perfect* from Yahuah (the LORD) long before the Sermon, and the Father who is perfect is the measure in both places. So the perfection asked on the mountain is the whole, upright walk Elohim (God) asked of Abram, not some new height.
cards.prose: Abram heard *walk before me, and be thou perfect* from Yahuah (the LORD) long before the Sermon, and the Father who is perfect is the measure in both places. So the perfection asked on the mountain is the whole, upright walk Elohim (God) asked of Abram, not some new height.
cards.member_note: Genesis 17:1 — *I am the El Shaddai (Almighty God); walk before me, and be thou perfect.* Yahuah (the LORD) told Abram to walk before him and be perfect, the same standard the Sermon closes on.

cards.src_text: Blessed are the poor in spirit: for theirs is the kingdom of heaven.
cards.tgt_text: For thus saith the high and lofty One that inhabiteth eternity, whose name is Holy; I dwell in the high and holy place, with him also that is of a contrite and humble spirit, to revive the spirit of the humble, and to revive the heart of the contrite ones.
cards.old_note: *I dwell in the high and holy place, with him also that is of a contrite and humble spirit* — the Tanakh-anchor of the *anawim*-posture.
cards.note: Isaiah 57:15 — *For thus saith the high and lofty One that inhabiteth eternity, whose name is Holy; I dwell in the high and holy place, with him also that is of a contrite and humble spirit, to revive the spirit of the humble, and to revive the heart of the contrite ones.* *Blessed are the poor in spirit: for theirs is the kingdom of heaven.* (Matthew 5:3) The poor in spirit are the very people Yahuah (the LORD) says he dwells with, the One who inhabits eternity keeping company with the contrite and the humble. Since the kingdom is theirs, it is no surprise that the same verse promises to revive them.
cards.prose: The poor in spirit are the very people Yahuah (the LORD) says he dwells with, the One who inhabits eternity keeping company with the contrite and the humble. Since the kingdom is theirs, it is no surprise that the same verse promises to revive them.
cards.member_note: Isaiah 57:15 — *I dwell in the high and holy place, with him also that is of a contrite and humble spirit.* The high and holy One says he dwells with the contrite and humble spirit and revives it.

cards.src_text: Blessed are they that mourn: for they shall be comforted.
cards.tgt_text: And Yahuah (LORD) said unto him, Go through the midst of the city, through the midst of Jerusalem, and set a mark upon the foreheads of the men that sigh and that cry for all the abominations that be done in the midst thereof.
cards.old_note: *Set a mark upon the foreheads of the men that sigh and that cry for all the abominations* — the framework reading: mourning is the prophetic-cry against abominations; the mark of Yahuah (the LORD) falls on this posture.
cards.note: Ezekiel 9:4 — *And Yahuah (LORD) said unto him, Go through the midst of the city, through the midst of Jerusalem, and set a mark upon the foreheads of the men that sigh and that cry for all the abominations that be done in the midst thereof.* *Blessed are they that mourn: for they shall be comforted.* (Matthew 5:4) The mourners here are not only sad. They are the men *that sigh and that cry for all the abominations*, and Yahuah (the LORD) marks them before the sword goes through the city. The comfort Yahusha (Jesus) promises belongs to that grief over what is done against Elohim (God).
cards.prose: The mourners here are not only sad. They are the men *that sigh and that cry for all the abominations*, and Yahuah (the LORD) marks them before the sword goes through the city. The comfort Yahusha (Jesus) promises belongs to that grief over what is done against Elohim (God).
cards.member_note: Ezekiel 9:4 — *set a mark upon the foreheads of the men that sigh and that cry for all the abominations.* Those who sigh and cry over the abominations in the city are the ones Yahuah (the LORD) sets his mark upon.

cards.src_text: Blessed are they which do hunger and thirst after righteousness: for they shall be filled.
cards.tgt_text: As the hart panteth after the water brooks, so panteth my soul after thee, O Elohim (God).
cards.old_note: *As the hart panteth after the water brooks, so panteth my soul after thee, O Elohim (God)* — the Tanakh-hunger-and-thirst posture.
cards.note: Psalm 42:1 — *As the hart panteth after the water brooks, so panteth my soul after thee, O Elohim (God).* *Blessed are they which do hunger and thirst after righteousness: for they shall be filled.* (Matthew 5:6) To hunger and thirst after righteousness is the longing of the hart at the water brooks, a soul crying for Elohim (God) himself. The promise that *they shall be filled* is the answer to that panting.
cards.prose: To hunger and thirst after righteousness is the longing of the hart at the water brooks, a soul crying for Elohim (God) himself. The promise that *they shall be filled* is the answer to that panting.
cards.member_note: Psalm 42:1 — *As the hart panteth after the water brooks, so panteth my soul after thee, O Elohim (God).* The psalmist's soul pants after Elohim (God) like a deer after water, the thirst the Beatitude pronounces blessed.

cards.src_text: Blessed are they which do hunger and thirst after righteousness: for they shall be filled.
cards.tgt_text: Behold, the days come, saith Yahuah (LORD), that I will raise unto David a righteous Branch, and a King shall reign and prosper, and shall execute judgment and justice in the earth.
cards.old_note: *In his days Yahudah (Judah) shall be saved, and Yashar'el (Israel) shall dwell safely: and this is his name whereby he shall be called, Yahuah Tsidkenu (THE LORD OUR RIGHTEOUSNESS)* — the Messianic-source of the *tsedaqah* the hungering ones are filled with.
cards.note: Jeremiah 23:5 — *Behold, the days come, saith Yahuah (LORD), that I will raise unto David a righteous Branch, and a King shall reign and prosper, and shall execute judgment and justice in the earth.* *Blessed are they which do hunger and thirst after righteousness: for they shall be filled.* (Matthew 5:6) The righteousness the hungry are filled with has a person behind it, the righteous Branch raised up to David, and the next verse gives his name: *Yahuah Tsidkenu (THE LORD OUR RIGHTEOUSNESS)* (Jeremiah 23:6). Yahusha (Jesus) is that Branch, speaking on the mountain to the ones who hunger.
cards.prose: The righteousness the hungry are filled with has a person behind it, the righteous Branch raised up to David, and the next verse gives his name: *Yahuah Tsidkenu (THE LORD OUR RIGHTEOUSNESS)* (Jeremiah 23:6). Yahusha (Jesus) is that Branch, speaking on the mountain to the ones who hunger.
cards.member_note: Jeremiah 23:5 — *I will raise unto David a righteous Branch, and a King shall reign and prosper.* A righteous Branch is raised to David to reign and execute judgment and justice, the source of the righteousness the hungry are filled with.

cards.src_text: Blessed are the pure in heart: for they shall see Elohim (God).
cards.tgt_text: Who shall ascend into the hill of Yahuah (LORD)? or who shall stand in his holy place?
cards.old_note: *Who shall ascend into the hill of Yahuah (the LORD)? or who shall stand in his holy place? He that hath clean hands, and a pure heart* — the Tanakh-anchor of the pure-heart ascent.
cards.note: Psalm 24:3 — *Who shall ascend into the hill of Yahuah (LORD)? or who shall stand in his holy place?* *Blessed are the pure in heart: for they shall see Elohim (God).* (Matthew 5:8) The question of who shall stand in the holy place is answered right there: *He that hath clean hands, and a pure heart* (Psalm 24:4). Yahusha (Jesus) takes up that same answer, and the pure in heart who see Elohim (God) are the ones who stand in his place.
cards.prose: The question of who shall stand in the holy place is answered right there: *He that hath clean hands, and a pure heart* (Psalm 24:4). Yahusha (Jesus) takes up that same answer, and the pure in heart who see Elohim (God) are the ones who stand in his place.
cards.member_note: Psalm 24:3 — *Who shall ascend into the hill of Yahuah (LORD)? or who shall stand in his holy place?* The question of who may ascend Yahuah's (the LORD's) hill and stand in his holy place is the one the pure in heart answer.

cards.src_text: Blessed are the pure in heart: for they shall see Elohim (God).
cards.tgt_text: But this shall be the covenant that I will make with the house of Yashar'el (Israel); After those days, saith Yahuah (LORD), I will put my law in their inward parts, and write it in their hearts; and will be their Elohim (God), and they shall be my people.
cards.old_note: *I will put my law in their inward parts, and write it in their hearts* — the new-heart promise that produces the *pure in heart*.
cards.note: Jeremiah 31:33 — *But this shall be the covenant that I will make with the house of Yashar'el (Israel); After those days, saith Yahuah (LORD), I will put my law in their inward parts, and write it in their hearts; and will be their Elohim (God), and they shall be my people.* *Blessed are the pure in heart: for they shall see Elohim (God).* (Matthew 5:8) A pure heart is a heart where the law is written. Yahuah (the LORD) promises to put his law in the inward parts of the house of Yashar'el (Israel), the same law set inside, so those who are pure in heart see Elohim (God) because the commandment is in them where he put it.
cards.prose: A pure heart is a heart where the law is written. Yahuah (the LORD) promises to put his law in the inward parts of the house of Yashar'el (Israel), the same law set inside, so those who are pure in heart see Elohim (God) because the commandment is in them where he put it.
cards.member_note: Jeremiah 31:33 — *I will put my law in their inward parts, and write it in their hearts.* Yahuah (the LORD) promises to write his law in the hearts of the house of Yashar'el (Israel), the source of a pure heart.

cards.src_text: Blessed are the pure in heart: for they shall see Elohim (God).
cards.tgt_text: A new heart also will I give you, and a new spirit will I put within you: and I will take away the stony heart out of your flesh, and I will give you an heart of flesh.
cards.old_note: *A new heart also will I give you* — the new-heart promise companion.
cards.note: Ezekiel 36:26 — *A new heart also will I give you, and a new spirit will I put within you: and I will take away the stony heart out of your flesh, and I will give you an heart of flesh.* *Blessed are the pure in heart: for they shall see Elohim (God).* (Matthew 5:8) Who can be pure in heart? Here Yahuah (the LORD) promises to take away the stony heart and give a heart of flesh. The pure heart is something he gives to the scattered he gathers home, and the next words say what it is for: *cause you to walk in my statutes* (Ezekiel 36:27).
cards.prose: Who can be pure in heart? Here Yahuah (the LORD) promises to take away the stony heart and give a heart of flesh. The pure heart is something he gives to the scattered he gathers home, and the next words say what it is for: *cause you to walk in my statutes* (Ezekiel 36:27).
cards.member_note: Ezekiel 36:26 — *A new heart also will I give you, and a new spirit will I put within you: and I will take away the stony heart out of your flesh, and I will give you an heart of flesh.* Yahuah (the LORD) promises a new heart and a heart of flesh, the gift from which the pure in heart come.

cards.src_text: Think not that I am come to destroy the law, or the prophets: I am not come to destroy, but to fulfil.
cards.tgt_text: Yahuah (LORD) is well pleased for his righteousness’ sake; he will magnify the law, and make it honourable.
cards.old_note: *Yahuah (the LORD) is well pleased for his righteousness' sake; he will magnify the law, and make it honourable* — the Messianic-mission as Torah-magnification, not Torah-abolition; Yahusha (Jesus) walks Yeshayahu (Isaiah) 42:21.
cards.note: Isaiah 42:21 — *Yahuah (LORD) is well pleased for his righteousness’ sake; he will magnify the law, and make it honourable.* *Think not that I am come to destroy the law, or the prophets: I am not come to destroy, but to fulfil.* (Matthew 5:17) Yahuah (the LORD) said of his servant that *he will magnify the law, and make it honourable*, and that is the work Yahusha (Jesus) says he has come to do. To fulfil the law, as he means it, is to make it great and honourable, which is the opposite of destroying it.
cards.prose: Yahuah (the LORD) said of his servant that *he will magnify the law, and make it honourable*, and that is the work Yahusha (Jesus) says he has come to do. To fulfil the law, as he means it, is to make it great and honourable, which is the opposite of destroying it.
cards.member_note: Isaiah 42:21 — *Yahuah (LORD) is well pleased for his righteousness’ sake; he will magnify the law, and make it honourable.* The servant of Yahuah (the LORD) is promised to magnify the law and make it honourable, which is what fulfilling it means.

cards.src_text: Think not that I am come to destroy the law, or the prophets: I am not come to destroy, but to fulfil.
cards.tgt_text: And it is easier for heaven and earth to pass, than one tittle of the law to fail.
cards.old_note: *It is easier for heaven and earth to pass, than one tittle of the law to fail* — the Lukan parallel of Matt 5:18, confirming the framework reading.
cards.note: Luke 16:17 — *And it is easier for heaven and earth to pass, than one tittle of the law to fail.* *Think not that I am come to destroy the law, or the prophets: I am not come to destroy, but to fulfil.* (Matthew 5:17) Luke has the saying on the same ground. The one who says he did not come to destroy is the one who says the smallest stroke of the law will outlast the sky and the ground under it, so both gospels hand the law to the reader whole and standing.
cards.prose: Luke has the saying on the same ground. The one who says he did not come to destroy is the one who says the smallest stroke of the law will outlast the sky and the ground under it, so both gospels hand the law to the reader whole and standing.
cards.member_note: Luke 16:17 — *And it is easier for heaven and earth to pass, than one tittle of the law to fail.* Luke records the same saying, that heaven and earth will pass sooner than one tittle of the law fails.

cards.src_text: Whosoever therefore shall break one of these least commandments, and shall teach men so, he shall be called the least in the kingdom of heaven: but whosoever shall do and teach them, the same shall be called great in the kingdom of heaven.
cards.tgt_text: For whosoever shall keep the whole law, and yet offend in one point, he is guilty of all.
cards.old_note: *Whosoever shall keep the whole law, and yet offend in one point, he is guilty of all* — Ya'aqov's (James's) affirmation of the unity of the commandments; the breaking of *even the least* is named gravely.
cards.note: James 2:10 — *For whosoever shall keep the whole law, and yet offend in one point, he is guilty of all.* *Whosoever therefore shall break one of these least commandments, and shall teach men so, he shall be called the least in the kingdom of heaven: but whosoever shall do and teach them, the same shall be called great in the kingdom of heaven.* (Matthew 5:19) Matthew says the one who breaks the least commandment and teaches others to do so is called least, and James says the same from the other side: the law is one, and offending in a single point reaches the whole of it. Neither leaves a small commandment lying loose for a man to drop.
cards.prose: Matthew says the one who breaks the least commandment and teaches others to do so is called least, and James says the same from the other side: the law is one, and offending in a single point reaches the whole of it. Neither leaves a small commandment lying loose for a man to drop.
cards.member_note: James 2:10 — *For whosoever shall keep the whole law, and yet offend in one point, he is guilty of all.* James says whoever offends in one point of the law is guilty of all, so even the least commandment cannot be dropped.

cards.src_text: Be you therefore perfect, even as your Father which is in heaven is perfect.
cards.tgt_text: But as he which hath called you is holy, so be ye holy in all manner of conversation;
cards.old_note: *But as he which hath called you is holy, so be ye holy in all manner of conversation; Because it is written, Be ye holy; for I am holy* — Kefa's (Peter's) NT carry-forward of the same Torah-pattern.
cards.note: 1 Peter 1:15 — *But as he which hath called you is holy, so be ye holy in all manner of conversation;* *Be you therefore perfect, even as your Father which is in heaven is perfect.* (Matthew 5:48) Peter puts the last word of the Sermon in the same pattern the Torah uses, the one who called you being holy and you being holy as he is. Matthew says perfect as your Father is perfect, and in both places the measure is the Father himself and not a new rule.
cards.prose: Peter puts the last word of the Sermon in the same pattern the Torah uses, the one who called you being holy and you being holy as he is. Matthew says perfect as your Father is perfect, and in both places the measure is the Father himself and not a new rule.
cards.member_note: 1 Peter 1:15 — *But as he which hath called you is holy, so be ye holy in all manner of conversation;* Peter carries forward the same standard, that those called are to be holy as the one who called them is holy.

cards.src_text: But I say unto you, That whosoever shall put away his wife, saving for the cause of fornication, causes her to commit adultery: and whosoever shall marry her that is divorced commits adultery.
cards.tgt_text: For Yahuah (LORD), the Elohim (God) of Yashar'el (Israel), saith that he hateth putting away: for one covereth violence with his garment, saith Yahuah Tseva'ot (LORD of hosts): therefore take heed to your spirit, that ye deal not treacherously.
cards.old_note: *...Therefore take heed to your spirit, and let none deal treacherously against the wife of his youth* (Malachi 2:15). Yahuah (LORD) is witness between a man and the wife of his covenant (Malachi 2:14); He hates the treacherous putting-away. Matthew 5:32 stands squarely on Malachi — divorce wielded against the covenant-wife is treachery.
cards.note: Malachi 2:16 — *For Yahuah (LORD), the Elohim (God) of Yashar'el (Israel), saith that he hateth putting away: for one covereth violence with his garment, saith Yahuah Tseva'ot (LORD of hosts): therefore take heed to your spirit, that ye deal not treacherously.* *But I say unto you, That whosoever shall put away his wife, saving for the cause of fornication, causes her to commit adultery: and whosoever shall marry her that is divorced commits adultery.* (Matthew 5:32) Yahuah (the LORD) says through Malachi that he *hateth putting away*, and what he names is treachery against the wife of a man's covenant. Yahusha (Jesus) speaks the same way about the man who puts his wife away, so his word stands on this one and does not step off it.
cards.prose: Yahuah (the LORD) says through Malachi that he *hateth putting away*, and what he names is treachery against the wife of a man's covenant. Yahusha (Jesus) speaks the same way about the man who puts his wife away, so his word stands on this one and does not step off it.
cards.member_note: Malachi 2:16 — *saith that he hateth putting away: for one covereth violence with his garment.* Yahuah (the LORD) says he hates putting away and calls it treachery, the ground Yahusha's (Jesus's) word on divorce stands on.

cards.src_text: After this manner therefore pray you: Our Father which art in heaven, Hallowed be your name.
cards.tgt_text: Therefore say unto the house of Yashar'el (Israel), Thus saith Adonai Yahuah (the Lord GOD); I do not this for your sakes, O house of Yashar'el (Israel), but for mine holy name’s sake, which ye have profaned among the heathen, whither ye went.
cards.old_note: The sanctification of the Name is *for mine holy name's sake* — the grace-from-name's-sake grammar that the *Hallowed be thy name* prayer presupposes.
cards.note: Ezekiel 36:22 — *Therefore say unto the house of Yashar'el (Israel), Thus saith Adonai Yahuah (the Lord GOD); I do not this for your sakes, O house of Yashar'el (Israel), but for mine holy name’s sake, which ye have profaned among the heathen, whither ye went.* *After this manner therefore pray you: Our Father which art in heaven, Hallowed be your name.* (Matthew 6:9) The prayer asks that the Father's name be hallowed, and the prophet shows whose name that is and why it needs hallowing: the house of Yashar'el (Israel) carried it into the nations and profaned it there. Yahuah (the LORD) says he will act for the sake of that name, so the petition asks him to do what he has already said he would do.
cards.prose: The prayer asks that the Father's name be hallowed, and the prophet shows whose name that is and why it needs hallowing: the house of Yashar'el (Israel) carried it into the nations and profaned it there. Yahuah (the LORD) says he will act for the sake of that name, so the petition asks him to do what he has already said he would do.
cards.member_note: Ezekiel 36:22 — *but for mine holy name’s sake, which ye have profaned among the heathen, whither ye went.* Yahuah (the LORD) says he will act for his own holy name, which his scattered people profaned among the nations.

cards.src_text: And forgive us our debts, as we forgive our debtors.
cards.tgt_text: For on that day shall the priest make an atonement for you, to cleanse you, that ye may be clean from all your sins before Yahuah (LORD).
cards.old_note: *For on that day shall the priest make an atonement for you, to cleanse you, that ye may be clean from all your sins before Yahuah (the LORD)* — the Yom Kippur atonement architecture the forgiveness-petition draws on.
cards.note: Leviticus 16:30 — *For on that day shall the priest make an atonement for you, to cleanse you, that ye may be clean from all your sins before Yahuah (LORD).* *And forgive us our debts, as we forgive our debtors.* (Matthew 6:12) Asking to be forgiven was never a new thing laid on the disciples. Once a year the people were told the priest makes atonement so they may be clean before Yahuah (the LORD), and the petition about debts comes out of that same need to stand clean before him. The words go on to say the one asking must also release his own debtors.
cards.prose: Asking to be forgiven was never a new thing laid on the disciples. Once a year the people were told the priest makes atonement so they may be clean before Yahuah (the LORD), and the petition about debts comes out of that same need to stand clean before him. The words go on to say the one asking must also release his own debtors.
cards.member_note: Leviticus 16:30 — *to cleanse you, that ye may be clean from all your sins before Yahuah (LORD).* The yearly atonement was how the people were made clean from all their sins before Yahuah (the LORD).

cards.src_text: For if you forgive men their trespasses, your heavenly Father will also forgive you:
cards.tgt_text: Then his lord, after that he had called him, said unto him, O thou wicked servant, I forgave thee all that debt, because thou desiredst me:
cards.old_note: The parable of the unforgiving servant — the king reverses the forgiveness; the framework's NT illustration of the principle.
cards.note: Matthew 18:32 — *Then his lord, after that he had called him, said unto him, O thou wicked servant, I forgave thee all that debt, because thou desiredst me:* *For if you forgive men their trespasses, your heavenly Father will also forgive you:* (Matthew 6:14) Here the master says *I forgave thee all that debt* and then calls the servant wicked because he would not show his own fellow the same. The parable puts a face on what the verse says plainly: forgiveness received from the Father is meant to be passed on, and the man who refuses answers for his refusal.
cards.prose: Here the master says *I forgave thee all that debt* and then calls the servant wicked because he would not show his own fellow the same. The parable puts a face on what the verse says plainly: forgiveness received from the Father is meant to be passed on, and the man who refuses answers for his refusal.
cards.member_note: Matthew 18:32 — *O thou wicked servant, I forgave thee all that debt, because thou desiredst me.* A servant who was forgiven a great debt is called wicked for refusing his fellow what he himself received.

cards.src_text: For if you forgive men their trespasses, your heavenly Father will also forgive you:
cards.tgt_text: Woe unto them! for they have fled from me: destruction unto them! because they have transgressed against me: though I have redeemed them, yet they have spoken lies against me.
cards.old_note: *Though I have redeemed them, yet they have spoken lies against me* — the anchor verse for the grace-and-the-opportunity-that-can-be-lost teaching.
cards.note: Hosea 7:13 — *Woe unto them! for they have fled from me: destruction unto them! because they have transgressed against me: though I have redeemed them, yet they have spoken lies against me.* *For if you forgive men their trespasses, your heavenly Father will also forgive you:* (Matthew 6:14) Yahuah (the LORD) says he redeemed these people, and still woe comes on them because they fled from him and spoke lies against him. Being redeemed did not hold them in place once they walked off. That is the weight behind the second half of the verse about forgiveness: what the Father gives, a man can lose by how he turns.
cards.prose: Yahuah (the LORD) says he redeemed these people, and still woe comes on them because they fled from him and spoke lies against him. Being redeemed did not hold them in place once they walked off. That is the weight behind the second half of the verse about forgiveness: what the Father gives, a man can lose by how he turns.
cards.member_note: Hosea 7:13 — *though I have redeemed them, yet they have spoken lies against me.* Though redeemed, the people fled and spoke lies against Yahuah (the LORD), and woe follows them.

cards.src_text: For if you forgive men their trespasses, your heavenly Father will also forgive you:
cards.tgt_text: But when the righteous turneth away from his righteousness, and committeth iniquity, and doeth according to all the abominations that the wicked man doeth, shall he live? All his righteousness that he hath done shall not be mentioned: in his trespass that he hath trespassed, and in his sin that he hath sinned, in them shall he die.
cards.old_note: *When the righteous turneth away from his righteousness, and committeth iniquity ... all his righteousness that he hath done shall not be mentioned* — the righteous can fall away.
cards.note: Ezekiel 18:24 — *But when the righteous turneth away from his righteousness, and committeth iniquity, and doeth according to all the abominations that the wicked man doeth, shall he live? All his righteousness that he hath done shall not be mentioned: in his trespass that he hath trespassed, and in his sin that he hath sinned, in them shall he die.* *For if you forgive men their trespasses, your heavenly Father will also forgive you:* (Matthew 6:14) The prophet says a man counted righteous who turns to iniquity finds his earlier righteousness is not remembered, and in his sin he dies. Forgiveness in the verse stands on the same terms. It is kept as a man goes on in the Father's way, and it is not a standing that cannot be forfeited.

All his righteousness that he hath done shall not be mentioned.* A righteous man who turns to iniquity has his past righteousness set aside, and dies in his sin.

cards.src_text: For if you forgive men their trespasses, your heavenly Father will also forgive you:
cards.tgt_text: Therefore, thou son of Adam, say unto the children of thy people, The righteousness of the righteous shall not deliver him in the day of his transgression: as for the wickedness of the wicked, he shall not fall thereby in the day that he turneth from his wickedness; neither shall the righteous be able to live for his righteousness in the day that he sinneth.
cards.old_note: *The righteousness of the righteous shall not deliver him in the day of his transgression* — explicit naming of the conditional-continuation.
cards.note: Ezekiel 33:12 — *Therefore, thou son of Adam, say unto the children of thy people, The righteousness of the righteous shall not deliver him in the day of his transgression: as for the wickedness of the wicked, he shall not fall thereby in the day that he turneth from his wickedness; neither shall the righteous be able to live for his righteousness in the day that he sinneth.* *For if you forgive men their trespasses, your heavenly Father will also forgive you:* (Matthew 6:14) The prophet sets the matter both ways: yesterday's righteousness does not deliver a man on the day he transgresses, and the wicked who turns is not undone by his old wickedness. So the Father's forgiveness in the verse is spoken to the day a man is standing in, and a refusal to forgive today is not covered by obedience before it.

cards.member_note: Ezekiel 33:12 — *The righteousness of the righteous shall not deliver him in the day of his transgression.* The righteousness of the righteous does not deliver him on the day he transgresses.

cards.src_text: For if you forgive men their trespasses, your heavenly Father will also forgive you:
cards.tgt_text: And Yahuah (LORD) said unto Moses, Whosoever hath sinned against me, him will I blot out of my book.
cards.old_note: *Whosoever hath sinned against me, him will I blot out of my book* — names can be blotted out for lawlessness; the warning is to the wheat, not to the tares.
cards.note: Exodus 32:33 — *And Yahuah (LORD) said unto Moses, Whosoever hath sinned against me, him will I blot out of my book.* *For if you forgive men their trespasses, your heavenly Father will also forgive you:* (Matthew 6:14) Yahuah (the LORD) says this to Moses after the people made the calf, and it is said of those who stand written in his book. Sin against him can cost a name its place there. That is why the Father's word that he will not forgive the one who will not forgive is no figure of speech.
cards.prose: Yahuah (the LORD) says this to Moses after the people made the calf, and it is said of those who stand written in his book. Sin against him can cost a name its place there. That is why the Father's word that he will not forgive the one who will not forgive is no figure of speech.
cards.member_note: Exodus 32:33 — *And Yahuah (LORD) said unto Moses, Whosoever hath sinned against me, him will I blot out of my book.* Whoever has sinned against Yahuah (the LORD) he will blot out of his book, which is a real loss.

cards.src_text: For if you forgive men their trespasses, your heavenly Father will also forgive you:
cards.tgt_text: Let them be blotted out of the book of the living, and not be written with the righteous.
cards.old_note: *Let them be blotted out of the book of the living* — the Psalmist's invocation of the blotting-out architecture.
cards.note: Psalm 69:28 — *Let them be blotted out of the book of the living, and not be written with the righteous.* *For if you forgive men their trespasses, your heavenly Father will also forgive you:* (Matthew 6:14) The psalmist is praying for certain men to lose their place in the book of the living and to stand outside the company of the righteous, so that book is no picture and a name can be taken from it. Matthew's verse draws a line in the same place, between the man who is forgiven and the man who is not, and the line follows whether he forgives.

cards.src_text: For if you forgive men their trespasses, your heavenly Father will also forgive you:
cards.tgt_text: For if we sin wilfully after that we have received the knowledge of the truth, there remaineth no more sacrifice for sins,
cards.old_note: *If we sin wilfully after that we have received the knowledge of the truth, there remaineth no more sacrifice for sins* — the apostolic warning that the redeemed who walk away forfeit the redemption.
cards.note: Hebrews 10:26 — *For if we sin wilfully after that we have received the knowledge of the truth, there remaineth no more sacrifice for sins,* *For if you forgive men their trespasses, your heavenly Father will also forgive you:* (Matthew 6:14) If a man sins on purpose after he has come to know the truth, no sacrifice remains for those sins. That is the door the second half of the verse shuts: the one who knows what the Father asks and still refuses to forgive has chosen the sin, and has no sacrifice left to cover it.

cards.member_note: Hebrews 10:26 — *For if we sin wilfully after that we have received the knowledge of the truth, there remaineth no more sacrifice for sins,* Wilful sin after the truth is known leaves no sacrifice remaining for those sins.

cards.src_text: For if you forgive men their trespasses, your heavenly Father will also forgive you:
cards.tgt_text: Not every one that saith unto me, Adonai (Lord), Adonai (Lord), shall enter into the kingdom of heaven; but he that doeth the will of my Father which is in heaven.
cards.old_note: *I never knew you: depart from me, ye that work iniquity* — Yahusha's (Jesus's) own naming of the forfeit at the close of the Sermon, addressed to those who invoked his name.
cards.note: Matthew 7:21 — *Not every one that saith unto me, Adonai (Lord), Adonai (Lord), shall enter into the kingdom of heaven; but he that doeth the will of my Father which is in heaven.* *For if you forgive men their trespasses, your heavenly Father will also forgive you:* (Matthew 6:14) At the close of the same sermon Yahusha (Jesus) says that calling him by his title does not open the kingdom, only doing the will of the Father does. Forgiving men is part of that will, so the warning here and the warning there come from one mouth about one man, the one who says the right words and does not do them.
cards.prose: At the close of the same sermon Yahusha (Jesus) says that calling him by his title does not open the kingdom, only doing the will of the Father does. Forgiving men is part of that will, so the warning here and the warning there come from one mouth about one man, the one who says the right words and does not do them.
cards.member_note: Matthew 7:21 — *but he that doeth the will of my Father which is in heaven.* Saying his title is not enough for the kingdom, only doing the will of the Father is.

cards.src_text: For if you forgive men their trespasses, your heavenly Father will also forgive you:
cards.tgt_text: If we confess our sins, he is faithful and just to forgive us our sins, and to cleanse us from all unrighteousness.
cards.old_note: *If we confess our sins, he is faithful and just to forgive us our sins* — the standing-receipt of forgiveness contingent on the confession-and-walking-in-light posture; Matt 6:14-15 names the kingdom-citizen's forgiveness-extension as the parallel condition.
cards.note: 1 John 1:9 — *If we confess our sins, he is faithful and just to forgive us our sins, and to cleanse us from all unrighteousness.* *For if you forgive men their trespasses, your heavenly Father will also forgive you:* (Matthew 6:14) John says the Father is *faithful and just to forgive us our sins* when we confess them, so forgiveness is met with something on our side. Yahusha (Jesus) names another thing on our side in this verse, the forgiving of men, and neither one is a wage. Each is how a person stands when he asks to be forgiven.
cards.prose: John says the Father is *faithful and just to forgive us our sins* when we confess them, so forgiveness is met with something on our side. Yahusha (Jesus) names another thing on our side in this verse, the forgiving of men, and neither one is a wage. Each is how a person stands when he asks to be forgiven.
cards.member_note: 1 John 1:9 — *If we confess our sins, he is faithful and just to forgive us our sins, and to cleanse us from all unrighteousness.* Forgiveness comes to the one who confesses his sins, so it is not received apart from a turned heart.

cards.src_text: Take heed that you do not your alms before men, to be seen of them: otherwise you have no reward of your Father which is in heaven.
cards.tgt_text: If there be among you a poor man of one of thy brethren within any of thy gates in thy land which Yahuah Elohayka (the LORD thy God) giveth thee, thou shalt not harden thine heart, nor shut thine hand from thy poor brother:
cards.old_note: The Torah's command on generous alms-giving — the practice Yahusha (Jesus) is correcting the motive on, not the practice itself.
cards.note: Deuteronomy 15:7 — *If there be among you a poor man of one of thy brethren within any of thy gates in thy land which Yahuah Elohayka (the LORD thy God) giveth thee, thou shalt not harden thine heart, nor shut thine hand from thy poor brother:* *Take heed that you do not your alms before men, to be seen of them: otherwise you have no reward of your Father which is in heaven.* (Matthew 6:1) Giving to the poor brother is commanded here, with a warning not to *harden thine heart* or *shut thine hand*. So when Yahusha (Jesus) says to take heed how alms are given, he is not setting the giving aside. He is guarding the heart the commandment speaks to, so the gift is not turned into a show.
cards.prose: Giving to the poor brother is commanded here, with a warning not to *harden thine heart* or *shut thine hand*. So when Yahusha (Jesus) says to take heed how alms are given, he is not setting the giving aside. He is guarding the heart the commandment speaks to, so the gift is not turned into a show.
cards.member_note: Deuteronomy 15:7 — *thou shalt not harden thine heart, nor shut thine hand from thy poor brother.* The Torah commands an open hand to the poor brother and forbids a hardened heart.

cards.src_text: Take heed that you do not your alms before men, to be seen of them: otherwise you have no reward of your Father which is in heaven.
cards.tgt_text: And when ye reap the harvest of your land, thou shalt not wholly reap the corners of thy field, neither shalt thou gather the gleanings of thy harvest.
cards.old_note: The gleaning-rights of the poor — the Torah's social-economy in which alms-giving is embedded.
cards.note: Leviticus 19:9 — *And when ye reap the harvest of your land, thou shalt not wholly reap the corners of thy field, neither shalt thou gather the gleanings of thy harvest.* *Take heed that you do not your alms before men, to be seen of them: otherwise you have no reward of your Father which is in heaven.* (Matthew 6:1) Yahuah (the LORD) built provision for the poor into the edges of the field, the corners left unreaped and the gleanings left on the ground. Nobody sounded a trumpet for it, since the poor simply came and took what was left for them. That is the quiet, ordinary giving the verse has in mind.
cards.prose: Yahuah (the LORD) built provision for the poor into the edges of the field, the corners left unreaped and the gleanings left on the ground. Nobody sounded a trumpet for it, since the poor simply came and took what was left for them. That is the quiet, ordinary giving the verse has in mind.
cards.member_note: Leviticus 19:9 — *thou shalt not wholly reap the corners of thy field, neither shalt thou gather the gleanings of thy harvest.* The corners of the field and the gleanings were left standing for the poor as part of the harvest.

cards.src_text: Take heed that you do not your alms before men, to be seen of them: otherwise you have no reward of your Father which is in heaven.
cards.tgt_text: When thou cuttest down thine harvest in thy field, and hast forgot a sheaf in the field, thou shalt not go again to fetch it: it shall be for the stranger, for the fatherless, and for the widow: that Yahuah Elohayka (the LORD thy God) may bless thee in all the work of thine hands.
cards.old_note: The forgotten-sheaf law for the stranger, fatherless, and widow — Tanakh-substance of alms-giving.
cards.note: Deuteronomy 24:19 — *When thou cuttest down thine harvest in thy field, and hast forgot a sheaf in the field, thou shalt not go again to fetch it: it shall be for the stranger, for the fatherless, and for the widow: that Yahuah Elohayka (the LORD thy God) may bless thee in all the work of thine hands.* *Take heed that you do not your alms before men, to be seen of them: otherwise you have no reward of your Father which is in heaven.* (Matthew 6:1) A sheaf forgotten in the field is left where it lies, for the stranger, the fatherless and the widow, and the owner is told not to go back for it. Giving that nobody watches is already in the Torah, and the blessing named belongs to Yahuah (the LORD), not to onlookers.
