cards.src_text: Take heed that you do not your alms before men, to be seen of them: otherwise you have no reward of your Father which is in heaven.
cards.tgt_text: Blessed is he that considereth the poor: Yahuah (LORD) will deliver him in time of trouble.
cards.old_note: *Blessed is he that considereth the poor* — the wisdom-stream's alms-substance.
cards.note: Psalm 41:1 — *Blessed is he that considereth the poor: Yahuah (LORD) will deliver him in time of trouble.* *Take heed that you do not your alms before men, to be seen of them: otherwise you have no reward of your Father which is in heaven.* (Matthew 6:1) The blessing falls on the one who *considereth the poor*, and the deliverance in time of trouble comes from Yahuah (the LORD), not from men watching. That shows where the reward lies. A man who gives to be seen has traded the reward of the Father for a lesser one.

cards.member_note: Psalm 41:1 — *Blessed is he that considereth the poor: Yahuah (LORD) will deliver him in time of trouble.* Blessing and deliverance in trouble belong to the man who considers the poor.

cards.src_text: Take heed that you do not your alms before men, to be seen of them: otherwise you have no reward of your Father which is in heaven.
cards.tgt_text: Let your light so shine before men, that they may see your good works, and glorify your Father which is in heaven.
cards.old_note: *Let your light so shine before men, that they may see your good works, and glorify your Father* — the apparent-tension verse the framework resolves by motive-distinction.
cards.note: Matthew 5:16 — *Let your light so shine before men, that they may see your good works, and glorify your Father which is in heaven.* *Take heed that you do not your alms before men, to be seen of them: otherwise you have no reward of your Father which is in heaven.* (Matthew 6:1) Earlier in the sermon the light is to shine so that men see good works and glorify the Father, and here alms are not to be done *to be seen of them*. The two do not fight. In the first the glory goes to the Father, in the second it goes to the doer, and what settles it is who the seen thing points to.
cards.prose: Earlier in the sermon the light is to shine so that men see good works and glorify the Father, and here alms are not to be done *to be seen of them*. The two do not fight. In the first the glory goes to the Father, in the second it goes to the doer, and what settles it is who the seen thing points to.
cards.member_note: Matthew 5:16 — *Let your light so shine before men, that they may see your good works, and glorify your Father which is in heaven.* Good works are seen so that the Father is glorified, which is the opposite of giving to be seen.

cards.src_text: And when you prayest, you shall not be as the hypocrites are: for they love to pray standing in the synagogues and in the corners of the streets, that they may be seen of men. Verily I say unto you, They have their reward.
cards.tgt_text: And Solomon stood before the altar of Yahuah (LORD) in the presence of all the congregation of Yashar'el (Israel), and spread forth his hands toward heaven:
cards.old_note: Shlomo's (Solomon's) temple-dedication prayer — the Tanakh's longest public-prayer record, demonstrating that public prayer is not what Matt 6:5-6 prohibits.
cards.note: 1 Kings 8:22 — *And Solomon stood before the altar of Yahuah (LORD) in the presence of all the congregation of Yashar'el (Israel), and spread forth his hands toward heaven:* *And when you prayest, you shall not be as the hypocrites are: for they love to pray standing in the synagogues and in the corners of the streets, that they may be seen of men. Verily I say unto you, They have their reward.* (Matthew 6:5) Solomon prays in front of the whole congregation with his hands spread out, and the prayer is right. So the verse about the street corners is not against praying in the open. It is against praying in order to be seen, and the difference lies in who the praying is for.
cards.prose: Solomon prays in front of the whole congregation with his hands spread out, and the prayer is right. So the verse about the street corners is not against praying in the open. It is against praying in order to be seen, and the difference lies in who the praying is for.
cards.member_note: 1 Kings 8:22 — *in the presence of all the congregation of Yashar'el (Israel), and spread forth his hands toward heaven.* Solomon prayed openly before the whole congregation at the altar, so public prayer is not what is forbidden.

cards.src_text: And when you prayest, you shall not be as the hypocrites are: for they love to pray standing in the synagogues and in the corners of the streets, that they may be seen of men. Verily I say unto you, They have their reward.
cards.tgt_text: These all continued with one accord in prayer and supplication, with the women, and Mary the mother of Yahusha (Jesus), and with his brethren.
cards.old_note: The apostolic-community gathered prayer — the New Testament's pattern of corporate prayer in the disciples Yahusha (Jesus) is now teaching.
cards.note: Acts 1:14 — *These all continued with one accord in prayer and supplication, with the women, and Mary the mother of Yahusha (Jesus), and with his brethren.* *And when you prayest, you shall not be as the hypocrites are: for they love to pray standing in the synagogues and in the corners of the streets, that they may be seen of men. Verily I say unto you, They have their reward.* (Matthew 6:5) The same men who were taught to pray in secret later continued *with one accord* in prayer together, with the women and the family of Yahusha (Jesus). The shut door is about the heart, not a ban on praying with others, and here the company is joined in a single purpose before the Father.
cards.prose: The same men who were taught to pray in secret later continued *with one accord* in prayer together, with the women and the family of Yahusha (Jesus). The shut door is about the heart, not a ban on praying with others, and here the company is joined in a single purpose before the Father.
cards.member_note: Acts 1:14 — *These all continued with one accord in prayer and supplication, with the women, and Mary the mother of Yahusha (Jesus), and with his brethren.* The disciples continued together in prayer and supplication with one accord, so praying with others is not ruled out.

cards.src_text: And when you prayest, you shall not be as the hypocrites are: for they love to pray standing in the synagogues and in the corners of the streets, that they may be seen of men. Verily I say unto you, They have their reward.
cards.tgt_text: And they continued stedfastly in the apostles’ doctrine and fellowship, and in breaking of bread, and in prayers.
cards.old_note: *They continued stedfastly in the apostles' doctrine and fellowship, and in breaking of bread, and in prayers* — the gathered prayer as a defining mark of the early assembly.
cards.note: Acts 2:42 — *And they continued stedfastly in the apostles’ doctrine and fellowship, and in breaking of bread, and in prayers.* *And when you prayest, you shall not be as the hypocrites are: for they love to pray standing in the synagogues and in the corners of the streets, that they may be seen of men. Verily I say unto you, They have their reward.* (Matthew 6:5) Prayers stand here beside the teaching, the fellowship and the breaking of bread as part of how that company lived. Yahusha (Jesus) is not ruling out shared prayer. He is dealing with why a man prays before others, whether it is for them or for the Father.
cards.prose: Prayers stand here beside the teaching, the fellowship and the breaking of bread as part of how that company lived. Yahusha (Jesus) is not ruling out shared prayer. He is dealing with why a man prays before others, whether it is for them or for the Father.
cards.member_note: Acts 2:42 — *And they continued stedfastly in the apostles’ doctrine and fellowship, and in breaking of bread, and in prayers.* Prayers were one of the things the first company held to steadily, along with teaching, fellowship and bread.

cards.src_text: And when you prayest, you shall not be as the hypocrites are: for they love to pray standing in the synagogues and in the corners of the streets, that they may be seen of men. Verily I say unto you, They have their reward.
cards.tgt_text: And when they heard that, they lifted up their voice to Elohim (God) with one accord, and said, Yahuah (Lord), thou art Elohim (God), which hast made heaven, and earth, and the sea, and all that in them is:
cards.old_note: The first assembly's gathered prayer at the release of Kepha (Peter) and Yochanan (John).
cards.note: Acts 4:24 — *And when they heard that, they lifted up their voice to Elohim (God) with one accord, and said, Yahuah (Lord), thou art Elohim (God), which hast made heaven, and earth, and the sea, and all that in them is:* *And when you prayest, you shall not be as the hypocrites are: for they love to pray standing in the synagogues and in the corners of the streets, that they may be seen of men. Verily I say unto you, They have their reward.* (Matthew 6:5) When they lifted up their voice together, what they said was spoken to the Maker of heaven, earth and sea, and nothing in it was aimed at listeners. A company can pray aloud without performing, and that was the very thing the hypocrites on the street corners had lost.
cards.prose: When they lifted up their voice together, what they said was spoken to the Maker of heaven, earth and sea, and nothing in it was aimed at listeners. A company can pray aloud without performing, and that was the very thing the hypocrites on the street corners had lost.
cards.member_note: Acts 4:24 — *they lifted up their voice to Elohim (God) with one accord, and said.* The company raised their voice together to the one who made heaven, earth and sea.

cards.src_text: And when you prayest, you shall not be as the hypocrites are: for they love to pray standing in the synagogues and in the corners of the streets, that they may be seen of men. Verily I say unto you, They have their reward.
cards.tgt_text: Then they took away the stone from the place where the dead was laid. And Yahusha (Jesus) lifted up his eyes, and said, Father, I thank thee that thou hast heard me.
cards.old_note: Yahusha's (Jesus's) own public prayer at the raising of El'azar (Lazarus) — *I said it, that they may believe that thou hast sent me* — naming the public posture explicitly.
cards.note: John 11:41 — *Then they took away the stone from the place where the dead was laid. And Yahusha (Jesus) lifted up his eyes, and said, Father, I thank thee that thou hast heard me.* *And when you prayest, you shall not be as the hypocrites are: for they love to pray standing in the synagogues and in the corners of the streets, that they may be seen of men. Verily I say unto you, They have their reward.* (Matthew 6:5) Yahusha (Jesus) prays aloud with a crowd around him, thanking the Father who had heard him, and then says why: *that they may believe that thou hast sent me* (John 11:42). His prayer is spoken to the Father first and heard by others second, which is the order the verse about the street corners turns on.
cards.prose: Yahusha (Jesus) prays aloud with a crowd around him, thanking the Father who had heard him, and then says why: *that they may believe that thou hast sent me* (John 11:42). His prayer is spoken to the Father first and heard by others second, which is the order the verse about the street corners turns on.
cards.member_note: John 11:41 — *Yahusha (Jesus) lifted up his eyes, and said, Father, I thank thee that thou hast heard me.* Yahusha (Jesus) prayed aloud before the crowd, speaking to the Father who had heard him.

cards.src_text: And when you prayest, you shall not be as the hypocrites are: for they love to pray standing in the synagogues and in the corners of the streets, that they may be seen of men. Verily I say unto you, They have their reward.
cards.tgt_text: O Yahuah (LORD), thou hast searched me, and known me.
cards.old_note: *Thou understandest my thought afar off ... there is not a word in my tongue, but, lo, O Yahuah (LORD), thou knowest it altogether* — the Father-knows-before-the-asking Tanakh substance the lock at Matt 6:8 rests on.
cards.note: Psalm 139:1 — *O Yahuah (LORD), thou hast searched me, and known me.* *And when you prayest, you shall not be as the hypocrites are: for they love to pray standing in the synagogues and in the corners of the streets, that they may be seen of men. Verily I say unto you, They have their reward.* (Matthew 6:5) A man who knows he is already searched and known has no one to impress. The psalm goes on, *there is not a word in my tongue, but, lo, O Yahuah (LORD), thou knowest it altogether* (Psalm 139:4), and that is why a prayer needs neither an audience nor padding.
cards.prose: A man who knows he is already searched and known has no one to impress. The psalm goes on, *there is not a word in my tongue, but, lo, O Yahuah (LORD), thou knowest it altogether* (Psalm 139:4), and that is why a prayer needs neither an audience nor padding.
cards.member_note: Psalm 139:1 — *O Yahuah (LORD), thou hast searched me, and known me.* Yahuah (the LORD) has searched and known the one who prays, so there is nothing to show him.

cards.src_text: After this manner therefore pray you: Our Father which art in heaven, Hallowed be your name.
cards.tgt_text: Do ye thus requite Yahuah (LORD), O foolish people and unwise? is not he thy father that hath bought thee? hath he not made thee, and established thee?
cards.old_note: *Is not he thy Father that hath bought thee?* — third Tanakh-Father-address anchor.
cards.note: Deuteronomy 32:6 — *Do ye thus requite Yahuah (LORD), O foolish people and unwise? is not he thy father that hath bought thee? hath he not made thee, and established thee?* *After this manner therefore pray you: Our Father which art in heaven, Hallowed be your name.* (Matthew 6:9) Moses reminds the people that the one they have been treating so badly is their father, who bought them, made them and established them. So when Yahusha (Jesus) teaches them to say Our Father, he is not bringing in a new name for the Maker. Yashar'el (Israel) was already told he is their father, and told it as a rebuke.

cards.src_text: Give us this day our daily bread.
cards.tgt_text: Then said Yahuah (LORD) unto Moses, Behold, I will rain bread from heaven for you; and the people shall go out and gather a certain rate every day, that I may prove them, whether they will walk in my law, or no.
cards.old_note: The manna-pattern — *that I may prove them, whether they will walk in my law, or no* — the daily-bread Tanakh-substance.
cards.note: Exodus 16:4 — *Then said Yahuah (LORD) unto Moses, Behold, I will rain bread from heaven for you; and the people shall go out and gather a certain rate every day, that I may prove them, whether they will walk in my law, or no.* *Give us this day our daily bread.* (Matthew 6:11) The bread asked for this day is the bread Yahuah (the LORD) rained from heaven, gathered a day at a time. He gave it to prove whether the people would walk in his law, so the daily bread in the prayer comes with the Father's instruction attached and not apart from it.

cards.src_text: Give us this day our daily bread.
cards.tgt_text: Remove far from me vanity and lies: give me neither poverty nor riches; feed me with food convenient for me:
cards.old_note: *Give me neither poverty nor riches; feed me with food convenient for me* — the wisdom-stream's daily-bread petition.
cards.note: Proverbs 30:8 — *Remove far from me vanity and lies: give me neither poverty nor riches; feed me with food convenient for me:* *Give us this day our daily bread.* (Matthew 6:11) A man here asks for neither poverty nor riches, only the food fitting for him. That is the size of what the prayer asks for, bread for the day and no more, put in the same plain terms by someone who wanted to be kept from both extremes.

cards.src_text: Give us this day our daily bread.
cards.tgt_text: But he answered and said, It is written, Man shall not live by bread alone, but by every word that proceedeth out of the mouth of Elohim (God).
cards.old_note: *Man shall not live by bread alone, but by every word that proceedeth out of the mouth of Elohim (God)* — Yahusha's (Jesus's) wilderness-citation of Deuteronomy 8:3; the daily-bread carries both physical and Torah-bread registers.
cards.note: Matthew 4:4 — *But he answered and said, It is written, Man shall not live by bread alone, but by every word that proceedeth out of the mouth of Elohim (God).* *Give us this day our daily bread.* (Matthew 6:11) Yahusha (Jesus) answered the tempter with these words in the wilderness, so he knows what bread is for. The prayer asks for bread, and the answer he gave says a man needs more than bread: the word that comes out of the mouth of Elohim (God). The two belong together in one request.

cards.src_text: And lead us not into temptation, but deliver us from evil: For yours is the kingdom, and the power, and the glory, for ever. Amen.
cards.tgt_text: Then was Yahusha (Jesus) led up of the Spirit into the wilderness to be tempted of the devil.
cards.old_note: The wilderness-temptation Yahusha (Jesus) just walked — the petition is for the Father's protective leading the disciples will need as they walk what their Master walked.
cards.note: Matthew 4:1 — *Then was Yahusha (Jesus) led up of the Spirit into the wilderness to be tempted of the devil.* *And lead us not into temptation, but deliver us from evil: For yours is the kingdom, and the power, and the glory, for ever. Amen.* (Matthew 6:13) The one teaching the prayer had just been led into the wilderness and tempted, so he is not speaking of something far from himself. He was led there by the Ruach HaKodesh (Holy Spirit) and still came through, which is what the petition asks of the Father for his disciples: to be brought through and delivered from evil.

cards.tgt_text: There hath no temptation taken you but such as is common to man: but Elohim (God) is faithful, who will not suffer you to be tempted above that ye are able; but will with the temptation also make a way to escape, that ye may be able to bear it.
cards.old_note: *Elohim (God) is faithful, who will not suffer you to be tempted above that ye are able* — the apostolic confirmation of the petition's substance.
cards.note: 1 Corinthians 10:13 — *There hath no temptation taken you but such as is common to man: but Elohim (God) is faithful, who will not suffer you to be tempted above that ye are able; but will with the temptation also make a way to escape, that ye may be able to bear it.* *And lead us not into temptation, but deliver us from evil: For yours is the kingdom, and the power, and the glory, for ever. Amen.* (Matthew 6:13) Here is the answer to what the petition asks: the Father is faithful, and he does not let temptation press past what a man can bear but makes a way out beside it. The prayer asks to be delivered from evil, and this verse says what deliverance looks like in the middle of the trial.

cards.src_text: And lead us not into temptation, but deliver us from evil: For yours is the kingdom, and the power, and the glory, for ever. Amen.
cards.tgt_text: Let no man say when he is tempted, I am tempted of Elohim (God): for Elohim (God) cannot be tempted with evil, neither tempteth he any man:
cards.old_note: *Elohim (God) cannot be tempted with evil, neither tempteth he any man* — the apostolic clarification that the petition is not about *do not cause us to be tempted.*
cards.note: James 1:13 — *Let no man say when he is tempted, I am tempted of Elohim (God): for Elohim (God) cannot be tempted with evil, neither tempteth he any man:* *And lead us not into temptation, but deliver us from evil: For yours is the kingdom, and the power, and the glory, for ever. Amen.* (Matthew 6:13) James shuts off a wrong reading of the petition. Asking not to be led into temptation does not mean the Father tempts anyone, since he cannot be tempted with evil and tempts no man. The prayer asks him to keep his children clear of the temptation that comes from elsewhere.

cards.src_text: Moreover when you fast, be not, as the hypocrites, of a sad countenance: for they disfigure their faces, that they may appear unto men to fast. Verily I say unto you, They have their reward.
cards.tgt_text: Also on the tenth day of this seventh month there shall be a day of atonement: it shall be an holy convocation unto you; and ye shall afflict your souls, and offer an offering made by fire unto Yahuah (LORD).
cards.old_note: The Yom Kippur fast — *ye shall afflict your souls* — the Torah's central fast-command.
cards.note: Leviticus 23:27 — *Also on the tenth day of this seventh month there shall be a day of atonement: it shall be an holy convocation unto you; and ye shall afflict your souls, and offer an offering made by fire unto Yahuah (LORD).* *Moreover when you fast, be not, as the hypocrites, of a sad countenance: for they disfigure their faces, that they may appear unto men to fast. Verily I say unto you, They have their reward.* (Matthew 6:16) The Torah itself commands a day when the people afflict their souls, so fasting is not something Yahusha (Jesus) invents or sets aside. What he corrects is the sad face worn for others to see. A commanded fast is kept before Yahuah (the LORD), and putting on a look for men makes it theirs.

cards.tgt_text: Sanctify ye a fast, call a solemn assembly, gather the elders and all the inhabitants of the land into the house of Yahuah Elohaychem (the LORD your God), and cry unto Yahuah (LORD),
cards.old_note: The prophet's call for a national fast — *sanctify ye a fast, call a solemn assembly* — Tanakh-substance of corporate fasting.
cards.note: Joel 1:14 — *Sanctify ye a fast, call a solemn assembly, gather the elders and all the inhabitants of the land into the house of Yahuah Elohaychem (the LORD your God), and cry unto Yahuah (LORD),* *Moreover when you fast, be not, as the hypocrites, of a sad countenance: for they disfigure their faces, that they may appear unto men to fast. Verily I say unto you, They have their reward.* (Matthew 6:16) The prophet calls the elders and all the people of the land together to sanctify a fast and cry out to Yahuah (the LORD). A fast kept openly by the whole land is right when it is held for him. So the Father who sees in secret is not against fasting together, only against the face put on for onlookers.

cards.src_text: But lay up for yourselves treasures in heaven, where neither moth nor rust does corrupt, and where thieves do not break through nor steal:
cards.tgt_text: Riches profit not in the day of wrath: but righteousness delivereth from death.
cards.old_note: *Riches profit not in the day of wrath: but righteousness delivereth from death* — the wisdom-stream futility-of-earth-treasure.
cards.note: Proverbs 11:4 — *Riches profit not in the day of wrath: but righteousness delivereth from death.* *But lay up for yourselves treasures in heaven, where neither moth nor rust does corrupt, and where thieves do not break through nor steal:* (Matthew 6:20) Riches do not help on the day of wrath, and righteousness does. That is the reason to lay up treasure where moth, rust and thieves cannot reach it: a day comes when only what was laid up in righteousness is of any use.

cards.tgt_text: Labour not to be rich: cease from thine own wisdom.
cards.old_note: *Riches certainly make themselves wings; they fly away as an eagle toward heaven* — second wisdom-stream witness.
cards.note: Proverbs 23:4 — *Labour not to be rich: cease from thine own wisdom.* *But lay up for yourselves treasures in heaven, where neither moth nor rust does corrupt, and where thieves do not break through nor steal:* (Matthew 6:20) The wise man says not to wear yourself out to get rich, and gives the reason in the next line: *riches certainly make themselves wings; they fly away as an eagle toward heaven* (Proverbs 23:5). Treasure on earth leaves on its own, which is why moth, rust and thieves are named in the verse.

cards.src_text: But lay up for yourselves treasures in heaven, where neither moth nor rust does corrupt, and where thieves do not break through nor steal:
cards.tgt_text: Be not thou afraid when one is made rich, when the glory of his house is increased;
cards.old_note: The futility-of-riches psalm — *when he dieth he shall carry nothing away.*
cards.note: Psalm 49:16 — *Be not thou afraid when one is made rich, when the glory of his house is increased;* *But lay up for yourselves treasures in heaven, where neither moth nor rust does corrupt, and where thieves do not break through nor steal:* (Matthew 6:20) The psalmist tells his hearer not to be afraid when another grows rich, and says why: *when he dieth he shall carry nothing away* (Psalm 49:17), and his glory does not follow him down. What a man stores here stays here, so the verse sends the treasure to the one place that does not decay.

cards.src_text: But lay up for yourselves treasures in heaven, where neither moth nor rust does corrupt, and where thieves do not break through nor steal:
cards.tgt_text: Sell that ye have, and give alms; provide yourselves bags which wax not old, a treasure in the heavens that faileth not, where no thief approacheth, neither moth corrupteth.
cards.old_note: The Lukan parallel of Matt 6:19-21 — *provide yourselves bags which wax not old, a treasure in the heavens that faileth not.*
cards.note: Luke 12:33 — *Sell that ye have, and give alms; provide yourselves bags which wax not old, a treasure in the heavens that faileth not, where no thief approacheth, neither moth corrupteth.* *But lay up for yourselves treasures in heaven, where neither moth nor rust does corrupt, and where thieves do not break through nor steal:* (Matthew 6:20) Luke carries the same teaching and says how the treasure is laid up: by selling and giving alms. The treasure in heaven is made out of open-handed giving to the poor, the very command the first verses of this chapter were guarding, so the alms and the treasure are one subject.

cards.src_text: No man can serve two masters: for either he will hate the one, and love the other; or else he will hold to the one, and despise the other. You cannot serve Elohim (God) and mammon.
cards.tgt_text: Thou shalt have no other gods before me.
cards.old_note: *Thou shalt have no other gods before me* — the first commandment ruling out competing masters categorically.
cards.note: Exodus 20:3 — *Thou shalt have no other gods before me.* *No man can serve two masters: for either he will hate the one, and love the other; or else he will hold to the one, and despise the other. You cannot serve Elohim (God) and mammon.* (Matthew 6:24) The first of the ten words already says there is no room for a second master. When Yahusha (Jesus) puts mammon beside Elohim (God) as a rival to be served, he is saying money can become the other god, and the commandment stands against it as it stood against the gods of the nations.

cards.note: Deuteronomy 6:4 — *Hear, O Yashar'el (Israel): Yahuah Eloheinu (The LORD our God) is one Yahuah (LORD):* *No man can serve two masters: for either he will hate the one, and love the other; or else he will hold to the one, and despise the other. cards.tgt_text: And Elijah came unto all the people, and said, How long halt ye between two opinions? if Yahuah (LORD) be Elohim (God), follow him: but if Baal, then follow him. And the people answered him not a word.

cards.src_text: The light of the body is the eye: if therefore your eye be single, your whole body shall be full of light.
cards.tgt_text: He that hath a bountiful eye shall be blessed; for he giveth of his bread to the poor.
cards.old_note: *He that hath a bountiful eye (tov-ayin) shall be blessed; for he giveth of his bread to the poor* — the Hebrew-idiom anchor; good-eye = generous heart.
cards.note: Proverbs 22:9 — *He that hath a bountiful eye shall be blessed; for he giveth of his bread to the poor.* *The light of the body is the eye: if therefore your eye be single, your whole body shall be full of light.* (Matthew 6:22) The proverb shows what a good eye is: the man with a bountiful eye gives of his bread to the poor. So when the verse says the body is full of light if the eye is single, it is speaking of an open-handed heart and not of eyesight.

cards.tgt_text: Eat thou not the bread of him that hath an evil eye, neither desire thou his dainty meats:
cards.old_note: *Eat thou not the bread of him that hath an evil eye (ra-ayin)* — the contrasting idiom; evil-eye = stingy/grasping heart.
cards.note: Proverbs 23:6 — *Eat thou not the bread of him that hath an evil eye, neither desire thou his dainty meats:* *The light of the body is the eye: if therefore your eye be single, your whole body shall be full of light.* (Matthew 6:22) The proverb's evil eye belongs to a grudging man who sets out food while *his heart is not with thee* (Proverbs 23:7). That is the eye behind the body full of darkness in the verse: a stingy, grasping heart and not a failing of sight.

cards.src_text: The light of the body is the eye: if therefore your eye be single, your whole body shall be full of light.
cards.tgt_text: Beware that there be not a thought in thy wicked heart, saying, The seventh year, the year of release, is at hand; and thine eye be evil against thy poor brother, and thou givest him nought; and he cry unto Yahuah (LORD) against thee, and it be sin unto thee.
cards.old_note: *Thine eye be evil against thy poor brother* — the same evil-eye idiom in Torah-context, naming the stinginess-toward-the-poor that the Torah forbids; locks the Hebrew-idiom reading of Matt 6:22-23.
cards.note: Deuteronomy 15:9 — *Beware that there be not a thought in thy wicked heart, saying, The seventh year, the year of release, is at hand; and thine eye be evil against thy poor brother, and thou givest him nought; and he cry unto Yahuah (LORD) against thee, and it be sin unto thee.* *The light of the body is the eye: if therefore your eye be single, your whole body shall be full of light.* (Matthew 6:22) Moses uses the evil eye in a command about the poor: do not count down to the year of release and give nothing, or he cries to Yahuah (the LORD) against you and it is sin. The same Torah that commands the open hand names the closed eye as sin, and the single eye is the one that obeys.
cards.prose: Moses uses the evil eye in a command about the poor: do not count down to the year of release and give nothing, or he cries to Yahuah (the LORD) against you and it is sin. The same Torah that commands the open hand names the closed eye as sin, and the single eye is the one that obeys.
cards.member_note: Deuteronomy 15:9 — *and thine eye be evil against thy poor brother, and thou givest him nought; and he cry unto Yahuah (LORD) against thee, and it be sin unto thee.* An eye evil against a poor brother who is given nothing is sin in the Torah.

cards.src_text: The light of the body is the eye: if therefore your eye be single, your whole body shall be full of light.
cards.tgt_text: He that hasteth to be rich hath an evil eye, and considereth not that poverty shall come upon him.
cards.old_note: *He that hasteth to be rich hath an evil eye* — fourth wisdom-stream witness of the evil-eye = stingy-heart idiom.
cards.note: Proverbs 28:22 — *He that hasteth to be rich hath an evil eye, and considereth not that poverty shall come upon him.* *The light of the body is the eye: if therefore your eye be single, your whole body shall be full of light.* (Matthew 6:22) Here the evil eye belongs to the man in a hurry to be rich, who does not see that poverty is coming for him. A greedy eye chasing money leaves the body dark, which is the opposite of the single eye that sees the poor and gives, and the proverb ends with the loss he cannot see.
cards.prose: Here the evil eye belongs to the man in a hurry to be rich, who does not see that poverty is coming for him. A greedy eye chasing money leaves the body dark, which is the opposite of the single eye that sees the poor and gives, and the proverb ends with the loss he cannot see.
cards.member_note: Proverbs 28:22 — *He that hasteth to be rich hath an evil eye, and considereth not that poverty shall come upon him.* The man in haste to be rich has an evil eye and does not see that poverty is coming.

cards.src_text: Behold the fowls of the air: for they sow not, neither do they reap, nor gather into barns; yet your heavenly Father feedeth them. Are you not much better than they?
cards.tgt_text: He giveth to the beast his food, and to the young ravens which cry.
cards.old_note: *He giveth to the beast his food, and to the young ravens which cry* — the Father's covenant-care for the creatures.
cards.note: Psalm 147:9 — *He giveth to the beast his food, and to the young ravens which cry.* *Behold the fowls of the air: for they sow not, neither do they reap, nor gather into barns; yet your heavenly Father feedeth them. Are you not much better than they?* (Matthew 6:26) Yahuah (the LORD) gives the beast its food, and even the young ravens that cry. The birds in the verse are not a sentimental picture. They are his own care, already sung in the psalms, and the man asked to look at them is asked to look at what the psalmist had praised.
cards.prose: Yahuah (the LORD) gives the beast its food, and even the young ravens that cry. The birds in the verse are not a sentimental picture. They are his own care, already sung in the psalms, and the man asked to look at them is asked to look at what the psalmist had praised.
cards.member_note: Psalm 147:9 — *He giveth to the beast his food, and to the young ravens which cry.* Yahuah (the LORD) gives food to the beast and to the young ravens that cry.

cards.src_text: Behold the fowls of the air: for they sow not, neither do they reap, nor gather into barns; yet your heavenly Father feedeth them. Are you not much better than they?
cards.tgt_text: Where wast thou when I laid the foundations of the earth? declare, if thou hast understanding.
cards.old_note: The creation-care testimony from the whirlwind — the architectural-witness to the Father's sustaining of every creature.
cards.note: Job 38:4 — *Where wast thou when I laid the foundations of the earth? declare, if thou hast understanding.* *Behold the fowls of the air: for they sow not, neither do they reap, nor gather into barns; yet your heavenly Father feedeth them. Are you not much better than they?* (Matthew 6:26) Yahuah (the LORD) answers Job out of the whirlwind by asking where he was when the earth was laid. The one who set the foundations in place is the one the verse says feeds the fowls, so a man's worry about his food is held up against the size of the one who cares.
cards.prose: Yahuah (the LORD) answers Job out of the whirlwind by asking where he was when the earth was laid. The one who set the foundations in place is the one the verse says feeds the fowls, so a man's worry about his food is held up against the size of the one who cares.
cards.member_note: Job 38:4 — *Where wast thou when I laid the foundations of the earth? declare, if thou hast understanding.* Yahuah (the LORD) asks Job where he was when the foundations of the earth were laid, and shows whose hands hold creation.

cards.src_text: Behold the fowls of the air: for they sow not, neither do they reap, nor gather into barns; yet your heavenly Father feedeth them. Are you not much better than they?
cards.tgt_text: He sendeth the springs into the valleys, which run among the hills.
cards.old_note: The comprehensive creation-care psalm — *He causeth the grass to grow for the cattle.*
cards.note: Psalm 104:10 — *He sendeth the springs into the valleys, which run among the hills.* *Behold the fowls of the air: for they sow not, neither do they reap, nor gather into barns; yet your heavenly Father feedeth them. Are you not much better than they?* (Matthew 6:26) The psalm shows how wide his feeding goes: he sends springs into the valleys and makes grass grow on the mountains, so the creatures are fed by a whole arrangement he made and keeps. If he supplies water and grass for them, the man who looks to him for food is not forgotten.
cards.prose: The psalm shows how wide his feeding goes: he sends springs into the valleys and makes grass grow on the mountains, so the creatures are fed by a whole arrangement he made and keeps. If he supplies water and grass for them, the man who looks to him for food is not forgotten.
cards.member_note: Psalm 104:10 — *He sendeth the springs into the valleys, which run among the hills.* The springs sent into the valleys show the Father's provision reaching every creature, which the birds stand for.

cards.src_text: But seek you first the kingdom of Elohim (God), and his righteousness; and all these things shall be added unto you.
cards.tgt_text: And Elohim (God) said unto him, Because thou hast asked this thing, and hast not asked for thyself long life; neither hast asked riches for thyself, nor hast asked the life of thine enemies; but hast asked for thyself understanding to discern judgment;
cards.old_note: Shlomo's (Solomon's) Gibeon-dream — he asked for wisdom rather than wealth, and Yahuah (the LORD) added the wealth; the Tanakh-pattern of *seek first the kingdom, and these things shall be added.*
cards.note: 1 Kings 3:11 — *And Elohim (God) said unto him, Because thou hast asked this thing, and hast not asked for thyself long life; neither hast asked riches for thyself, nor hast asked the life of thine enemies; but hast asked for thyself understanding to discern judgment;* *But seek you first the kingdom of Elohim (God), and his righteousness; and all these things shall be added unto you.* (Matthew 6:33) Solomon asked for an understanding heart and not for long life or riches, and Elohim (God) was pleased and then gave him the riches he did not ask for as well. That is seeking first and having it added: the thing sought was right judgment, and the rest came on top of it.
cards.prose: Solomon asked for an understanding heart and not for long life or riches, and Elohim (God) was pleased and then gave him the riches he did not ask for as well. That is seeking first and having it added: the thing sought was right judgment, and the rest came on top of it.
cards.member_note: 1 Kings 3:11 — *Because thou hast asked this thing, and hast not asked for thyself long life; neither hast asked riches for thyself.* Solomon asked for understanding and not for riches, and the riches were given to him as well.

cards.src_text: But seek you first the kingdom of Elohim (God), and his righteousness; and all these things shall be added unto you.
cards.tgt_text: Delight thyself also in Yahuah (LORD); and he shall give thee the desires of thine heart.
cards.old_note: *Delight thyself also in Yahuah (the LORD); and he shall give thee the desires of thine heart* — the priority-orientation pattern.
cards.note: Psalm 37:4 — *Delight thyself also in Yahuah (LORD); and he shall give thee the desires of thine heart.* *But seek you first the kingdom of Elohim (God), and his righteousness; and all these things shall be added unto you.* (Matthew 6:33) Delight set on Yahuah (the LORD) comes first in the psalm, and what the heart wants follows. It has the same order as the verse: the kingdom and righteousness first, then the things a man would otherwise worry about added to him. The giving rests on where the delight is placed.
cards.prose: Delight set on Yahuah (the LORD) comes first in the psalm, and what the heart wants follows. It has the same order as the verse: the kingdom and righteousness first, then the things a man would otherwise worry about added to him. The giving rests on where the delight is placed.
cards.member_note: Psalm 37:4 — *Delight thyself also in Yahuah (LORD); and he shall give thee the desires of thine heart.* Delight in Yahuah (the LORD) comes first, and he gives the desires of the heart after it.

cards.src_text: But seek you first the kingdom of Elohim (God), and his righteousness; and all these things shall be added unto you.
cards.tgt_text: Blessed are they which do hunger and thirst after righteousness: for they shall be filled.
cards.old_note: *Blessed are they which do hunger and thirst after righteousness: for they shall be filled* — the Beatitude that Matt 6:33 names in practice.
cards.note: Matthew 5:6 — *Blessed are they which do hunger and thirst after righteousness: for they shall be filled.* *But seek you first the kingdom of Elohim (God), and his righteousness; and all these things shall be added unto you.* (Matthew 6:33) The man who hungers and thirsts after righteousness is told he will be filled, and the verse in this chapter tells the anxious man to seek the kingdom and his righteousness first. The hunger that is blessed is the same seeking, turned from worry over food and clothes to the thing that fills.
cards.prose: The man who hungers and thirsts after righteousness is told he will be filled, and the verse in this chapter tells the anxious man to seek the kingdom and his righteousness first. The hunger that is blessed is the same seeking, turned from worry over food and clothes to the thing that fills.
cards.member_note: Matthew 5:6 — *Blessed are they which do hunger and thirst after righteousness: for they shall be filled.* Those who hunger and thirst after righteousness are blessed and will be filled, which is the seeking of the kingdom first.

cards.src_text: Judge not, that you be not judged.
cards.tgt_text: Judge not according to the appearance, but judge righteous judgment.
cards.old_note: *Judge not according to the appearance, but judge righteous judgment* — Yahusha's (Jesus's) explicit reframing that locks Matt 7:1 as a kind-of-judgment-correction, not abolition of judgment.
cards.note: John 7:24 — *Judge not according to the appearance, but judge righteous judgment.* *Judge not, that you be not judged.* (Matthew 7:1) Yahusha (Jesus) is not shutting the door on judgment here, because in Jerusalem he himself tells the crowd to *judge righteous judgment*. What he turns away in the Sermon is the crooked scale that weighs a man by how he looks, so the two sayings stand together and tell the hypocrite from the honest judge.
cards.prose: Yahusha (Jesus) is not shutting the door on judgment here, because in Jerusalem he himself tells the crowd to *judge righteous judgment*. What he turns away in the Sermon is the crooked scale that weighs a man by how he looks, so the two sayings stand together and tell the hypocrite from the honest judge.
cards.member_note: John 7:24 — *Judge not according to the appearance, but judge righteous judgment.* Yahusha (Jesus) names the judging he forbids, which goes by appearance, and commands the righteous judgment that the Torah asks for.

cards.src_text: Give not that which is holy unto the dogs, neither cast you your pearls before swine, lest they trample them under their feet, and turn again and rend you.
cards.tgt_text: And whosoever shall not receive you, nor hear your words, when ye depart out of that house or city, shake off the dust of your feet.
cards.old_note: *Whosoever shall not receive you, nor hear your words, when ye depart out of that house or city, shake off the dust of your feet* — Yahusha's (Jesus's) instruction to the disciples on the same discrimination-of-audience pattern.
cards.note: Matthew 10:14 — *And whosoever shall not receive you, nor hear your words, when ye depart out of that house or city, shake off the dust of your feet.* *Give not that which is holy unto the dogs, neither cast you your pearls before swine, lest they trample them under their feet, and turn again and rend you.* (Matthew 7:6) When Yahusha (Jesus) sends his disciples out, the same line is drawn from the other side. The word goes to whoever will hear it, and where a house or city will not receive it, they *shake off the dust of your feet* and the proclamation stops there. That is the pearl left where it was refused.
cards.prose: When Yahusha (Jesus) sends his disciples out, the same line is drawn from the other side. The word goes to whoever will hear it, and where a house or city will not receive it, they *shake off the dust of your feet* and the proclamation stops there. That is the pearl left where it was refused.
cards.member_note: Matthew 10:14 — *whosoever shall not receive you, nor hear your words.* Where the word is not received or heard, Yahusha (Jesus) tells his disciples to leave that place and shake off the dust.

cards.src_text: If you then, being evil, know how to give good gifts unto your children, how much more shall your Father which is in heaven give good things to them that ask him?
cards.tgt_text: If ye then, being evil, know how to give good gifts unto your children: how much more shall your heavenly Father give the Ruach HaKodesh (Holy Spirit) to them that ask him?
cards.old_note: *How much more shall your heavenly Father give the Holy Spirit to them that ask him?* — Lukan parallel; specifies *good things* as the Ruach HaKodesh (Holy Spirit).
cards.note: Luke 11:13 — *If ye then, being evil, know how to give good gifts unto your children: how much more shall your heavenly Father give the Ruach HaKodesh (Holy Spirit) to them that ask him?* *If you then, being evil, know how to give good gifts unto your children, how much more shall your Father which is in heaven give good things to them that ask him?* (Matthew 7:11) Matthew leaves the good things the Father gives unnamed, and Luke fills them in. The Father who is asked gives the Ruach HaKodesh (Holy Spirit), so the good gift is the Spirit himself, given to the child who asks.
cards.prose: Matthew leaves the good things the Father gives unnamed, and Luke fills them in. The Father who is asked gives the Ruach HaKodesh (Holy Spirit), so the good gift is the Spirit himself, given to the child who asks.
cards.member_note: Luke 11:13 — *how much more shall your heavenly Father give the Ruach HaKodesh (Holy Spirit) to them that ask him.* Luke names the good thing the Father gives to those who ask: the Ruach HaKodesh (Holy Spirit).

cards.src_text: If you then, being evil, know how to give good gifts unto your children, how much more shall your Father which is in heaven give good things to them that ask him?
cards.tgt_text: But this shall be the covenant that I will make with the house of Yashar'el (Israel); After those days, saith Yahuah (LORD), I will put my law in their inward parts, and write it in their hearts; and will be their Elohim (God), and they shall be my people.
cards.old_note: *I will put my law in their inward parts, and write it in their hearts* — the new-heart promise the Spirit-gift enables.
cards.note: Jeremiah 31:33 — *But this shall be the covenant that I will make with the house of Yashar'el (Israel); After those days, saith Yahuah (LORD), I will put my law in their inward parts, and write it in their hearts; and will be their Elohim (God), and they shall be my people.* *If you then, being evil, know how to give good gifts unto your children, how much more shall your Father which is in heaven give good things to them that ask him?* (Matthew 7:11) The good things the Father gives reach down to what Yahuah (the LORD) promised the house of Yashar'el (Israel) through Jeremiah, his *law* set in their inward parts and written in their hearts. The asking ends with the commandment no longer standing outside a man but written inside him, and nothing in the gift sets it against the Torah.
cards.prose: The good things the Father gives reach down to what Yahuah (the LORD) promised the house of Yashar'el (Israel) through Jeremiah, his *law* set in their inward parts and written in their hearts. The asking ends with the commandment no longer standing outside a man but written inside him, and nothing in the gift sets it against the Torah.
cards.member_note: Jeremiah 31:33 — *I will put my law in their inward parts, and write it in their hearts.* Yahuah (the LORD) promises to put his law inside his people and write it on their hearts, which is the good gift in full.

cards.src_text: If you then, being evil, know how to give good gifts unto your children, how much more shall your Father which is in heaven give good things to them that ask him?
cards.tgt_text: A new heart also will I give you, and a new spirit will I put within you: and I will take away the stony heart out of your flesh, and I will give you an heart of flesh.
cards.old_note: *A new heart also will I give you ... and cause you to walk in my statutes* — the Spirit-empowered Torah-walking promise the good gift produces.
cards.note: Ezekiel 36:26 — *A new heart also will I give you, and a new spirit will I put within you: and I will take away the stony heart out of your flesh, and I will give you an heart of flesh.* *If you then, being evil, know how to give good gifts unto your children, how much more shall your Father which is in heaven give good things to them that ask him?* (Matthew 7:11) Ezekiel spells out the good gift as a heart of flesh in the place of a stony one. The next verse says what that heart is for: *cause you to walk in my statutes, and ye shall keep my judgments, and do them* (Ezekiel 36:27). The Father who answers the child gives what makes his commandments the child's own.
cards.prose: Ezekiel spells out the good gift as a heart of flesh in the place of a stony one. The next verse says what that heart is for: *cause you to walk in my statutes, and ye shall keep my judgments, and do them* (Ezekiel 36:27). The Father who answers the child gives what makes his commandments the child's own.
cards.member_note: Ezekiel 36:26 — *A new heart also will I give you, and a new spirit will I put within you.* Yahuah (the LORD) promises a new heart and a new spirit, taking away the stony heart and giving a heart of flesh.

cards.src_text: Enter you in at the strait gate: for wide is the gate, and broad is the way, that leads to destruction, and many there be which go in thereat:
cards.tgt_text: And it shall come to pass in that day, that the remnant of Yashar'el (Israel), and such as are escaped of the house of Jacob, shall no more again stay upon him that smote them; but shall stay upon Yahuah (LORD), the Holy One of Yashar'el (Israel), in truth.
cards.old_note: The remnant-of-Yashar'el (Israel) Tanakh-pattern — only a remnant returns.
cards.note: Isaiah 10:20 — *And it shall come to pass in that day, that the remnant of Yashar'el (Israel), and such as are escaped of the house of Jacob, shall no more again stay upon him that smote them; but shall stay upon Yahuah (LORD), the Holy One of Yashar'el (Israel), in truth.* *Enter you in at the strait gate: for wide is the gate, and broad is the way, that leads to destruction, and many there be which go in thereat:* (Matthew 7:13) Many go in at the wide gate, and Isaiah had long said what that costs: *yet a remnant of them shall return* (Isaiah 10:22). Those who come through are the ones who stop leaning on the hand that struck them and lean on Yahuah (the LORD) in truth.
cards.prose: Many go in at the wide gate, and Isaiah had long said what that costs: *yet a remnant of them shall return* (Isaiah 10:22). Those who come through are the ones who stop leaning on the hand that struck them and lean on Yahuah (the LORD) in truth.
cards.member_note: Isaiah 10:20 — *the remnant of Yashar'el (Israel), and such as are escaped of the house of Jacob.* Isaiah says only a remnant of Yashar'el (Israel) escapes and leans on Yahuah (the LORD) in truth, which is the narrow way's own end.

cards.src_text: Enter you in at the strait gate: for wide is the gate, and broad is the way, that leads to destruction, and many there be which go in thereat:
cards.tgt_text: And it shall come to pass, that in all the land, saith Yahuah (LORD), two parts therein shall be cut off and die; but the third shall be left therein.
cards.old_note: *Two parts therein shall be cut off and die; but the third shall be left therein* — the third-part remnant; explicit numerical-minority structure.
cards.note: Zechariah 13:8 — *And it shall come to pass, that in all the land, saith Yahuah (LORD), two parts therein shall be cut off and die; but the third shall be left therein.* *Enter you in at the strait gate: for wide is the gate, and broad is the way, that leads to destruction, and many there be which go in thereat:* (Matthew 7:13) Matthew sets the many going in at the wide gate against a narrow way, and Zechariah puts a number on the difference: two parts cut off and die, and the third left. The third is not simply spared, since the verse after brings it through the fire to be refined as silver is refined.
cards.prose: Matthew sets the many going in at the wide gate against a narrow way, and Zechariah puts a number on the difference: two parts cut off and die, and the third left. The third is not simply spared, since the verse after brings it through the fire to be refined as silver is refined.
cards.member_note: Zechariah 13:8 — *two parts therein shall be cut off and die; but the third shall be left therein.* Zechariah gives the few a number, two parts cut off and one left, and says the one left is brought through the fire.

cards.src_text: Enter you in at the strait gate: for wide is the gate, and broad is the way, that leads to destruction, and many there be which go in thereat:
cards.tgt_text: I will also leave in the midst of thee an afflicted and poor people, and they shall trust in the name of Yahuah (LORD).
cards.old_note: *I will also leave in the midst of thee an afflicted and poor people, and they shall trust in the name of Yahuah (the LORD). The remnant of Yashar'el (Israel) shall not do iniquity* — the remnant defined by Torah-walking.
cards.note: Zephaniah 3:12 — *I will also leave in the midst of thee an afflicted and poor people, and they shall trust in the name of Yahuah (LORD).* *Enter you in at the strait gate: for wide is the gate, and broad is the way, that leads to destruction, and many there be which go in thereat:* (Matthew 7:13) The people Yahuah (the LORD) leaves are an afflicted and poor people who trust in his name, and the next verse says what marks them: *shall not do iniquity, nor speak lies* (Zephaniah 3:13). Those who find the narrow way are known by their walk, and by what they will not do.
cards.prose: The people Yahuah (the LORD) leaves are an afflicted and poor people who trust in his name, and the next verse says what marks them: *shall not do iniquity, nor speak lies* (Zephaniah 3:13). Those who find the narrow way are known by their walk, and by what they will not do.
cards.member_note: Zephaniah 3:12 — *I will also leave in the midst of thee an afflicted and poor people, and they shall trust in the name of Yahuah (LORD).* Zephaniah says Yahuah (the LORD) will leave an afflicted and poor people, and what marks them is that they trust in his name.

cards.src_text: Enter you in at the strait gate: for wide is the gate, and broad is the way, that leads to destruction, and many there be which go in thereat:
cards.tgt_text: Then said one unto him, Adonai (Lord), are there few that be saved? And he said unto them,
cards.old_note: *Strive to enter in at the strait gate: for many, I say unto you, will seek to enter in, and shall not be able* — Lukan parallel that intensifies the *few* of Matt 7:14.
cards.note: Luke 13:23 — *Then said one unto him, Adonai (Lord), are there few that be saved? And he said unto them,* *Enter you in at the strait gate: for wide is the gate, and broad is the way, that leads to destruction, and many there be which go in thereat:* (Matthew 7:13) A man asks Yahusha (Jesus) the very question the Sermon leaves hanging, whether the saved are few. His answer is a gate, the same strait gate: *Strive to enter in at the strait gate: for many, I say unto you, will seek to enter in, and shall not be able* (Luke 13:24).
cards.prose: A man asks Yahusha (Jesus) the very question the Sermon leaves hanging, whether the saved are few. His answer is a gate, the same strait gate: *Strive to enter in at the strait gate: for many, I say unto you, will seek to enter in, and shall not be able* (Luke 13:24).
cards.member_note: Luke 13:23 — *Then said one unto him, Adonai (Lord), are there few that be saved? And he said unto them,* Luke records the question whether few are saved, and Yahusha (Jesus) answers by naming the same strait gate.

cards.src_text: Beware of false prophets, which come to you in sheep’s clothing, but inwardly they are ravening wolves.
cards.tgt_text: For I know this, that after my departing shall grievous wolves enter in among you, not sparing the flock.
cards.old_note: Paul's warning to the Ephesian elders — *grievous wolves enter in among you, not sparing the flock. Also of your own selves shall men arise, speaking perverse things* — the apostolic confirmation of the false-prophets-among-the-gathering pattern.
cards.note: Acts 20:29 — *For I know this, that after my departing shall grievous wolves enter in among you, not sparing the flock.* *Beware of false prophets, which come to you in sheep’s clothing, but inwardly they are ravening wolves.* (Matthew 7:15) Yahusha (Jesus) says the wolves come in *sheep’s clothing*. Paul, leaving Ephesus, says the grievous wolves will enter in among the flock and not spare it, and then adds that they will not all come from outside: *Also of your own selves shall men arise, speaking perverse things, to draw away disciples after them* (Acts 20:30).
cards.prose: Yahusha (Jesus) says the wolves come in *sheep’s clothing*. Paul, leaving Ephesus, says the grievous wolves will enter in among the flock and not spare it, and then adds that they will not all come from outside: *Also of your own selves shall men arise, speaking perverse things, to draw away disciples after them* (Acts 20:30).
cards.member_note: Acts 20:29 — *For I know this, that after my departing shall grievous wolves enter in among you, not sparing the flock.* Paul warns the Ephesian elders that grievous wolves will enter in among the flock and not spare it.

cards.src_text: Therefore whosoever hears these sayings of mine, and does them, I will liken him unto a wise man, which built his house upon a rock:
cards.tgt_text: And he took the book of the covenant, and read in the audience of the people: and they said, All that Yahuah (LORD) hath said will we do, and be obedient.
cards.old_note: *All that Yahuah (the LORD) hath said will we do, and be obedient (na'aseh v'nishma)* — the do-and-hear Tanakh-pattern Matt 7:24-27 walks.
cards.note: Exodus 24:7 — *And he took the book of the covenant, and read in the audience of the people: and they said, All that Yahuah (LORD) hath said will we do, and be obedient.* *Therefore whosoever hears these sayings of mine, and does them, I will liken him unto a wise man, which built his house upon a rock:* (Matthew 7:24) Hearing and doing together is the oldest pairing Yashar'el (Israel) had. When Moses read the book of the covenant in the hearing of the people, they answered that they would do it and be obedient. The wise builder is that answer carried out, and the sayings Yahusha (Jesus) asks to be done are no stranger to the words Moses read.
cards.prose: Hearing and doing together is the oldest pairing Yashar'el (Israel) had. When Moses read the book of the covenant in the hearing of the people, they answered that they would do it and be obedient. The wise builder is that answer carried out, and the sayings Yahusha (Jesus) asks to be done are no stranger to the words Moses read.
cards.member_note: Exodus 24:7 — *All that Yahuah (LORD) hath said will we do, and be obedient.* The people answer that all Yahuah (the LORD) has said they will do and be obedient, the pattern of hearing and doing.

cards.src_text: Therefore whosoever hears these sayings of mine, and does them, I will liken him unto a wise man, which built his house upon a rock:
cards.tgt_text: He is the Rock, his work is perfect: for all his ways are judgment: a Elohim (God) of truth and without iniquity, just and right is he.
cards.old_note: *He is the Rock, his work is perfect* — the Tanakh's foundation-rock identification of Yahuah (the LORD).
cards.note: Deuteronomy 32:4 — *He is the Rock, his work is perfect: for all his ways are judgment: a Elohim (God) of truth and without iniquity, just and right is he.* *Therefore whosoever hears these sayings of mine, and does them, I will liken him unto a wise man, which built his house upon a rock:* (Matthew 7:24) The rock has a name in the song of Moses: Yahuah (the LORD) is the Rock, his work perfect and all his ways judgment. A house built on his sayings stands on his ways, and the verse after sets beside him a people who corrupted themselves, *a perverse and crooked generation* (Deuteronomy 32:5).

A house built on his sayings stands on his ways, and the verse after sets beside him a people who corrupted themselves, *a perverse and crooked generation* (Deuteronomy 32:5).
cards.member_note: Deuteronomy 32:4 — *He is the Rock, his work is perfect: for all his ways are judgment: a Elohim (God) of truth and without iniquity, just and right is he.* Moses names Yahuah (the LORD) as the Rock whose work is perfect and whose ways are all judgment.

cards.src_text: Therefore whosoever hears these sayings of mine, and does them, I will liken him unto a wise man, which built his house upon a rock:
cards.tgt_text: Yahuah (LORD) is my rock, and my fortress, and my deliverer; my Elohim (God), my strength, in whom I will trust; my buckler, and the horn of my salvation, and my high tower.
cards.old_note: *Yahuah (the LORD) is my rock, and my fortress* — the foundation-rock prayer-substance.
cards.note: Psalm 18:2 — *Yahuah (LORD) is my rock, and my fortress, and my deliverer; my Elohim (God), my strength, in whom I will trust; my buckler, and the horn of my salvation, and my high tower.* *Therefore whosoever hears these sayings of mine, and does them, I will liken him unto a wise man, which built his house upon a rock:* (Matthew 7:24) David calls on his rock with the flood already around him, and he says what it holds up under: *the floods of ungodly men made me afraid* (Psalm 18:4). The house that does not fall stands on the one he calls his rock, his fortress and his deliverer, Yahuah (the LORD) himself.

cards.member_note: Psalm 18:2 — *Yahuah (LORD) is my rock, and my fortress, and my deliverer.* David calls Yahuah (the LORD) his rock, fortress and deliverer, the ground that holds when the floods come.

cards.src_text: Therefore whosoever hears these sayings of mine, and does them, I will liken him unto a wise man, which built his house upon a rock:
cards.tgt_text: But be ye doers of the word, and not hearers only, deceiving your own selves.
cards.old_note: *But be ye doers of the word, and not hearers only ... whoso looketh into the perfect law of liberty, and continueth therein, he being not a forgetful hearer, but a doer of the work, this man shall be blessed in his deed* — Ya'aqov's (James's) apostolic restatement of the Matt 7:24-27 hearer-AND-doer standard.
cards.note: James 1:22 — *But be ye doers of the word, and not hearers only, deceiving your own selves.* *Therefore whosoever hears these sayings of mine, and does them, I will liken him unto a wise man, which built his house upon a rock:* (Matthew 7:24) James puts the two builders into one line. Hearing alone deceives a man, and the doer is the one who holds to *the perfect law of liberty* (James 1:25), the commandment the whole sermon rests on. The house on the rock is the word heard and done, and the house on the sand is the word heard and left there.

threads.title: The carrying away to Babylon, and the house still scattered
threads.summary_md:
It ain't new. The turn in Matthew's list was spoken of and written down long before he set it in his book.

*And Josias begat Jechonias and his brethren, about the time they were carried away to Babylon:* (Matthew 1:11)

Babylon was not the first captivity. The northern house of Yashar'el (Israel) had been taken out of the land well before, and it never came home in a body.

*In the ninth year of Hoshea the king of Assyria took Samaria, and carried Yashar'el (Israel) away into Assyria, and placed them in Halah and in Habor by the river of Gozan, and in the cities of the Medes.* (2 Kings 17:6)

Then Yahudah (Judah) was taken in her turn, and the land was emptied of nearly everyone who could lead it.

*And he carried away all Jerusalem, and all the princes, and all the mighty men of valour, even ten thousand captives, and all the craftsmen and smiths: none remained, save the poorest sort of the people of the land.* (2 Kings 24:14)

Jeremiah had already said how long it would last, so the captivity was not an accident that broke the line.

*And this whole land shall be a desolation, and an astonishment; and these nations shall serve the king of Babylon seventy years.* (Jeremiah 25:11)

Some did go home, but it was a partial return to Jerusalem and Yahudah (Judah), and nothing like the gathering of both houses that the prophets describe.

*Now these are the children of the province that went up out of the captivity, of those which had been carried away, whom Nebuchadnezzar the king of Babylon had carried away unto Babylon, and came again unto Jerusalem and Yahudah (Judah), every one unto his city;* (Ezra 2:1)

That is why Matthew counts the way he does.

*So all the generations from Abraham to David are fourteen generations; and from David until the carrying away into Babylon are fourteen generations; and from the carrying away into Babylon unto Messiah (Christ) are fourteen generations.* (Matthew 1:17)

The count runs straight through the carrying away and ends at Messiah (Christ). The line of the king is shown walking through exile, with the northern house still scattered and the return still ahead.

threads.title: Herod and the old hatred of Esau for Jacob (Genesis 27; Numbers 20; Obadiah; Psalm 137; Malachi 1; Ezekiel 35)
threads.summary_md:
It ain't new. When Herod the king hears that a King of the Yahudim (Jews) is born, the scripture says he is shaken:

*When Herod the king had heard these things, he was troubled, and all Jerusalem with him.* (Matthew 2:3)

The reader who looks back finds the same hatred in the same family, running from the first brothers to this king. Esau's heart was set on murder because of the blessing:

*And Esau hated Jacob because of the blessing wherewith his father blessed him: and Esau said in his heart, The days of mourning for my father are at hand; then will I slay my brother Jacob.* (Genesis 27:41)

The prophets name Edom's violence against Jacob, and give it its answer:

*For thy violence against thy brother Jacob shame shall cover thee, and thou shalt be cut off for ever.* (Obadiah 1:10)

The psalmist carries the cry that was made over the city on the day it fell:

*Remember, O Yahuah (LORD), the children of Edom in the day of Jerusalem; who said, Rase it, rase it, even to the foundation thereof.* (Psalm 137:7)

Over all of it stands the word of Yahuah (the LORD) that does not move with the kings:

*I have loved you, saith Yahuah (LORD). Yet ye say, Wherein hast thou loved us? Was not Esau Jacob’s brother? saith Yahuah (LORD): yet I loved Jacob,* (Malachi 1:2)

Herod's order shows where the old hatred lands. He cannot find the child, so he reaches for every child he can find:

*Then Herod, when he saw that he was mocked of the wise men, was exceeding wroth, and sent forth, and slew all the children that were in Bethlehem, and in all the coasts thereof, from two years old and under, according to the time which he had diligently enquired of the wise men.* (Matthew 2:16)

Herod was of Edom's house, an Idumean set on the throne in Jerusalem, and the prophets had already spoken to that house: Moses' message to the king of Edom at the border, the word given to Ezekiel against Mount Seir, the psalm that remembers the day the city fell. What Matthew shows in Herod is the old hatred of the blessing, sitting on a throne. It is the throne and the hatred the scripture names, and the word that stands over both is the one Malachi wrote down: *yet I loved Jacob*.

threads.title: The Jordan, where the people crossed and the prophets worked
threads.summary_md:
It ain't new. The river was already carrying this, and Matthew sets Yahusha (Jesus) where the older scripture had set the great turnings of the people.

*Then cometh Yahusha (Jesus) from Galilee to Jordan unto John, to be baptized of him.* (Matthew 3:13)

The people of Yashar'el (Israel) first came into their land through this water, with the ark going ahead of them.

*And it came to pass, when the people removed from their tents, to pass over Jordan, and the priests bearing the ark of the covenant before the people;* (Joshua 3:14)

The word that sent them over was spoken to a man whose name is the same name Yahusha (Jesus) carries.

*Now after the death of Moses the servant of Yahuah (LORD) it came to pass, that Yahuah (LORD) spake unto Joshua the son of Nun, Moses’ minister, saying,* (Joshua 1:1)

Then the prophets worked at the same river. Elijah was sent there, and Elisha went with him and would not turn back.

*And Elijah said unto him, Tarry, I pray thee, here; for Yahuah (LORD) hath sent me to Jordan. And he said, As Yahuah (LORD) liveth, and as thy soul liveth, I will not leave thee. And they two went on.* (2 Kings 2:6)

And a sick man was told to wash in it by the word of the prophet, and he came up clean.

*Then went he down, and dipped himself seven times in Jordan, according to the saying of the man of Elohim (God): and his flesh came again like unto the flesh of a little child, and he was clean.* (2 Kings 5:14)

So when John baptizes in the Jordan and the people come out confessing, the water is not a new place for a new thing. It is the river of the first entry, of the prophet's errand and of cleansing at a prophet's word, and Yahusha (Jesus) comes to it as the one leading the people home.
