members.member_note: Ezekiel 36:22 — *I do not this for your sakes, O house of Yashar'el (Israel), but for mine holy name’s sake.* Adonai Yahuah (the Lord GOD) tells the scattered house that he will act for his holy name's sake, not for theirs.

Deuteronomy 9:5 — *Not for thy righteousness, or for the uprightness of thine heart, dost thou go to possess their land.* The saving rests on the oath sworn to Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob, not on the goodness of the people who receive it.

Matthew 15:24 — *But he answered and said, I am not sent but unto the lost sheep of the house of Yashar'el (Israel).* Yahusha (Jesus) himself says he is sent only to the lost sheep of the house of Yashar'el (Israel), the same people the angel names.

Matthew 10:5 — *These twelve Yahusha (Jesus) sent forth, and commanded them, saying, Go not into the way of the Gentiles.* Yahusha (Jesus) sends the twelve first to his own people, which is the scope the angel gave at his birth.

Ezekiel 34:11 — *For thus saith Adonai Yahuah (the Lord GOD); Behold, I, even I, will both search my sheep, and seek them out.* Yahuah (the LORD) says he himself will search for his scattered sheep, which is the work Yahusha (Jesus) comes to do.
John 10:27 — *My sheep hear my voice, and I know them, and they follow me:* Yahusha (Jesus) says his sheep hear his voice, so the hearing shows who his people are.

Matthew 28:19 — *Go ye therefore, and teach all nations, baptizing them in the name of the Father, and of the Son, and of the Ruach HaKodesh (Holy Spirit).* The word is sent out among all nations after the resurrection, to reach the scattered sheep wherever they were driven.

Genesis 38:26 — *And Yahudah (Judah) acknowledged them, and said, She hath been more righteous than I; because that I gave her not to Shelah my son.* Yahudah (Judah) admits Tamar was more righteous than he, so the line of the king comes through his own failure and her claim.

Joshua 2:11 — *for Yahuah Elohaychem (the LORD your God), he is Elohim (God) in heaven above, and in earth beneath.* Rachab confesses Yahuah (the LORD) as Elohim (God) in heaven and earth, before she marries Salmon and enters the line.
Ruth 1:16 — *thy people shall be my people, and thy Elohim (God) my Elohim (God).* Ruth binds herself to Naomi's people and Naomi's Elohim (God), and her marriage to Booz brings her into the line.
Genesis 19:36 — *Thus were both the daughters of Lot with child by their father.* Moab came from Lot, Abraham's nephew, so Ruth's people were near kin to Abraham's house.

Ruth 4:14 — *Blessed be Yahuah (LORD), which hath not left thee this day without a kinsman, that his name may be famous in Yashar'el (Israel).* Booz is the kinsman who redeems Naomi's house, and he points ahead to Yahusha (Jesus) as the kinsman of the scattered house.
2 Samuel 11:27 — *But the thing that David had done displeased Yahuah (LORD).* Samuel says David's deed displeased Yahuah (the LORD), which is why Matthew names Solomon's mother by her first husband.

Genesis 12:3 — *And I will bless them that bless thee, and curse him that curseth thee: and in thee shall all families of the earth be blessed.* The promise to Abraham that all families of the earth be blessed in him is what the genealogy carries down to Yahusha (Jesus).

2 Samuel 7:12 — *I will set up thy seed after thee, which shall proceed out of thy bowels, and I will establish his kingdom.* Yahuah (the LORD) promises David a seed and an established kingdom, which Matthew's list traces to Yahusha (Jesus).

2 Kings 24:14 — *And he carried away all Jerusalem, and all the princes, and all the mighty men of valour, even ten thousand captives.* Kings shows the carrying away to Babylon that Matthew marks, with Jerusalem emptied of its leaders and fighting men.

2 Kings 17:6 — *took Samaria, and carried Yashar'el (Israel) away into Assyria, and placed them in Halah and in Habor.* The northern house of Yashar'el (Israel) was carried to Assyria well before Babylon and was still scattered when Matthew's list ends.

Jeremiah 25:11 — *And this whole land shall be a desolation, and an astonishment; and these nations shall serve the king of Babylon seventy years.* Jeremiah foretold the length of the Babylonian captivity, so the carrying away is part of what was spoken beforehand.
Ezekiel 37:15 — *The word of Yahuah (LORD) came again unto me, saying,* Yahuah (the LORD) speaks again to Ezekiel, and what follows is the joining of Yahudah (Judah) and Yashar'el (Israel) into one.

Ezekiel 20:33 — *As I live, saith Adonai Yahuah (the Lord GOD), surely with a mighty hand, and with a stretched out arm.* Adonai Yahuah (the Lord GOD) swears he will rule over the scattered house and gather them out of the countries.

Isaiah 11:11 — *Yahuah (Lord) shall set his hand again the second time to recover the remnant of his people.* Yahuah (the LORD) sets his hand a second time to recover the remnant of his people from every place they were scattered.

Hosea 1:11 — *Then shall the children of Yahudah (Judah) and the children of Yashar'el (Israel) be gathered together.* Hosea says Yahudah (Judah) and Yashar'el (Israel) will be gathered together under one head, the Messiah (Christ) Matthew names.

Ezra 2:1 — *Now these are the children of the province that went up out of the captivity.* Ezra lists the families that came back from Babylon, a return to Yahudah (Judah) that fell short of the prophets' ingathering.
John 1:14 — *And the Word was made flesh, and dwelt among us.* John says the Word became flesh and lived among us, which is how Elohim (God) is with us.
Exodus 33:20 — *And he said, Thou canst not see my face: for there shall no man see me, and live.* Moses is told no man can see the Father and live, so the one who is seen is the Son.

John 1:18 — *No man hath seen Elohim (God) at any time; the only begotten Son, which is in the bosom of the Father, he hath declared him.* John says no man has seen the Father and the only begotten Son has declared him.

Genesis 18:1 — *And Yahuah (LORD) appeared unto him in the plains of Mamre: and he sat in the tent door in the heat of the day;* Yahuah (the LORD) appears to Abraham at Mamre, the Son who walked with the fathers long before Mary.

Exodus 24:9 — *Then went up Moses, and Aaron, Nadab, and Abihu, and seventy of the elders of Yashar'el (Israel):* Moses, Aaron, and the seventy elders go up and see the Elohim (God) of Yashar'el (Israel), the Son who is seen.

1 Corinthians 15:28 — *And when all things shall be subdued unto him, then shall the Son also himself be subject unto him that put all things under him.* At the end the Son is subject to the Father who put all things under him, so the Son has a Father.

1 Corinthians 11:3 — *But I would have you know, that the head of every man is the Messiah (Christ); and the head of the woman is the man; and the head of the Messiah (Christ) is Elohim (God).* Paul says the head of the Messiah (Christ) is Elohim (God), so the Son is under the Father even in the flesh.

Numbers 13:16 — *These are the names of the men which Moses sent to spy out the land. And Moses called Oshea the son of Nun Jehoshua.* Moses renames Oshea Jehoshua, an older form of the name Yahusha (Jesus), with the Father's name inside it.

Psalm 68:4 — *Sing unto Elohim (God), sing praises to his name: extol him that rideth upon the heavens by his name JAH, and rejoice before him.* The psalm calls the singers to praise him by his name Yah, which is the first part of the name Yahusha (Jesus).

Joshua 1:1 — *Now after the death of Moses the servant of Yahuah (LORD) it came to pass, that Yahuah (LORD) spake unto Joshua the son of Nun, Moses’ minister, saying,* Joshua, who bears the same name as Yahusha (Jesus), is commissioned to lead the people into the land.

Philippians 2:9 — *Wherefore Elohim (God) also hath highly exalted him, and given him a name which is above every name:* Paul says Elohim (God) exalted him and gave him a name above every name, the name given at his birth.

1 Samuel 16:1 — *fill thine horn with oil, and go, I will send thee to Jesse the Beth-lehemite: for I have provided me a king among his sons.* Yahuah (the LORD) sends Samuel to anoint a king from among Jesse's sons, the founding of the king's line.
2 Samuel 11:1 — *But David tarried still at Jerusalem.* The account of David and Bath-sheba begins with the king staying home while the army fights, which is the root of Matthew's phrase.

2 Kings 23:34 — *And Pharaoh-nechoh made Eliakim the son of Josiah king in the room of Josiah his father, and turned his name to Jehoiakim.* After Josias, Pharaoh sets and removes the kings of Yahudah (Judah), the falling apart that leads to Babylon.

Jeremiah 22:24 — *As I live, saith Yahuah (LORD), though Coniah the son of Jehoiakim king of Yahudah (Judah) were the signet upon my right hand.* Yahuah (the LORD) pronounces judgment on Coniah, the Jechonias of Matthew's list, though the line still runs through him.

Luke 1:26 — *And in the sixth month the angel Gabriel was sent from Elohim (God) unto a city of Galilee, named Nazareth,* Luke begins the same conception from Mary's side, with Gabriel sent to Nazareth.

Deuteronomy 22:23 — *If a damsel that is a virgin be betrothed unto an husband, and a man find her in the city, and lie with her;* The Torah speaks of a betrothed virgin found with another man, the exposure Joseph's quiet course would have spared Mary.

Deuteronomy 24:1 — *then let him write her a bill of divorcement, and give it in her hand, and send her out of his house.* The bill of divorcement is the Torah's quiet way for Joseph to put Mary away without exposing her.

Genesis 28:12 — *And he dreamed, and behold a ladder set up on the earth, and the top of it reached to heaven: and behold the angels of Elohim (God) ascending and descending on it.* Jacob's dream at Beth-el shows an angel of Elohim (God) giving direction in a dream, as Joseph is given.
Genesis 37:5 — *And Joseph dreamed a dream, and he told it his brethren: and they hated him yet the more.* The patriarch Joseph received word in dreams, as Matthew's Joseph does.

Daniel 2:19 — *Then was the secret revealed unto Daniel in a night vision. Then Daniel blessed the Elohim (God) of heaven.* Daniel is shown a hidden thing in a night vision, the same way Joseph is shown the secret of the conception.

2 Samuel 7:12 — *I will set up thy seed after thee, which shall proceed out of thy bowels, and I will establish his kingdom.* The angel's name for Joseph, son of David, points to the promise of a seed and a kingdom.

Luke 2:7 — *And she brought forth her firstborn son, and wrapped him in swaddling clothes, and laid him in a manger; because there was no room for them in the inn.* Luke gives the birth of the firstborn son that Joseph's obedience in taking Mary made room for.

Exodus 13:2 — *Sanctify unto me all the firstborn, whatsoever openeth the womb among the children of Yashar'el (Israel), both of man and of beast: it is mine.* The Torah sets every firstborn apart to Yahuah (the LORD), which is the standing of the child Mary bears.

Colossians 1:15 — *Who is the image of the invisible Elohim (God), the firstborn of every creature:* Paul calls the firstborn the image of the invisible Father, so the child Mary bore is the Father's image.

Colossians 1:18 — *And he is the head of the body, the church: who is the beginning, the firstborn from the dead; that in all things he might have the preeminence.* Paul calls the firstborn the head of the body and the firstborn from the dead, the one with the highest place.

Daniel 2:48 — *made him ruler over the whole province of Babylon, and chief of the governors over all the wise men of Babylon.* Daniel is made chief over the wise men of Babylon, which gives the eastern wise men of Matthew a prophet's name behind their watching.

Daniel 9:24 — *to bring in everlasting righteousness, and to seal up the vision and prophecy, and to anoint the most Holy.* Daniel's seventy weeks fix the time of the anointed one, the timing the eastern wise men could have drawn from the prophet who served in their land.

Exodus 13:21 — *went before them by day in a pillar of a cloud, to lead them the way; and by night in a pillar of fire, to give them light.* Yahuah (the LORD) went before his people by day and by night in a visible sign, as the star goes before the wise men to the child.

Obadiah 1:10 — *For thy violence against thy brother Jacob shame shall cover thee, and thou shalt be cut off for ever.* Obadiah names Edom's violence against his brother Jacob, the old wrong that Herod's fear of the newborn King repeats.

Numbers 20:14 — *And Moses sent messengers from Kadesh unto the king of Edom, Thus saith thy brother Yashar'el (Israel), Thou knowest all the travail that hath befallen us:* Moses calls Edom's king his brother and asks for passage, the first place in the story where Edom stands against Yashar'el (Israel).

Malachi 1:2 — *I have loved you, saith Yahuah (LORD). Yet ye say, Wherein hast thou loved us? Was not Esau Jacob’s brother? saith Yahuah (LORD): yet I loved Jacob,* Yahuah (the LORD) says he loved Jacob and answers the question of Esau and Jacob, the choice that stands under Herod's hatred.

Ezekiel 35:1 — *Moreover the word of Yahuah (LORD) came unto me, saying,* The word of Yahuah (the LORD) comes to Ezekiel against Mount Seir, and it answers Edom's lasting hatred of the children of Yashar'el (Israel).

Psalm 137:7 — *Remember, O Yahuah (LORD), the children of Edom in the day of Jerusalem; who said, Rase it, rase it, even to the foundation thereof.* The psalmist asks Yahuah (the LORD) to remember Edom's cry to level Jerusalem, the same hostility now sitting on the throne at Herod's court.

Genesis 27:41 — *And Esau hated Jacob because of the blessing wherewith his father blessed him.* Esau hates Jacob for the blessing and resolves to kill him, the first murder planned out of that hatred, which Herod acts on at Bethlehem.

Exodus 1:8 — *Now there arose up a new king over Egypt, which knew not Joseph.* A new king arises over Egypt who knew not Joseph, the beginning of the hard rule that falls on the sons of Yashar'el (Israel).

Exodus 2:1 — *And there went a man of the house of Levi, and took to wife a daughter of Levi.* A man of the house of Levi takes a daughter of Levi to wife, the house into which Moses is born and hidden from the king.

Genesis 46:1 — *And Yashar'el (Israel) took his journey with all that he had, and came to Beer-sheba, and offered sacrifices unto the Elohim (God) of his father Isaac.* Jacob journeys toward Egypt with all he had and offers at Beer-sheba, the fathers' road down that Joseph and the child walk again.

Exodus 12:40 — *Now the sojourning of the children of Yashar'el (Israel), who dwelt in Egypt, was four hundred and thirty years.* The sojourn of the children of Yashar'el (Israel) in Egypt is counted at four hundred and thirty years before the going out.

Exodus 4:19 — *And Yahuah (LORD) said unto Moses in Midian, Go, return into Egypt: for all the men are dead which sought thy life.* Yahuah (the LORD) tells Moses in Midian to return to Egypt because the men who sought his life are dead, the words the angel echoes to Joseph.

Jeremiah 31:31 — *Behold, the days come, saith Yahuah (LORD), that I will make a new covenant with the house of Yashar'el (Israel), and with the house of Yahudah (Judah):* Yahuah (the LORD) promises a new covenant with both the house of Yashar'el (Israel) and the house of Yahudah (Judah), the comfort the same chapter gives Rachel.

Genesis 35:16 — *And they journeyed from Beth-el; and there was but a little way to come to Ephrath: and Rachel travailed, and she had hard labour.* Rachel travails and dies a little way from Ephrath, which is Bethlehem, fixing her weeping at the place Herod's soldiers came.

Jeremiah 31:9 — *They shall come with weeping, and with supplications will I lead them: I will cause them to walk by the rivers of waters in a straight way.* Yahuah (the LORD) leads the weeping remnant of Yashar'el (Israel) home by a straight way, with Ephraim, Rachel's grandson, called his firstborn.

Matthew 26:28 — *For this is my blood of the new testament, which is shed for many for the remission of sins.* Yahusha (Jesus) names his blood as the blood of the new covenant, the covenant of the chapter from which Rachel's weeping is quoted.

Jeremiah 23:5 — *Behold, the days come, saith Yahuah (LORD), that I will raise unto David a righteous Branch, and a King shall reign and prosper, and shall execute judgment and justice in the earth.* Jeremiah promises a righteous Branch raised to David, who reigns over the flock gathered back from the countries where it was driven.

Jeremiah 33:15 — *In those days, and at that time, will I cause the Branch of righteousness to grow up unto David; and he shall execute judgment and righteousness in the land.* Jeremiah says Yahuah (the LORD) will cause the Branch of righteousness to grow up to David and execute judgment in the land.

Zechariah 3:8 — *Hear now, O Joshua the high priest, thou, and thy fellows that sit before thee: for they are men wondered at: for, behold, I will bring forth my servant the BRANCH.* Yahuah (the LORD) promises to bring forth his servant the Branch, spoken to Joshua the high priest as a sign of what is coming.

Zechariah 6:12 — *Behold the man whose name is The BRANCH; and he shall grow up out of his place.* Zechariah names the man whose name is the Branch, who grows up out of his place and builds the house of Yahuah (the LORD).

Micah 5:2 — *yet out of thee shall he come forth unto me that is to be ruler in Yashar'el (Israel); whose goings forth have been from of old, from everlasting.* Micah names Bethlehem Ephratah as the place from which the ruler in Yashar'el (Israel) comes, whose goings forth are from of old.

1 Samuel 16:1 — *And Yahuah (LORD) said unto Samuel, How long wilt thou mourn for Saul, seeing I have rejected him from reigning over Yashar'el (Israel)? fill thine horn with oil, and go.* Yahuah (the LORD) sends Samuel to Jesse the Bethlehemite, because he has provided a king among his sons.

1 Samuel 16:4 — *And Samuel did that which Yahuah (LORD) spake, and came to Beth-lehem. And the elders of the town trembled at his coming, and said, Comest thou peaceably?* Samuel comes to Bethlehem at Yahuah's (the LORD's) word and the elders tremble at his coming, the place where David was found.

Ruth 4:11 — *Yahuah (LORD) make the woman that is come into thine house like Rachel and like Leah, which two did build the house of Yashar'el (Israel).* At the gate in Bethlehem, Ruth is blessed to be like Rachel and Leah, who built the house of Yashar'el (Israel), in the marriage that leads to David.

Exodus 30:34 — *Take unto thee sweet spices, stacte, and onycha, and galbanum; these sweet spices with pure frankincense.* Yahuah (the LORD) tells Moses to compound the holy incense with pure frankincense, the priestly use of the gift the wise men bring.

Psalm 45:8 — *All thy garments smell of myrrh, and aloes, and cassia, out of the ivory palaces, whereby they have made thee glad.* Myrrh, aloes and cassia scent the King's garments in the psalm, a royal perfume that the wise men lay before the child.

Isaiah 9:1 — *Nevertheless the dimness shall not be such as was in her vexation, when at the first he lightly afflicted the land of Zebulun and the land of Naphtali, and afterward did more grievously afflict her by the way of the sea, beyond Jordan, in Galilee of the nations.* Isaiah names Zebulun and Naphtali, Galilee, as the first land afflicted, the northern country where the light is promised next.

Malachi 4:5 — *Behold, I will send you Elijah the prophet before the coming of the great and dreadful day of Yahuah (LORD):* The closing word of the prophets promises Elijah before the great day of Yahuah (the LORD), and John arrives in the wilderness as that promise.
1 Kings 18:1 — *the word of Yahuah (LORD) came to Elijah in the third year.* Elijah is sent by the word of Yahuah (the LORD) to confront a king and call a people back, the pattern John follows.

Ezekiel 18:30 — *Repent, and turn yourselves from all your transgressions.* Yahuah (the LORD) calls the house of Yashar'el (Israel) to turn from all its transgressions, the same turning of a whole life John asks for.

Isaiah 40:3 — *Prepare ye the way of Yahuah (LORD), make straight in the desert a highway.* Isaiah's voice in the wilderness clears the road for Yahuah (the LORD) at the head of his comfort to his people, and John is that voice.

Matthew 23:33 — *Ye serpents, ye generation of vipers, how can ye escape the damnation of hell?* Yahusha (Jesus) later gives the scribes and Pharisees the same name John gave them at the Jordan, so the word was never a passing outburst.

John 8:44 — *Ye are of your father the devil, and the lusts of your father ye will do.* Yahusha (Jesus) names whose seed it is that does the father's work, which is what John saw coming to the water as vipers.
Genesis 3:15 — *between thee and the woman, and between thy seed and her seed.* Yahuah (the LORD) set enmity between the serpent's seed and the woman's seed, the line John's word vipers falls along.

Acts 15:1 — *Except ye be circumcised after the manner of Moses, ye cannot be saved.* Men teaching that a rite makes a man saved are the same flesh credential John would not let the Pharisees hide behind.

Galatians 2:4 — *false brethren unawares brought in, who came in privily to spy out our liberty.* Paul names the men who slipped in to bind others with a flesh credential, the same system John met at the Jordan.

Philippians 3:2 — *Beware of dogs, beware of evil workers, beware of the concision.* Paul warns against confidence in the flesh and then sets out his own credentials, which are what John says cannot shelter anyone.

John 3:1 — *There was a man of the Pharisees, named Nicodemus, a ruler of the Yahudim (Jews):* Nicodemus, a Pharisee and a ruler, comes to Yahusha (Jesus) himself, so a man standing inside that system can still turn and come.

Joshua 3:14 — *the priests bearing the ark of the covenant before the people.* Yashar'el (Israel) first crossed the Jordan behind the ark, the crossing into the land that Yahusha (Jesus) meets again at the same water.

Joshua 1:1 — *Yahuah (LORD) spake unto Joshua the son of Nun.* Joshua is commissioned to lead the people over the Jordan into the land, and Yahusha (Jesus), who has the same name, stands at the same river.
2 Kings 2:6 — *Yahuah (LORD) hath sent me to Jordan.* Elijah is sent to the Jordan and Elisha will not leave him there, the prophet's errand at the river that John's work at the Jordan repeats.

2 Kings 5:14 — *dipped himself seven times in Jordan, according to the saying of the man of Elohim (God).* Naaman is made clean in the Jordan at a prophet's word, showing the river as a place of cleansing before John baptized there.
Malachi 3:1 — *he shall come, saith Yahuah Tseva'ot (LORD of hosts).* Malachi's refiner's fire, the day of his coming and who can stand it, is the fire John says the coming one brings.

Isaiah 53:11 — *by his knowledge shall my righteous servant justify many.* The servant of Yahuah (the LORD) is called righteous and bears the iniquities of many, the work Yahusha (Jesus) takes up when he is baptized.
Psalm 91:11 — *For he shall give his angels charge over thee, to keep thee in all thy ways.* The psalm promises angels will keep him in all his ways, which the devil's quotation of it passes over.

Deuteronomy 6:16 — *Ye shall not tempt Yahuah Elohaychem (the LORD your God), as ye tempted him in Massah.* Moses forbids putting Yahuah (the LORD) to the test as Yashar'el (Israel) did at Massah, and Yahusha (Jesus) answers the pinnacle with it.
1 John 2:3 — *And hereby we do know that we know him, if we keep his commandments.* John says we know him by keeping his commandments, which rules out any reading of scripture that sets them aside.

Matthew 22:29 — *Yahusha (Jesus) answered and said unto them, Ye do err, not knowing the scriptures, nor the power of Elohim (God).* Yahusha (Jesus) tells the Sadducees their error comes from not knowing the scriptures, the same fault the devil trades on at the pinnacle.

2 Peter 3:16 — *unlearned and unstable wrest, as they do also the other scriptures, unto their own destruction.* Peter names the wresting of scripture that the devil begins at the pinnacle and that was later turned on Paul's letters.

Daniel 10:13 — *But the prince of the kingdom of Persia withstood me one and twenty days.* A prince stands behind the kingdom of Persia and resists the messenger, showing that powers sit behind the kingdoms of the world.

Daniel 10:20 — *and now will I return to fight with the prince of Persia: and when I am gone forth, lo, the prince of Grecia shall come.* After the prince of Persia the prince of Grecia comes next, so the powers behind the kingdoms follow one another.

Ephesians 6:12 — *against principalities, against powers, against the rulers of the darkness of this world.* Paul names the principalities and rulers of this world's darkness as the real opponent, not the people under them.
1 John 5:19 — *And we know that we are of Elohim (God), and the whole world lieth in wickedness.* John says the whole world lies in wickedness, which is the state of the kingdoms the devil holds out.
Daniel 7:13 — *and they brought him near before him.* Daniel sees the kingdom given to the one like the Son of Adam in the Father's presence, not taken by a bow.

Revelation 11:15 — *The kingdoms of this world are become the kingdoms of our Lord, and of his Messiah (Christ).* The kingdoms of this world become the Messiah's (Christ's) at the seventh trumpet, on the Father's timing.

Genesis 3:15 — *and between thy seed and her seed; it shall bruise thy head, and thou shalt bruise his heel.* The first word to the serpent says the seed of the woman will bruise his head, and the heel is bruised on the way.

Psalm 91:14 — *Because he hath set his love upon me, therefore will I deliver him: I will set him on high, because he hath known my name.* The promise of deliverance goes to the one who has set his love on Yahuah (the LORD) and known his name, not to a dare.

Hebrews 1:14 — *Are they not all ministering spirits, sent forth to minister for them who shall be heirs of salvation?* Angels are ministering spirits sent to serve the heirs, and here they come on their own once the testing is over.

1 Kings 19:5 — *And as he lay and slept under a juniper tree, behold, then an angel touched him, and said unto him, Arise and eat.* An angel touches Elijah in the wilderness and tells him to arise and eat, as angels serve Yahusha (Jesus) after his testing.
Matthew 3:2 — *And saying, Repent ye: for the kingdom of heaven is at hand.* John the Immerser cries the same call to turn that Yahusha (Jesus) takes up in Galilee, one message passed on.

Daniel 2:44 — *shall the Elohim (God) of heaven set up a kingdom, which shall never be destroyed.* Daniel told the king the Elohim (God) of heaven would set up a kingdom that never ends, the kingdom Yahusha (Jesus) calls at hand.

Daniel 7:13 — *one like the Son of Adam came with the clouds of heaven, and came to the Ancient of days.* Daniel sees the one like the Son of Adam brought to the Ancient of days, the king whose kingdom is at hand.

Isaiah 35:4 — *Say to them that are of a fearful heart, Be strong, fear not: behold, your Elohim (God) will come with vengeance, even Elohim (God) with a recompence; he will come and save you.* Isaiah promises that Elohim (God) will come and save, and the opened eyes and ears that follow are what Galilee sees.

Isaiah 61:1 — *he hath sent me to bind up the brokenhearted, to proclaim liberty to the captives.* The anointed one is sent to bind up the brokenhearted and free the captives, the commission Yahusha (Jesus) carries through Galilee.

Leviticus 19:17 — *Thou shalt not hate thy brother in thine heart: thou shalt in any wise rebuke thy neighbour, and not suffer sin upon him.* Moses forbids the hatred in the heart and the bearing of sin on a neighbour, which is where the sixth commandment was always rooted.

Exodus 20:17 — *Thou shalt not covet thy neighbour’s house, thou shalt not covet thy neighbour’s wife.* The tenth commandment forbids coveting a neighbour's wife, so the Torah had already named the desire that comes before the act.

Genesis 2:24 — *Therefore shall a man leave his father and his mother, and shall cleave unto his wife: and they shall be one flesh.* The first marriage tells what a marriage is, one flesh from the beginning, and that is the measure for any talk of putting a wife away.

Matthew 19:8 — *Moses because of the hardness of your hearts suffered you to put away your wives.* Yahusha (Jesus) himself says Moses allowed the writing of divorcement because of hard hearts and that it was not so from the beginning.

Matthew 23:16 — *Whosoever shall swear by the temple, it is nothing; but whosoever shall swear by the gold of the temple.* Yahusha (Jesus) names the system of graded oaths the scribes taught, which is what the saying in the Sermon had grown into.
Romans 13:3 — *For rulers are not a terror to good works, but to the evil.* Paul shows the ruler's office to punish evil still stands, so the Sermon speaks to the person wronged and not to the court.

Leviticus 19:34 — *the stranger that dwelleth with you shall be unto you as one born among you, and thou shalt love him as thyself.* Moses already extends the love command to the stranger dwelling with them, a part the added saying left out.

Exodus 23:4 — *If thou meet thine enemy’s ox or his ass going astray, thou shalt surely bring it back to him again.* The Torah commands a hand of help toward an enemy's straying animal, and nowhere commands hatred of an enemy.

Proverbs 25:21 — *If thine enemy be hungry, give him bread to eat; and if he be thirsty, give him water to drink:* The Proverbs tell the reader to feed a hungry enemy and give him water, which is love for an enemy shown in deed.
Genesis 17:1 — *I am the El Shaddai (Almighty God); walk before me, and be thou perfect.* Yahuah (the LORD) told Abram to walk before him and be perfect, the same standard the Sermon closes on.
Isaiah 57:15 — *I dwell in the high and holy place, with him also that is of a contrite and humble spirit.* The high and holy One says he dwells with the contrite and humble spirit and revives it.

Ezekiel 9:4 — *set a mark upon the foreheads of the men that sigh and that cry for all the abominations.* Those who sigh and cry over the abominations in the city are the ones Yahuah (the LORD) sets his mark upon.

Psalm 42:1 — *As the hart panteth after the water brooks, so panteth my soul after thee, O Elohim (God).* The psalmist's soul pants after Elohim (God) like a deer after water, the thirst the Beatitude pronounces blessed.

Jeremiah 23:5 — *I will raise unto David a righteous Branch, and a King shall reign and prosper.* A righteous Branch is raised to David to reign and execute judgment and justice, the source of the righteousness the hungry are filled with.

Psalm 24:3 — *Who shall ascend into the hill of Yahuah (LORD)? or who shall stand in his holy place?* The question of who may ascend Yahuah's (the LORD's) hill and stand in his holy place is the one the pure in heart answer.

Jeremiah 31:33 — *I will put my law in their inward parts, and write it in their hearts.* Yahuah (the LORD) promises to write his law in the hearts of the house of Yashar'el (Israel), the source of a pure heart.

Ezekiel 36:26 — *A new heart also will I give you, and a new spirit will I put within you: and I will take away the stony heart out of your flesh, and I will give you an heart of flesh.* Yahuah (the LORD) promises a new heart and a heart of flesh, the gift from which the pure in heart come.

Isaiah 42:21 — *Yahuah (LORD) is well pleased for his righteousness’ sake; he will magnify the law, and make it honourable.* The servant of Yahuah (the LORD) is promised to magnify the law and make it honourable, which is what fulfilling it means.

Luke 16:17 — *And it is easier for heaven and earth to pass, than one tittle of the law to fail.* Luke records the same saying, that heaven and earth will pass sooner than one tittle of the law fails.

James 2:10 — *For whosoever shall keep the whole law, and yet offend in one point, he is guilty of all.* James says whoever offends in one point of the law is guilty of all, so even the least commandment cannot be dropped.

1 Peter 1:15 — *But as he which hath called you is holy, so be ye holy in all manner of conversation;* Peter carries forward the same standard, that those called are to be holy as the one who called them is holy.

Malachi 2:16 — *saith that he hateth putting away: for one covereth violence with his garment.* Yahuah (the LORD) says he hates putting away and calls it treachery, the ground Yahusha's (Jesus's) word on divorce stands on.

Ezekiel 36:22 — *but for mine holy name’s sake, which ye have profaned among the heathen, whither ye went.* Yahuah (the LORD) says he will act for his own holy name, which his scattered people profaned among the nations.
Leviticus 16:30 — *to cleanse you, that ye may be clean from all your sins before Yahuah (LORD).* The yearly atonement was how the people were made clean from all their sins before Yahuah (the LORD).

Matthew 18:32 — *O thou wicked servant, I forgave thee all that debt, because thou desiredst me.* A servant who was forgiven a great debt is called wicked for refusing his fellow what he himself received.
Hosea 7:13 — *though I have redeemed them, yet they have spoken lies against me.* Though redeemed, the people fled and spoke lies against Yahuah (the LORD), and woe follows them.

Ezekiel 18:24 — *when the righteous turneth away from his righteousness, and committeth iniquity, and doeth according to all the abominations that the wicked man doeth, shall he live? All his righteousness that he hath done shall not be mentioned.* A righteous man who turns to iniquity has his past righteousness set aside, and dies in his sin.
Ezekiel 33:12 — *The righteousness of the righteous shall not deliver him in the day of his transgression.* The righteousness of the righteous does not deliver him on the day he transgresses.

Exodus 32:33 — *And Yahuah (LORD) said unto Moses, Whosoever hath sinned against me, him will I blot out of my book.* Whoever has sinned against Yahuah (the LORD) he will blot out of his book, which is a real loss.

Psalm 69:28 — *Let them be blotted out of the book of the living, and not be written with the righteous.* The book of the living is real, and the psalmist asks that men be blotted out of it and not written with the righteous.

Hebrews 10:26 — *For if we sin wilfully after that we have received the knowledge of the truth, there remaineth no more sacrifice for sins,* Wilful sin after the truth is known leaves no sacrifice remaining for those sins.
Matthew 7:21 — *but he that doeth the will of my Father which is in heaven.* Saying his title is not enough for the kingdom, only doing the will of the Father is.

1 John 1:9 — *If we confess our sins, he is faithful and just to forgive us our sins, and to cleanse us from all unrighteousness.* Forgiveness comes to the one who confesses his sins, so it is not received apart from a turned heart.
Deuteronomy 15:7 — *thou shalt not harden thine heart, nor shut thine hand from thy poor brother.* The Torah commands an open hand to the poor brother and forbids a hardened heart.

Leviticus 19:9 — *thou shalt not wholly reap the corners of thy field, neither shalt thou gather the gleanings of thy harvest.* The corners of the field and the gleanings were left standing for the poor as part of the harvest.

Deuteronomy 24:19 — *thou shalt not go again to fetch it: it shall be for the stranger, for the fatherless, and for the widow: that Yahuah Elohayka (the LORD thy God) may bless thee in all the work of thine hands.* A forgotten sheaf is left for the stranger, the fatherless and the widow, and Yahuah (the LORD) blesses the giver.
Psalm 41:1 — *Blessed is he that considereth the poor: Yahuah (LORD) will deliver him in time of trouble.* Blessing and deliverance in trouble belong to the man who considers the poor.

Matthew 5:16 — *Let your light so shine before men, that they may see your good works, and glorify your Father which is in heaven.* Good works are seen so that the Father is glorified, which is the opposite of giving to be seen.

1 Kings 8:22 — *in the presence of all the congregation of Yashar'el (Israel), and spread forth his hands toward heaven.* Solomon prayed openly before the whole congregation at the altar, so public prayer is not what is forbidden.

Acts 1:14 — *These all continued with one accord in prayer and supplication, with the women, and Mary the mother of Yahusha (Jesus), and with his brethren.* The disciples continued together in prayer and supplication with one accord, so praying with others is not ruled out.

Acts 2:42 — *And they continued stedfastly in the apostles’ doctrine and fellowship, and in breaking of bread, and in prayers.* Prayers were one of the things the first company held to steadily, along with teaching, fellowship and bread.
Acts 4:24 — *they lifted up their voice to Elohim (God) with one accord, and said.* The company raised their voice together to the one who made heaven, earth and sea.
John 11:41 — *Yahusha (Jesus) lifted up his eyes, and said, Father, I thank thee that thou hast heard me.* Yahusha (Jesus) prayed aloud before the crowd, speaking to the Father who had heard him.
Psalm 139:1 — *O Yahuah (LORD), thou hast searched me, and known me.* Yahuah (the LORD) has searched and known the one who prays, so there is nothing to show him.
Deuteronomy 32:6 — *is not he thy father that hath bought thee? hath he not made thee, and established thee?* Yahuah (the LORD) is called the father who bought, made and established his people.

Exodus 16:4 — *the people shall go out and gather a certain rate every day, that I may prove them, whether they will walk in my law, or no.* The manna came a day at a time to prove whether the people would walk in his law.

Proverbs 30:8 — *Remove far from me vanity and lies: give me neither poverty nor riches; feed me with food convenient for me:* The wise man asks for neither poverty nor riches, only food convenient for him.
Matthew 4:4 — *Man shall not live by bread alone, but by every word that proceedeth out of the mouth of Elohim (God).* A man lives by every word from the mouth of Elohim (God), not by bread alone.

Matthew 4:1 — *Then was Yahusha (Jesus) led up of the Spirit into the wilderness to be tempted of the devil.* Yahusha (Jesus) had himself just been led into the wilderness to be tempted, and knows the road he teaches them to pray about.

1 Corinthians 10:13 — *Elohim (God) is faithful, who will not suffer you to be tempted above that ye are able; but will with the temptation also make a way to escape, that ye may be able to bear it.* Elohim (God) is faithful and does not let the temptation go beyond what a man can bear, but makes a way out.

James 1:13 — *for Elohim (God) cannot be tempted with evil, neither tempteth he any man.* Elohim (God) cannot be tempted with evil and tempts no man, so the petition cannot mean he leads anyone into evil.

Leviticus 23:27 — *there shall be a day of atonement: it shall be an holy convocation unto you; and ye shall afflict your souls, and offer an offering made by fire unto Yahuah (LORD).* The Torah commands a day of atonement on which the people afflict their souls.
Joel 1:14 — *Sanctify ye a fast, call a solemn assembly, gather the elders and all the inhabitants of the land.* Joel calls the whole land to sanctify a fast and cry to Yahuah (the LORD) together.
Matthew 4:2 — *And when he had fasted forty days and forty nights, he was afterward an hungred.* Yahusha (Jesus) himself fasted forty days and nights, and was hungry only afterward.
Proverbs 11:4 — *Riches profit not in the day of wrath: but righteousness delivereth from death.* Riches are of no use on the day of wrath, but righteousness delivers from death.
Proverbs 23:4 — *Labour not to be rich: cease from thine own wisdom.* Riches grow wings and fly away, so the wise man says not to labour to be rich.
Psalm 49:16 — *Be not thou afraid when one is made rich, when the glory of his house is increased;* A rich man's glory does not go down with him at death, so no one need fear his wealth.

Luke 12:33 — *provide yourselves bags which wax not old, a treasure in the heavens that faileth not, where no thief approacheth, neither moth corrupteth.* Selling and giving alms is how the treasure in the heavens is provided, where no thief or moth reaches it.
Exodus 20:3 — *Thou shalt have no other gods before me.* No other gods before Yahuah (the LORD) is the commandment behind the refusal to serve two masters.

Deuteronomy 6:4 — *Hear, O Yashar'el (Israel): Yahuah Eloheinu (The LORD our God) is one Yahuah (LORD):* Yahuah (the LORD) is one, and the whole heart belongs to him, which leaves no share for another master.

1 Kings 18:21 — *How long halt ye between two opinions? if Yahuah (LORD) be Elohim (God), follow him: but if Baal, then follow him.* Elijah demands that the people choose between Yahuah (the LORD) and Baal, and they cannot answer.
Proverbs 22:9 — *He that hath a bountiful eye shall be blessed; for he giveth of his bread to the poor.* A bountiful eye is one that gives bread to the poor, and it is blessed.
Proverbs 23:6 — *Eat thou not the bread of him that hath an evil eye, neither desire thou his dainty meats:* The man with an evil eye is a grudging host, whose food the wise are told not to desire.

Deuteronomy 15:9 — *and thine eye be evil against thy poor brother, and thou givest him nought; and he cry unto Yahuah (LORD) against thee, and it be sin unto thee.* An eye evil against a poor brother who is given nothing is sin in the Torah.

Proverbs 28:22 — *He that hasteth to be rich hath an evil eye, and considereth not that poverty shall come upon him.* The man in haste to be rich has an evil eye and does not see that poverty is coming.
Psalm 147:9 — *He giveth to the beast his food, and to the young ravens which cry.* Yahuah (the LORD) gives food to the beast and to the young ravens that cry.

Job 38:4 — *Where wast thou when I laid the foundations of the earth? declare, if thou hast understanding.* Yahuah (the LORD) asks Job where he was when the foundations of the earth were laid, and shows whose hands hold creation.
Psalm 104:10 — *He sendeth the springs into the valleys, which run among the hills.* The springs sent into the valleys show the Father's provision reaching every creature, which the birds stand for.

1 Kings 3:11 — *Because thou hast asked this thing, and hast not asked for thyself long life; neither hast asked riches for thyself.* Solomon asked for understanding and not for riches, and the riches were given to him as well.
Psalm 37:4 — *Delight thyself also in Yahuah (LORD); and he shall give thee the desires of thine heart.* Delight in Yahuah (the LORD) comes first, and he gives the desires of the heart after it.

Matthew 5:6 — *Blessed are they which do hunger and thirst after righteousness: for they shall be filled.* Those who hunger and thirst after righteousness are blessed and will be filled, which is the seeking of the kingdom first.

John 7:24 — *Judge not according to the appearance, but judge righteous judgment.* Yahusha (Jesus) names the judging he forbids, which goes by appearance, and commands the righteous judgment that the Torah asks for.
Matthew 10:14 — *whosoever shall not receive you, nor hear your words.* Where the word is not received or heard, Yahusha (Jesus) tells his disciples to leave that place and shake off the dust.

Luke 11:13 — *how much more shall your heavenly Father give the Ruach HaKodesh (Holy Spirit) to them that ask him.* Luke names the good thing the Father gives to those who ask: the Ruach HaKodesh (Holy Spirit).

Jeremiah 31:33 — *I will put my law in their inward parts, and write it in their hearts.* Yahuah (the LORD) promises to put his law inside his people and write it on their hearts, which is the good gift in full.

Ezekiel 36:26 — *A new heart also will I give you, and a new spirit will I put within you.* Yahuah (the LORD) promises a new heart and a new spirit, taking away the stony heart and giving a heart of flesh.

Isaiah 10:20 — *the remnant of Yashar'el (Israel), and such as are escaped of the house of Jacob.* Isaiah says only a remnant of Yashar'el (Israel) escapes and leans on Yahuah (the LORD) in truth, which is the narrow way's own end.

Zechariah 13:8 — *two parts therein shall be cut off and die; but the third shall be left therein.* Zechariah gives the few a number, two parts cut off and one left, and says the one left is brought through the fire.

Zephaniah 3:12 — *I will also leave in the midst of thee an afflicted and poor people, and they shall trust in the name of Yahuah (LORD).* Zephaniah says Yahuah (the LORD) will leave an afflicted and poor people, and what marks them is that they trust in his name.

Luke 13:23 — *Then said one unto him, Adonai (Lord), are there few that be saved? And he said unto them,* Luke records the question whether few are saved, and Yahusha (Jesus) answers by naming the same strait gate.

Acts 20:29 — *For I know this, that after my departing shall grievous wolves enter in among you, not sparing the flock.* Paul warns the Ephesian elders that grievous wolves will enter in among the flock and not spare it.
Exodus 24:7 — *All that Yahuah (LORD) hath said will we do, and be obedient.* The people answer that all Yahuah (the LORD) has said they will do and be obedient, the pattern of hearing and doing.

Deuteronomy 32:4 — *He is the Rock, his work is perfect: for all his ways are judgment: a Elohim (God) of truth and without iniquity, just and right is he.* Moses names Yahuah (the LORD) as the Rock whose work is perfect and whose ways are all judgment.
Psalm 18:2 — *Yahuah (LORD) is my rock, and my fortress, and my deliverer.* David calls Yahuah (the LORD) his rock, fortress and deliverer, the ground that holds when the floods come.
James 1:22 — *But be ye doers of the word, and not hearers only, deceiving your own selves.* James says to be doers of the word and not hearers only, and so restates the wise and foolish builders.
